definition_zh: 不确定；不确定性；疑虑；未知之事；测量的不确定度；风险与不可预测性
definition_en: the state of not being sure or not being known, and the range within which a measurement or forecast may vary
core_image: 一根指针停在两个刻度之间，微微抖动，既不落在这边也不落在那边
scene: 预报员看着云图，风向在半天之内改了三次，他只能说周末可能下雨也可能不下。 The uncertainty in the forecast kept the organizers from booking the outdoor stage.
sceneCN: 这里指预报结果无法确定的状态（第 3 个义项：不可预测、结果未定）；句意为预报中的不确定性让主办方无法预订露天舞台。场景图取象：指针停在两个刻度之间微微抖动。

pos.zh: 不确定；疑虑（不可数，指心理状态）
不确定之事；变数（可数，常用复数）
不确定度（测量学，指结果可能波动的范围）
（经济与管理）不可预测性、风险

derivatives.zh: 不确定的；不肯定的（加表示否定的前缀，指不处于已被判定的状态）
确定性；必然之事（去掉否定前缀后由「已被判定」的形容词加名词词尾构成）
确定的；某个的（由拉丁语「已判定」义而来，经由表示「筛定」的动词）
没有把握地；迟疑地（在形容词后加副词词尾）
确信；笃定（与 certain 同源的名词，多指主观上的确定感）

senses.title: Not knowing for sure
senses.definition: the state of not knowing whether something is true or what will happen
senses.definitionCN: 不知道某事是否为真、或将会如何的状态
senses.example: Her uncertainty about the answer was obvious.
senses.exampleCN: 她对答案没有把握，这一点很明显。
senses.why: The word negates a Latin adjective meaning settled, so it names the condition of not being settled.
senses.whyCN: 这个词否定了一个意为「已判定」的拉丁形容词，因此指未被定下来的状态。

senses.title: Something not yet decided
senses.definition: a matter whose outcome is not yet fixed, often counted in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 结果尚未确定的事情，常用复数计数
senses.example: The plan has too many uncertainties to price.
senses.exampleCN: 这个计划变数太多，无法定价。
senses.why: Uncertainty can be a thing as well as a mood, and business counts the things rather than the mood.
senses.whyCN: 不确定性既能是心情，也能是事情，商界数的是事情而非心情。

senses.title: What cannot be predicted
senses.definition: the part of a situation that cannot be forecast, as in weather or markets
senses.definitionCN: 局面中无法预报的部分，如天气或市场中的情形
senses.example: The uncertainty in the forecast kept the organizers from booking the outdoor stage.
senses.exampleCN: 预报中的不确定性让主办方无法预订露天舞台。
senses.why: Forecasting separates what is known from what remains open, and the open part takes this name.
senses.whyCN: 预报把已知与仍未定的部分分开，仍未定的那部分就用这个名字。

senses.title: The spread of a measurement
senses.definition: the range within which the true value of a measurement is expected to lie
senses.definitionCN: 测量的真值预期落在其中的范围
senses.example: The result was reported with an uncertainty of two per cent.
senses.exampleCN: 结果报告时附有百分之二的不确定度。
senses.why: Metrology refuses to give a bare number; every figure comes with the width of its doubt.
senses.whyCN: 计量学不肯给出光秃秃的数字，每个数都带着它那份怀疑的宽度。

senses.title: The quantum limit
senses.definition: the limit on how precisely certain paired properties of a particle can be known at once
senses.definitionCN: 粒子的某些成对属性无法同时被测得足够精确的限度
senses.example: The uncertainty principle is about knowledge, not about laboratory clumsiness.
senses.exampleCN: 不确定性原理讲的是知识限度，而不是实验室笨手笨脚。
senses.why: Physics found a doubt built into nature itself, and borrowed the everyday word for it.
senses.whyCN: 物理学发现怀疑被造进了自然本身，于是借用了日常的词来称它。

senses.title: Economic unpredictability
senses.definition: unpredictability in prices, demand or policy that makes planning difficult
senses.definitionCN: 价格、需求或政策上的不可预测，使规划变得困难
senses.example: Uncertainty over tariffs froze new investment.
senses.exampleCN: 关税上的不确定让新投资停滞。
senses.why: Firms do not react to bad news so much as to not knowing, which is why the word dominates economics.
senses.whyCN: 企业反应的与其说是坏消息，不如说是「不知道」，所以这个词在经济领域举足轻重。

senses.title: Hesitation in a person
senses.definition: a feeling of doubt that makes a person hesitate or speak cautiously
senses.definitionCN: 使人迟疑或说话谨慎的怀疑感
senses.example: He answered with a slight uncertainty in his voice.
senses.exampleCN: 他回答时声音里带着一点迟疑。
senses.why: The inner sense is the oldest: an unsettled judgement shows in the voice before it shows in the data.
senses.whyCN: 内心的义项最古老：未定的判断先露在声音里，然后才露在数据里。

senses.title: Risk that cannot be counted
senses.definition: a situation whose probabilities are unknown, distinguished from risk in which odds can be assigned
senses.definitionCN: 概率未知的处境，与可以给出赔率的「风险」相区别
senses.example: Decision theory separates uncertainty from measurable risk.
senses.exampleCN: 决策理论把不确定性与可计量的风险分开。
senses.why: If the odds are known it is risk; if they are not, it is uncertainty, and the distinction matters to insurers.
senses.whyCN: 赔率已知的是风险，未知的是不确定性，这一区分对保险业至关重要。

senses.title: The open future
senses.definition: the general condition of the future being undecided, a theme in philosophy and literature
senses.definitionCN: 未来尚未定局的一般状况，是哲学与文学的常见主题
senses.example: The novel turns uncertainty into a kind of freedom.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说把不确定变成了一种自由。
senses.why: If the future were closed, choice would be pointless; the word can name that openness rather than a lack.
senses.whyCN: 若未来已经闭合，选择便无意义；这个词也能指那种敞开，而不只是一种缺失。

intro.en: Uncertainty is the negative of certainty, from Latin certus 'settled', itself from cernere 'to sift, to decide'. The root history is generally accepted; only the exact date of the English noun is uncertain.
intro.cn: uncertainty 是 certainty 的否定形式，certainty 出自拉丁语 certus「已定的」，而 certus 又出自 cernere「筛、判定」。词根历史一般认为可靠，只有这个英语名词的确切年代不确定。

items.en: Cernere meant to sift or to separate, and from sifting came the sense of deciding a matter.
items.cn: cernere 意为筛、分开，从筛选中引出判定一件事的意思。

items.en: Certus meant settled or decided, said of a thing no longer in doubt.
items.cn: certus 意为已定、已决，用于不再有疑问之事。

items.en: Latin added the negative prefix to make incertus, not settled, the direct ancestor of uncertain.
items.cn: 拉丁语加上否定前缀构成 incertus「未定的」，正是 uncertain 的直接祖先。

items.en: Old French uncertain and the noun forme carried the word into English in the Middle Ages.
items.cn: 古法语的形式把这个词与名词形态在中世纪带入英语。

items.en: In the nineteenth and twentieth centuries the word was given a numeric sense, the band around a measured value.
items.cn: 十九与二十世纪，这个词获得数量含义，指测量值周围的那一条带。

items.en: Quantum theory and modern finance both made uncertainty a technical quantity, one in nature and one in markets.
items.cn: 量子理论与现代金融都把不确定性做成了技术量，一个在自然里，一个在市场里。

note.en: The first group shares the settled root or looks similar; the second group names neighbouring states that are often folded into uncertainty.
note.cn: 第一组或共享「已定」词根，或字形相近；第二组是常被并入「不确定性」的邻近状态。

entries.definition: The adjective: not sure, not settled.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词：不确定的、未定的。

entries.definition: The positive noun: the state of being settled.
entries.definitionCN: 肯定形式的名词：已被确定的状态。

entries.definition: A feeling of complete sureness, usually subjective.
entries.definitionCN: 完全的确定感，通常指主观上的。

entries.definition: To find out for certain; it shares cernere but not the negative prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 查明、确定；共享「筛定」词根，不含否定前缀。

entries.definition: Strange in a way that unsettles; it looks like the same negative but comes from ken, knowledge.
entries.definitionCN: 怪得令人不安；看似同一否定前缀，其实出自表示「知晓」的词。

entries.definition: A feeling of not being convinced, the personal side of uncertainty.
entries.definitionCN: 未被说服的感觉，是不确定性在个人身上的那一面。

entries.definition: Having more than one possible meaning, a property of statements rather than of the future.
entries.definitionCN: 存在不止一种可能含义，是陈述的属性而非未来的属性。

entries.definition: Exposure to a loss whose probability can be estimated.
entries.definitionCN: 暴露于损失之中，而其概率可以估算。

entries.definition: The tendency of a quantity to change, which produces uncertainty in measurement.
entries.definitionCN: 数量容易变动的倾向，正是它造成测量上的不确定。

entries.definition: The rate at which prices swing, a market measure of uncertainty.
entries.definitionCN: 价格摆动的幅度，是市场对不确定性的度量。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real sifting root, the real family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「筛定」词根、真实同族词与真实固定搭配。

normal.en: Certain comes from a Latin verb meaning to sift, so certainty is what survives the sieve and uncertainty is what does not.
normal.cn: certain 出自意为「筛」的拉丁动词，确定性是筛后留下之物，不确定性是没留下的。

normal.en: The family pairs neatly: certain and certainty against uncertain and uncertainty.
normal.cn: 同族词成对出现：确定的、确定性，对不确定的、不确定性。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: measurement uncertainty, economic uncertainty, the uncertainty principle.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出用法：测量不确定度、经济不确定性、不确定性原理。

normal.en: In decision theory risk has countable odds, uncertainty does not.
normal.cn: 在决策理论里，风险有可数的赔率，不确定性没有。

normal.en: The plural uncertainties names concrete open questions, not a mood.
normal.cn: 复数形式指一件件还没定的事，而不是一种心情。

abstract.en: Uncertainty is the space in which a decision is still a decision.
abstract.cn: 不确定性是那块空间，决定在其中还算得上决定。

abstract.en: A number without an uncertainty is a claim pretending to be a fact.
abstract.cn: 没有不确定度的数字，是假装成事实的主张。

abstract.en: Uncertainty is not the enemy of knowledge; it is the shape knowledge takes at its edges.
abstract.cn: 不确定性不是知识的敌人，而是知识在边缘处呈现的形状。

examples.en: Uncertainty about the funding delayed the whole project.
examples.cn: 资金上的不确定拖住了整个项目。

examples.en: Every measurement carries an uncertainty that must be stated.
examples.cn: 每次测量都带有必须说明的不确定度。

examples.en: She learned to work despite the uncertainty of the outcome.
examples.cn: 她学会了在结果未定之时照样做事。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「安色滕提」——心里那根针迟迟不落定：不确定

root: certainty 的否定形式；certain 出自拉丁语 certus「已定」← cernere「筛、判定」，加否定前缀构成 incertus「未定」，经古法语进入英语。二十世纪起在测量学、量子物理与金融中获得技术含义。名词进入英语的确切年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses move from a private doubt to a public quantity: not knowing, an open question, an unpredictable part, the spread of a measurement, the quantum limit, economic unpredictability, personal hesitation, uncountable risk, and the openness of the future.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从私人的疑虑走到公共的量：拿不准、尚未定的事、无法预测的部分、测量的不确定度、量子限度、经济上的不可预测、个人的迟疑、无法计数的风险，以及未来的敞开。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a needle resting between two marks and trembling, belonging to neither.
core.cn: 核心意象：指针停在两个刻度之间微微抖动，哪一边都不属于。

branches.en: THE UNSETTLED MIND: a judgement not yet made, showing as hesitation in a voice.
branches.cn: 未定的心：尚未作出的判断，先从声音里的迟疑露出来。

branches.en: THE OPEN QUESTION: a matter whose outcome is still unfixed and can be counted.
branches.cn: 未决的问题：结果尚未确定、还可以数出来的一件事。

branches.en: THE UNFORECASTABLE: weather that may or may not hold, tariffs that may or may not change.
branches.cn: 无法预报之物：可能下也可能不下的雨，可能改也可能不改的关税。

branches.en: THE WIDTH OF A NUMBER: the band around a measured value, and the quantum limit on knowing two things at once.
branches.cn: 数字的宽度：测量值周围那一条带，以及同时知道两件事的量子限度。

branches.en: THE OPEN FUTURE: risk without countable odds, and the freedom of a future not yet closed.
branches.cn: 敞开的未来：没有可数赔率的风险，以及尚未闭合的未来的自由。

intro.en: Uncertainty negates a Latin adjective of settledness and turns it into an abstract noun.
intro.cn: uncertainty 否定一个表示「已定」的拉丁形容词，并把它变成抽象名词。

latinIntro.en: The base is certus from cernere, with the negative prefix and the noun ending added in turn.
latinIntro.cn: 基础是出自 cernere 的 certus，先后加上否定前缀与名词词尾。

items.meaning: the state of not being settled
items.example: The noun covers both a mood and a measured range.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词既指心情，也指测量出的范围。

items.example: It turns certain into uncertain.
items.exampleCN: 它把确定的变成不确定的。

items.example: It comes from the verb for sifting.
items.exampleCN: 它出自表示筛的动词。

items.meaning: to sift, to separate, to decide
items.example: The image is a sieve that leaves only what is sure.
items.exampleCN: 意象是一只筛子，只留下确定的东西。

items.example: It builds certainty and uncertainty.
items.exampleCN: 它构成确定性与不确定性。

items.example: The adjective also means a particular one.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词也有「某一个」的意思。

items.example: The pair makes a clean positive and negative.
items.exampleCN: 这一对构成干净的正与负。

items.example: It shares the root without the negative.
items.exampleCN: 它共享词根，却没有否定。

items.example: The noun names the feeling rather than the fact.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指感觉而非事实。

latinEntries.example: Latin incertus means not settled, doubtful.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 incertus 意为未定的、可疑的。

latinEntries.structure: Latin adjective certus (settled, sure), from cernere
latinEntries.example: Latin certus means settled or sure.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 certus 意为已定的、可靠的。

latinEntries.structure: Latin verb cernere (cern-, cretum; to sift, decide)
latinEntries.example: Latin cernere means to sift, and so to decide.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 cernere 意为筛，因而也指判定。

definition_zh: 程序的；程序性的；手续上的；（法律）程序法的；按步骤操作的
definition_en: relating to the steps or rules by which something is done, rather than to its substance or result
core_image: 一张按序号排好的流程图贴在墙上，每一步都用箭头连到下一步
scene: 法官没有讨论谁更有理，而是先问警方取证时是否按规定的步骤通知了当事人。 The court raised a procedural question about whether the search had followed the required steps.
sceneCN: 这里指与程序、步骤有关的（第 2 个义项：法律程序上的）；句意为法院提出了一个程序问题，即这次搜查是否按规定的步骤进行。场景图取象：墙上贴着按序号排好的流程图。

pos.zh: 程序的；程序性的
（法律）程序法的；与程序有关的
（计算机）过程式的；按步骤展开的

derivatives.zh: 程序；步骤；手续（由表示「向前走」的拉丁动词加名词词尾构成，指一步步走的路径）
在程序上；按程序地（加副词词尾，指从程序角度看）
继续进行；行进（同源动词，字面即「向前走」，是 procedure 的动作基础）
诉讼程序；会议记录（现在分词转名词，指正在进行的一系列步骤）
过程；处理（同出「向前走」的拉丁词根，但走的是另一条名词化路径）
程序主义（在形容词后加表示「学说、倾向」的后缀，指重视程序的立场）

senses.title: Belonging to the steps
senses.definition: relating to the way in which something is done, rather than to what is done
senses.definitionCN: 关涉做事的方式与步骤，而非所做之事的内容
senses.example: The change was procedural, not a matter of policy.
senses.exampleCN: 这一改动是程序上的，不涉及政策本身。
senses.why: The base noun procedure names a path walked step by step, so the adjective marks the path rather than the destination.
senses.whyCN: 基础名词指一步步走过的路径，因此这个形容词标的是路径而非终点。

senses.title: Of the rules of court
senses.definition: concerning the rules that govern how a legal case is conducted
senses.definitionCN: 关于主导案件如何审理的规则的
senses.example: The appeal was lost on procedural grounds.
senses.exampleCN: 上诉因程序上的理由而失败。
senses.why: Law separates substance from procedure, and the adjective names the second half of that split.
senses.whyCN: 法律把实体与程序分开，这个形容词指这一划分的后一半。

senses.title: Fair in the way it is done
senses.definition: describing fairness in the process itself, such as being heard before a decision
senses.definitionCN: 指过程本身的公正，例如在决定之前有陈述的机会
senses.example: Procedural fairness required the board to hear both sides.
senses.exampleCN: 程序公正要求委员会听取双方意见。
senses.why: A good result reached by a bad path is still suspect, so fairness attaches to the steps.
senses.whyCN: 用坏路径得到的好结果仍然可疑，所以公正落在步骤上。

senses.title: Safeguards against error
senses.definition: of rules designed to catch mistakes, such as a second reading or a signature
senses.definitionCN: 指为发现错误而设的规则，如二次审读或签名确认
senses.example: The agency added procedural checks before approving loans.
senses.exampleCN: 该机构在批准贷款前增加了程序性核查。
senses.why: Bureaucracy is often defended as a set of small procedural brakes on haste.
senses.whyCN: 官僚程序常被辩护为一组对仓促行事的小小刹车。

senses.title: Step-by-step in computing
senses.definition: of a programming style built from named sequences of instructions, as opposed to object-oriented style
senses.definitionCN: 指由命名的指令序列构成的编程风格，与面向对象风格相对
senses.example: The course starts with procedural programming in a simple language.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课从简单语言的过程式编程讲起。
senses.why: Software borrowed the word for code that reads like a list of steps to be walked through.
senses.whyCN: 软件领域借这个词指读起来像一串待走步骤的代码。

senses.title: Of a parliamentary motion
senses.definition: concerning the conduct of a meeting, such as a motion on speaking time
senses.definitionCN: 关于会议如何进行的，如关于发言时间的动议
senses.example: The chair ruled the objection procedural and set it aside.
senses.exampleCN: 主席裁定这一异议属程序问题，暂不处理。
senses.why: Assemblies run on rules of order, and a procedural motion keeps the argument about the rules.
senses.whyCN: 议会依议事规则运转，程序性动议把争论留在规则层面。

senses.title: Characteristic of a procedure
senses.definition: having the character of a routine, done in a fixed order without much judgement
senses.definitionCN: 带有例行程序的特征，按固定次序执行而少有判断
senses.example: The interview felt procedural, with the same questions for everyone.
senses.exampleCN: 这场面谈显得很程序化，每个人都问同样的问题。
senses.why: When a human act becomes a fixed sequence, the adjective moves from describing rules to describing behaviour.
senses.whyCN: 当人的行为变成固定序列，这个形容词就从描述规则转为描述举止。

senses.title: Of medical procedures
senses.definition: relating to a medical or surgical procedure rather than to diagnosis alone
senses.definitionCN: 关涉医疗或外科操作本身，而非仅指诊断
senses.example: The clinic offers procedural sedation for minor surgery.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所的小手术提供操作中的镇静。
senses.why: Medicine names by procedure what is done with hands, and the adjective separates it from talk and tests.
senses.whyCN: 医学以操作命名动手做的事，这个形容词把它与谈话和检查分开。

intro.en: Procedural is procedure plus -al. Procedure comes from Latin procedere 'to go forward', from pro- 'forward' and cedere 'to go'. The line is clear; the exact date of the adjective in English is uncertain.
intro.cn: procedural 是 procedure 加 -al。procedure 出自拉丁语 procedere「向前走」，由 pro-「向前」与 cedere「走」构成。线索清楚，这个形容词进入英语的确切年代不确定。

items.en: Cedere meant to go, to yield or to give way, and it stands behind proceed, process and succeed.
items.cn: cedere 意为走、让步或退让，proceed、process 与 succeed 都由它而来。

items.en: Procedere combined the forward prefix with that verb to mean to go forward, to advance, to come out.
items.cn: procedere 把表示向前的前缀与这个动词结合，意为前行、推进、走出。

items.en: Old French procedure named the manner of conducting a case, a word of courts before it was a word of offices.
items.cn: 古法语的 procedure 指审理案件的方式，先是法庭用语，后成公务用语。

items.en: English borrowed the noun in the sixteenth century, first in law and then in general administration.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入这个名词，先用于法律，随后用于一般行政。

items.en: The adjective followed, and modern law fixed the contrast between procedural and substantive rules.
items.cn: 形容词随后出现，现代法律确立了程序规则与实体规则的对立。

items.en: In the later twentieth century the adjective was applied to programming built from named steps.
items.cn: 二十世纪后期，这个形容词被用来指由命名步骤构成的编程方式。

note.en: The first group shares the going-forward root or looks close; the second group holds words that describe rules and steps but are not the same contrast.
note.cn: 第一组或共享「向前走」词根，或字形相近；第二组描述规则与步骤，却不是同一个对立面。

entries.definition: The noun: a set of steps for doing something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词：做事的一套步骤。

entries.definition: To go on or move forward, the verb inside the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 继续或向前走，是名词里的动词。

entries.definition: A course of action, often in the plural for legal or formal business.
entries.definitionCN: 一系列行动，复数多指法律或正式事务。

entries.definition: A series of changes; it shares cedere through a different Latin noun.
entries.definitionCN: 一系列变化；经另一个拉丁名词共享同一词根。

entries.definition: Wastefully generous; it looks like the same prefix but comes from a verb meaning to squander.
entries.definitionCN: 挥霍的；前缀看似相同，词根却意为耗费。

entries.definition: Following established rules, which often overlaps with procedural but concerns form.
entries.definitionCN: 遵循既定规则，常与程序重叠，但着眼在形式。

entries.definition: Concerning the running of an organisation rather than its policy.
entries.definitionCN: 关涉机构运转而非政策。

entries.definition: A fixed sequence of actions with symbolic weight, closer to ceremony than to rule.
entries.definitionCN: 带象征分量的固定动作序列，更近仪式而非规则。

entries.definition: Done by an ordered plan, emphasising method rather than rules.
entries.definitionCN: 按有序计划进行，强调方法而非规则。

entries.definition: Concerning the actual rights and duties at issue, the opposite half of the legal split.
entries.definitionCN: 关涉争议中的实际权利与义务，是法律划分的另一半。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real going-forward root, the real family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「向前走」词根、真实同族词与真实固定搭配。

normal.en: Cedere means to go, and procedere means to go forward, so a procedure is a path walked step by step.
normal.cn: 词根意为走，加向前的前缀即前行，程序就是一步步走过的路径。

normal.en: The family runs proceed, procedure, proceeding, procedural and process.
normal.cn: 同族词有 proceed、procedure、proceeding、procedural 与 process。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: procedural rules, procedural fairness, procedural law, procedural error.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出用法：程序规则、程序公正、程序法、程序性错误。

normal.en: Law divides the world into procedural and substantive, and the adjective owns one half.
normal.cn: 法律把世界分成程序与实体，这个形容词占一半。

normal.en: Procedure is the noun, procedural the adjective, procedurally the adverb.
normal.cn: 名词是 procedure，形容词是 procedural，副词是 procedurally。

abstract.en: Procedure is fairness made repeatable, so that the same case gets the same path.
abstract.cn: 程序是把公正做成可重复的，好让同样的案子走同样的路。

abstract.en: When procedure becomes an end in itself, the path eats the destination.
abstract.cn: 当程序本身成了目的，路径就把终点吃掉了。

abstract.en: A procedure is a promise that the next person will get the same treatment.
abstract.cn: 程序是一个承诺：下一个人也会受到同样的对待。

examples.en: The delay was procedural and did not affect the merits.
examples.cn: 这次延误属程序问题，不影响案件实体。

examples.en: Procedural fairness matters even when the answer is obvious.
examples.cn: 即使答案显而易见，程序公正仍然要紧。

examples.en: The older software was written in a procedural style.
examples.cn: 那套旧软件是过程式风格写成的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「普若西哲柔」——照着流程图上编号一步步走：程序的

root: procedure ＋ 形容词词尾 -al；procedure 出自拉丁语 procedere「向前走」← pro-「向前」＋ cedere「走」，同源有 proceed、process、proceeding。十六世纪进入英语，先在法律后及行政；二十世纪后期用于编程风格。形容词确切年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow the path: the steps themselves, court rules, fairness of process, safeguards, step-by-step code, meeting order, routine behaviour, and medical procedures.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着这条路径展开：步骤本身、法庭规则、过程公正、防错保障、按步执行的代码、议事秩序、例行举止，以及医疗操作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a numbered flow chart on a wall, each box linked to the next by an arrow.
core.cn: 核心意象：墙上贴着编号的流程图，每个方框都用箭头连到下一个。

branches.en: THE MANNER OF DOING: the steps rather than the substance, and behaviour that has become a fixed sequence.
branches.cn: 做事的方式：步骤而非实体，以及变成固定序列的举止。

branches.en: THE RULES OF THE ROOM: court rules and the motions that keep a meeting arguing about its own order.
branches.cn: 场内规则：法庭规则，以及让会议只争论自身秩序的动议。

branches.en: THE GUARDED PATH: hearing both sides, and the checks that catch a mistake before it travels.
branches.cn: 有护栏的路径：听取双方，以及错误传开之前抓住它的核查。

branches.en: THE CODE THAT READS LIKE STEPS: named sequences of instructions walked through in order.
branches.cn: 读起来像步骤的代码：按次序走过的命名指令序列。

branches.en: THE PROCEDURE IN MEDICINE: what is done with hands, as distinct from diagnosis and talk.
branches.cn: 医学里的操作：动手所做之事，与诊断和谈话相区别。

intro.en: Procedural rests on the Latin verb for going forward and adds an English adjective ending.
intro.cn: procedural 依托表示「向前走」的拉丁动词，再加上英语形容词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin procedere and the noun procedura are the sources behind the English pair procedure and procedural.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 procedere 与名词 procedura 是英语 procedure 与 procedural 这对词的来源。

items.example: The adjective marks manner rather than substance.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词标的是方式而非实体。

items.example: The noun names the path as a whole.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指整条路径。

items.example: It gives the direction of the walking.
items.exampleCN: 它给出行走的方向。

items.example: It also stands behind process and succeed.
items.exampleCN: process 与 succeed 也由它而来。

items.example: It builds procedural, formal and substantial.
items.exampleCN: 它构成程序的、形式的与实质的等词。

items.meaning: result or manner of an act
items.example: It builds procedure and departure.
items.exampleCN: 它构成程序与离开等词。

items.example: It builds procedurally, as in procedurally flawed.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 procedurally，如程序上有瑕疵。

items.example: The plural names the whole run of steps.
items.exampleCN: 复数形式指整套步骤的进行。

latinEntries.meaning: to go forward; to come out
latinEntries.example: Latin procedere means to go forward.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 procedere 意为向前走。

latinEntries.example: Latin pro- appears in producere, to lead forward.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 pro- 见于 producere（向前引出）。

latinEntries.structure: Latin verb cedere (ced-, cessum; to go, yield)
latinEntries.example: Latin cedere means to go or yield, and gives cede and process.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 cedere 意为走、让步，并给出 cede 与 process。

definition_zh: 公平的；公正的；按规则行事的；浅色的；晴朗的；尚可的；相当多的；（旧）美丽的；（名词）集市、交易会
definition_en: treating people equally and following the rules, and, by older widening, light in colour, clear in weather, moderate in degree, handsome in appearance, or a gathering where goods are traded
core_image: 一架天平两端放着同样的砝码，指针停在正中，旁边摊开的规则手册对双方写着一模一样的条款
scene: 裁判在中线把球权判给先触球的一方，双方队员都照同一份规则手册行事。 The referee awarded the ball to the side that touched it first, and both teams played a fair game.
sceneCN: 这里指「按共同规则行事、不偏袒任何一方」，对应第 2 个义项：在竞赛或交易中依照事先约定的规则而不取巧；句意为裁判把球权判给先触球的一方，两队都按规则比赛。画面要点：中线、裁判手势、两队球衣、摊开的规则手册。

pos.zh: 公平的；公正的；按规则的；浅色的；晴朗的；尚可的；相当多的；（旧）美丽的
集市；交易会；博览会（另出一源，与形容词不同源）
公平地；按规则地（常用于表示按规则做事的固定说法）

collocations.zh: 公平的交易；公正的待遇

derivatives.zh: 公平；公正（基础词加古英语表性质的名词后缀，由形容词转为抽象状态）
公平地；相当地（基础词加副词后缀，语义由「公正」扩展到「程度适中」）
不公平的（否定前缀加基础词，指偏离规则或偏袒一方）
公正的；不偏不倚的（基础词与「心智」一词加过去分词后缀构成的复合形容词，指判断不受私利影响）
集市或博览会的场地（基础词与「地面」一词构成的复合名词，语义由交易会转向其举办场所）

senses.title: Even-handed in judgment
senses.titleCN: 判断时不偏袒任何一方
senses.definition: treating people equally and not letting personal preference decide an outcome
senses.definitionCN: 平等待人，不让个人好恶决定结果
senses.example: A fair judge hears both sides before ruling.
senses.exampleCN: 公正的法官在裁决前会听取双方陈述。
senses.why: The oldest sense of the word was 'beautiful, clean'; an unblemished decision was felt as something clean and pleasing, so the idea of even-handedness grew out of that older picture rather than from a word for law.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最古老的意思是「美好的、洁净的」；不受污染的裁决被感受为洁净而令人愉悦之物，因此「公正」义是从那幅旧图景长出来的，而不是来自某个表示法律的词。

senses.title: According to the agreed rules
senses.titleCN: 依照事先约定的规则行事
senses.definition: played or done in the way the rules require, without trickery or advantage taken
senses.definitionCN: 按照规则要求去做，不取巧、不占便宜
senses.example: The referee awarded the ball to the side that touched it first, and both teams played a fair game.
senses.exampleCN: 裁判把球权判给先触球的一方，两队都按规则比赛。
senses.why: Once equal treatment is expected between opponents, the word names the conduct that keeps the contest equal, which is why sport fixed the phrase fair play.
senses.whyCN: 当对手之间被期待受到同等对待，这个词就用来指维持竞赛对等的行为，体育因此固定下「公平竞赛」这一说法。

senses.title: Light in colour
senses.definition: pale or light in colour, especially of hair, skin or cloth
senses.definitionCN: 颜色浅淡，尤指头发、皮肤或织物
senses.example: The child had fair hair and a sunburned nose.
senses.exampleCN: 那孩子头发浅淡，鼻子晒得发红。
senses.why: A clean, bright appearance was the core of the old sense, and lightness of colour is exactly what that brightness looks like on a surface.
senses.whyCN: 洁净明亮的外观是旧义的核心，而颜色的浅淡正是这种明亮落在表面上的样子。

senses.title: Clear and cloudless weather
senses.definition: bright and dry, with no rain and little cloud
senses.definitionCN: 明亮干燥、无雨少云
senses.example: The forecast promised fair weather for the crossing.
senses.exampleCN: 预报说渡海期间天气晴好。
senses.why: A sky without cloud shares the same visual core of brightness and cleanliness, so the weather sense needs no separate origin.
senses.whyCN: 无云的天空共享同一个明亮洁净的视觉核心，因此天气义无需另找来源。

senses.title: Moderately good, no more
senses.definition: acceptable but not excellent; average in quality
senses.definitionCN: 可以接受但不算出色；质量中等
senses.example: The hotel was fair, neither luxurious nor shabby.
senses.exampleCN: 那家旅馆还算可以，既不豪华也不破旧。
senses.why: In grading, 'pleasing enough' slid downward from praise to mere adequacy, and the old phrase fair to middling fixed the middling reading.
senses.whyCN: 在评级中，「足够令人满意」从称赞滑向仅仅及格，旧说法「尚可、中不溜」把这种中等义固定了下来。

senses.title: Considerable in size or amount
senses.definition: large enough to be worth noticing, though not stated exactly
senses.definitionCN: 大到值得注意，但没有确切说出数量
senses.example: A fair number of students stayed after class to ask questions.
senses.exampleCN: 相当多的学生下课后留下来提问。
senses.why: The 'handsome, ample' reading came from the sense of something fine and substantial, not from justice, which is why a fair amount can be large without being equal.
senses.whyCN: 「可观、充足」这一读法来自「美好而结实」的意思，与公正无关；所以「相当多的量」可以很大，却与平等无关。

senses.title: Beautiful, in older use
senses.definition: lovely to look at, used of women in older literature and ballads
senses.definitionCN: 容貌秀美，旧文学与民谣中用于形容女子
senses.example: The fair maiden in the old ballad waited by the well.
senses.exampleCN: 古老民谣里那位美丽的少女在井边等候。
senses.why: This is the earliest recorded sense and the source of all the others; it survives in fixed literary phrases rather than in everyday speech.
senses.whyCN: 这是有记录的最早义项，也是其余义项的源头；它只残留在固定的文学说法里，不再用于日常口语。

senses.title: A gathering where goods are traded
senses.titleCN: 集市、交易会（名词，另出一源）
senses.definition: a large outdoor or indoor event where stalls and companies show and sell goods
senses.definitionCN: 在户外或室内举办、由摊位与公司展示并销售商品的大型活动
senses.example: Farmers brought wool and cheese to the annual fair.
senses.exampleCN: 农民把羊毛和奶酪带到一年一度的集市上。
senses.why: The noun is a different word: Latin feria 'festival day' came through Old French and fell together with the adjective in spelling, so the market sense has no link to justice.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词是另一个词：拉丁语中意为「节日」的词经古法语传入，拼写上才与形容词合流，因此集市义与公正义并无牵连。

intro.en: Fair as an adjective comes from Old English fæger 'beautiful, pleasant, clean', a Germanic word with recorded relatives in Gothic. The noun for a market is a separate borrowing from Latin feria 'festival day'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 作形容词的 fair 来自古英语 fæger「美好的、愉悦的、洁净的」，属日耳曼语词，哥特语中有可考的同族形式。作「集市」解的名词另出拉丁 feria「节日」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Fæger meant 'beautiful, pleasant, clean' and was applied to people, weather, land and objects alike. All the later senses grow from this single descriptive word.
items.cn: fæger 意为「美好的、愉悦的、洁净的」，可用于人、天气、土地与器物。后来各义项都从这一个描写性词生长出来。

items.en: The reconstructed Germanic form *fagraz is posited as the common ancestor; Gothic fagrs 'fitting, suitable' is its closest recorded relative. The starred form is a reconstruction, not an attested word.
items.cn: 学界拟构的日耳曼语形式 *fagraz 被推为共同祖先；哥特语 fagrs「合适的、相称的」是它最近的可考同族词。带星号的形式属重构形式，并非有文献实证的词。

items.en: Source uncertain: no accepted Indo-European ancestor is established for the Germanic adjective. A connection with a root meaning 'to make beautiful' has been suggested, but it remains a hypothesis rather than a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这个日耳曼形容词尚无公认的印欧语祖先。有人提出它与一个意为「使美」的词根相关，但那只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: By the Middle English period the word described decisions and dealings that were clean of bias, and this equitable sense became the dominant everyday one.
items.cn: 到中古英语时期，这个词已用来描述不带偏私的裁决与交易，这一公正义随后成为日常使用中的主导义。

items.en: Light hair and cloudless skies were both called fair because both shared the old core of clean brightness; neither sense required a new source.
items.cn: 浅色的头发与无云的天空都被称作 fair，因为两者都共享「洁净明亮」这一旧核心；这两个义项都不需要新的来源。

items.en: The market noun descends from Latin feria 'festival day', through Old French feire. It is homonymous with the adjective only in modern spelling; the two words are unrelated at the root.
items.cn: 「集市」这一名词出自拉丁 feria「节日」，经古法语 feire 传入。它只在现代拼写上与形容词同形；两个词在词根上并无关联。

note.en: The first group holds look-alikes and homophones that are constantly mistaken for this word; the second group holds near alternatives for the idea of even-handedness.
note.cn: 第一组是极易与这个词混淆的形近词与同音词；第二组是「不偏不倚」这一意思的近义替代。

entries.definition: The money paid for a journey, or food provided; it comes from an Old English word for a journey, not from the adjective for beauty or justice.
entries.definitionCN: 旅费或供应的饮食；出自古英语中表示「行程」的词，与表示美好或公正的形容词无关。

entries.definition: A small magical being; the word comes from Old French faerie 'enchantment', so the resemblance to fair is accidental.
entries.definitionCN: 一种小巧的魔法生灵；该词出自古法语中表示「魔法、魅惑」的词，因此与「美好」一词的相似只是巧合。

entries.definition: The adverb of fair, but it splits into 'in a just manner' and 'to a moderate degree', the second being far more common in speech.
entries.definitionCN: 这是该形容词的副词形式，但分成「以公正的方式」与「达到中等程度」两读，后者在口语中常见得多。

entries.definition: A deliberately archaic spelling of the market noun, used by organisers to suggest a traditional festival; it adds no new meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 「集市」这一名词故意仿古的拼法，主办方用它暗示传统节庆；并不增添新义。

entries.definition: Conforming to what is morally right or lawful; it judges the outcome, while fair stresses the equal treatment that produced it.
entries.definitionCN: 符合道德上正确或法律上正当的要求；它评判结果，而本词更强调产生结果时的平等待遇。

entries.definition: Fair in a formal or legal setting, often correcting a strict rule to reach a balanced result; it is the technical counterpart of the plainer word.
entries.definitionCN: 在正式或法律语境中表示公平，常用来修正过严的规则以取得平衡结果；它是较朴素那个词的专业对应词。

entries.definition: Not favouring one party over another; it describes the absence of bias, whereas fair can also praise a positive even-handedness.
entries.definitionCN: 不偏袒任何一方；它描述的是没有偏见，而本词还可称赞一种积极的持平态度。

entries.definition: Light in colour, often suggesting less brightness than normal; it covers one sense of fair but never carries judgment or weather.
entries.definitionCN: 颜色浅，常暗示比正常情况少了些血色或亮度；它只覆盖其中一个义项，从不带判断或天气之意。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the recorded Old English sense, real derived words and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：有文献可考的古英语义项、真实派生词与真实固定搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The oldest sense is 'beautiful, clean', so a fair decision is pictured as an unblemished surface.
normal.cn: 最古老的意思是「美好的、洁净的」，因此公正的裁决被想象成一块没有污点的表面。

normal.en: The family runs fair, fairly, fairness, unfair, fair-minded and fairground.
normal.cn: 同族词包括本词及其副词形式、表性质的名词、否定形式与复合形式。

normal.en: Fixed phrases sort the senses: fair play, fair weather, fair hair, a fair amount, a trade fair.
normal.cn: 固定搭配把各义项分开：公平竞赛、晴朗天气、浅色头发、相当多的量、贸易博览会。

normal.en: Fare, the price of a journey, sounds identical but belongs to a different Old English word.
normal.cn: 表示旅费的另一个同音词读音完全相同，却属于另一个古英语词。

normal.en: The market noun came from Latin feria 'festival day', so a county fair and a fair judgment are unrelated at the root.
normal.cn: 表示集市的名词出自拉丁语中意为「节日」的词，因此乡村集市与公正裁决在词根上毫不相干。

abstract.en: Picture a balance whose two pans carry different weights but whose beam stays level because the rulebook sits on the fulcrum.
abstract.cn: 想象一架天平，两只托盘放着不同的重量，横梁却保持水平，因为规则手册就垫在支点上。

abstract.en: Picture a white sky over a pale field, the same brightness spread across weather, hair and cloth.
abstract.cn: 想象苍白田野上方的白色天空，同一种明亮铺在天气、头发与布料上。

abstract.en: Picture two separate rivers that happen to join at one estuary: one carries an old song, the other a holiday crowd.
abstract.cn: 想象两条本不相干的河流恰在同一河口汇合：一条载着古老的歌，一条载着过节的人群。

examples.en: The committee reached a fair settlement that both sides could accept.
examples.cn: 委员会达成了一个双方都能接受的公平和解。

examples.en: Fair weather held until the boats were halfway across the bay.
examples.cn: 晴好的天气一直持续到船只驶过海湾中段。

examples.en: She keeps a fair number of old maps in the bottom drawer.
examples.cn: 她在最下面的抽屉里存着相当多的旧地图。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「费厄」——费厄泼赖就是按规则公平竞赛，凡事照同一本规则来 → 公平的、按规则的

root: 古英语 fæger「美好的、洁净的」，与哥特语 fagrs「相称的」同族；更深来源不确定，有「使美」词根的假说，属重构形式。名词「集市」义另出拉丁 feria「节日」，经古法语 feire 借入，与形容词不同源。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses fan out from one picture: a surface that is clean and bright. That brightness becomes light colour, then clear weather, then a beautiful person, then a decision with no stain on it. From the unstained decision come rule-bound play, mere adequacy and a sizeable amount, while the market sense enters English by a separate Latin road.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一幅图景展开：一块洁净明亮的表面。这种明亮先成为浅色，再成为晴朗，再成为美丽的容貌，再成为没有污点的裁决。从无污点的裁决又分出依规则行事、仅够及格与数量可观；而集市义则沿着另一条拉丁语道路进入英语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a clean, bright surface on which no stain or tilt can be seen.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块洁净明亮的表面，看不出任何污点或倾斜。

branches.en: UNSTAINED JUDGMENT: the ethical reading, where no personal preference leaves a mark on the outcome.
branches.cn: 无污点的判断：伦理层面的读法，个人好恶不在结果上留下痕迹。

branches.en: RULES AND ADEQUACY: equal conduct between opponents, and the milder reading of 'good enough' that grading produced.
branches.cn: 规则与及格：对手之间的对等行为，以及评级产生的「还算可以」这一较弱读法。

branches.en: BRIGHTNESS ON A SURFACE: light hair and cloudless sky are the old brightness seen outdoors and on a body.
branches.cn: 表面上的明亮：浅色头发与无云天空，是那种旧有的明亮落在户外与人身上。

branches.en: AMPLE AND LOVELY: a handsome size, and the oldest literary sense of beauty that started the whole family.
branches.cn: 充足与秀美：可观的规模，以及开启整个词族的最早文学义「美」。

branches.en: SEPARATE MARKET WORD: a festival day borrowed from Latin, joined only by spelling.
branches.cn: 另源的集市词：从拉丁语借来的节日，只靠拼写与前者合流。

intro.en: Fair is a native English adjective whose endings are Germanic, while the market noun arrived separately from Latin, so the family carries two unrelated histories.
intro.cn: 该词是英语本族的形容词，其词尾属日耳曼语；而表示集市的名词另从拉丁语传入，因此这个词族携带两段互不相干的历史。

latinIntro.en: The adjective has no Latin source. The Latin forms below belong only to the market noun, and the Latin word for a festival day is not related to the adjective for beauty or justice.
latinIntro.cn: 这个形容词没有拉丁语来源。下列拉丁形式只属于表示集市的名词；拉丁语中表示节日的词，与表示美或公正的形容词并无关联。

items.example: Both teams played a fair game.
items.exampleCN: 两队都按规则比赛。

items.example: The shares were fairly divided.
items.exampleCN: 份额被公平地分开了。

items.example: The review questioned the fairness of the test.
items.exampleCN: 评审质疑这项测试的公平性。

items.example: It was unfair to single out one applicant.
items.exampleCN: 单独挑出一名申请者是不公平的。

items.meaningCN: 愿意不带偏见地判断的
items.example: A fair-minded reader will check the sources.
items.exampleCN: 公正的读者会去核对来源。

items.meaning: the site of a market or show
items.example: Trucks queued at the gate of the fairground.
items.exampleCN: 卡车在集市场地门口排队。

items.meaning: loyal only while things go well
items.example: A fair-weather ally left when the storm came.
items.exampleCN: 一个只能同甘的盟友在风暴来时就离开了。

items.example: The coach praised the visiting side for its fair play.
items.exampleCN: 教练称赞客队遵守规则。

items.structure: fayre (revived spelling of the market noun)
items.meaningCN: 仿古拼写的集市或节庆
items.example: The village held a summer fayre on the green.
items.exampleCN: 村子在草地上举办了夏季集市。

derivatives.zh: 公平；公正（基础词加表性质的名词后缀，由形容词转为抽象状态）
公正地；相当地（基础词加副词后缀，语义扩展到程度适中）

公正的（基础词与「心智」复合再加分词后缀，指判断不受私利左右）

definition_zh: 繁殖；育种；饲养；教养；繁殖季
definition_en: the process of producing offspring, or the controlled improvement of animals and plants
core_image: 春天的鱼塘里，工人忙着分池、配对、记录鱼卵
scene: 鱼塘在春天进入最忙的季节，工人忙着分池和配对。场长说： Breeding starts when the water warms above fifteen degrees.
sceneCN: 这里指「繁殖」（第 1 个义项：生物产生后代的过程）；句意为当水温升到十五度以上时，繁殖就开始了。

pos.zh: 繁殖；育种；饲养；教养；繁殖季（不可数）

senses.title: The production of offspring
senses.definition: the process by which animals or plants produce young
senses.definitionCN: 动物或植物产生后代的过程
senses.example: Breeding starts when the water warms above fifteen degrees.
senses.exampleCN: 当水温升到十五度以上时，繁殖就开始了。
senses.why: The core sense is biological: one generation produces the next, with or without human help.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是生物的：一个世代产生下一个世代，无论有没有人帮助。

senses.title: Controlled breeding and improvement
senses.definition: the deliberate selection of parents to improve a line or breed
senses.definitionCN: 有意选择亲本以改良品系或品种
senses.example: Selective breeding raised the sugar content of the beets.
senses.exampleCN: 选择育种提高了甜菜的含糖量。
senses.why: Humans take the natural process and steer it, so breeding becomes a planned method of improvement.
senses.whyCN: 人类接手自然过程并操控方向，于是繁殖成为有计划的改良方法。

senses.title: Keeping and raising animals
senses.definition: the work of keeping animals for reproduction or production
senses.definitionCN: 为繁殖或生产而饲养动物的工作
senses.example: Fish breeding requires clean water and steady temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 鱼类养殖需要清洁的水与稳定的温度。
senses.why: Once animals are kept, breeding names the whole husbandry activity, not only the mating.
senses.whyCN: 一旦动物被饲养，breeding 就命名整套养殖活动，而不只是交配。

senses.title: Good manners or upbringing
senses.definition: the manners and behaviour produced by upbringing
senses.definitionCN: 由养育形成的举止与行为方式
senses.example: His calm breeding showed in every room he entered.
senses.exampleCN: 他从容的教养在每走进一个房间时都显露出来。
senses.why: The old metaphor treats upbringing as cultivation: a person is 'bred' the way an animal is bred.
senses.whyCN: 旧的隐喻把养育当作栽培：人像动物一样被「育」出来。

senses.title: The breeding season or behaviour
senses.definition: the period or set of behaviours associated with mating
senses.definitionCN: 与交配相关的时期或行为组合
senses.example: The birds return to the island for breeding in April.
senses.exampleCN: 这些鸟在四月回到岛上繁殖。
senses.why: Animals breed in seasons, so the noun also names the time and the behaviour that go with reproduction.
senses.whyCN: 动物在特定季节繁殖，因此这个名词也命名与繁殖相伴的时期与行为。

senses.title: Developing a new variety
senses.definition: the long process of producing a stable new variety
senses.definitionCN: 培育稳定新品种的长期过程
senses.example: The breeding of this rose took twelve years.
senses.exampleCN: 培育这个月季品种花了十二年。
senses.why: A variety is not made in one cross; breeding names the repeated cycles that stabilize it.
senses.whyCN: 一个品种不是一次杂交就能做成；breeding 命名使它稳定的反复循环。

senses.title: Mating arrangements
senses.definition: the pairing of selected males and females
senses.definitionCN: 把选定的雌雄个体配对
senses.example: The breeding of the two prize animals was arranged months ahead.
senses.exampleCN: 两头获奖动物的配种提前几个月就安排好了。
senses.why: In practice breeding often means the specific pairing decisions a manager makes.
senses.whyCN: 在实践中，breeding 常指管理者做出的具体配对决定。

senses.title: A place or source that fosters something
senses.definition: a situation or place that encourages something to develop
senses.definitionCN: 促使某事物发展的情境或场所
senses.example: Stagnant water is a breeding ground for mosquitoes.
senses.exampleCN: 积水是蚊子的滋生地。
senses.why: The picture of animals multiplying in a favorable place extends to anything that lets a problem multiply.
senses.whyCN: 动物在有利场所大量繁殖的图像，被扩展到任何让问题滋生的地方。

intro.en: Breeding is the noun from breed, which comes from Old English bredan 'to warm, cherish, produce young'. The word is native Germanic, with no Latin source. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: breeding 是 breed 的名词形式，而 breed 来自古英语 bredan「保暖、抚育、生育」。这个词是本族日耳曼词，没有拉丁语来源。年代均为约数。

items.en: Bredan meant 'to warm, keep warm, cherish', especially young. The sense 'produce offspring' grew from the care given to young animals.
items.cn: bredan 意为「保暖、保温、抚育」，尤指抚育幼仔。「生育后代」义从对幼仔的照料发展而来。

items.en: Breed is related to brood 'a family of young' and broth 'liquid in which food is cooked', both going back to a Germanic root connected with warming.
items.cn: breed 与 brood「一窝幼仔」、broth「煮食物的汤液」相关，它们都追溯到与「加温」有关的日耳曼词根。

items.en: In Middle English the verb extended from cherishing the young to producing them, and the noun breeding named the whole process.
items.cn: 在中古英语中，这个动词从抚育幼仔扩展到生育幼仔，名词 breeding 则命名整个过程。

items.en: By the sixteenth century breeding also meant the manners formed by upbringing, a metaphor of cultivation applied to people.
items.cn: 到 16 世纪，breeding 也指由养育形成的举止，这是把栽培隐喻用于人。

items.en: The nineteenth century made breeding a technical term for controlled improvement of plants and stock, alongside pedigree records and selection.
items.cn: 19 世纪使 breeding 成为有控改良动植物品种的技术术语，并与谱系记录和选择相伴。

items.en: Source uncertain (root): the deeper Indo-European origin of the Germanic warming root is reconstructed with competing accounts, and the first use of breeding for manners is dated only approximately.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词根）：日耳曼「加温」词根的更深印欧来源属重构，存在不同假说；breeding 表示举止的最早使用也只有大致年代。

note.en: Group one holds forms from the same breed family that are easily confused; group two holds near terms for producing and raising young.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 breed 词族、容易混淆的形式；第二组是表示生育与养育的邻近词。

entries.definition: To produce offspring, or a group of animals of one type; breeding is the process noun.
entries.definitionCN: 指生育后代，或指一类动物；breeding 是过程名词。

entries.definition: The past tense and past participle of breed; it is a verb form, not the activity.
entries.definitionCN: breed 的过去式与过去分词；是动词形式，不是活动本身。

entries.definition: A person who breeds animals or plants; the -er suffix names the agent.
entries.definitionCN: 指从事动植物繁育的人；-er 后缀命名施动者。

entries.definition: The young of one hatching or birth, or to sit on eggs; it is related to breed but names the group or the sitting.
entries.definitionCN: 指一次孵化或生产的一窝幼仔，或指孵蛋；与 breed 相关，但命名群体或孵卧行为。

entries.definition: The biological process by which organisms make new organisms; it is wider and includes plants and microbes.
entries.definitionCN: 指生物产生新个体的生物学过程；范围更广，包括植物与微生物。

entries.definition: The care and feeding of young until they are independent; breeding is conception and birth, rearing comes after.
entries.definitionCN: 指对幼体的照料与喂养直到独立；breeding 关乎受孕与出生，rearing 在其后。

entries.definition: Producing new plants or spreading a group; it is common in horticulture and can be asexual.
entries.definitionCN: 指产生新植物或扩大群体；常用于园艺，也可以是无性的。

entries.definition: Preparing land and growing crops; it is about tending plants, not producing offspring.
entries.definitionCN: 指整地并种植作物；关乎照料植物，而非产生后代。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: breed + -ing: the process of producing young.
normal.cn: breed + -ing：产生后代的过程。

normal.en: The family runs breed, bred, breeder, breeding, crossbreeding, inbreeding.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 breed、bred、breeder、breeding、crossbreeding、inbreeding。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: breeding season, breeding program, captive breeding.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：繁殖季、育种计划、圈养繁殖。

normal.en: Selective breeding is the human-guided version of natural reproduction.
normal.cn: 选择育种是自然繁殖的人为指导版本。

normal.en: The figurative breeding ground lets a problem multiply like animals.
normal.cn: 比喻的滋生地让问题像动物一样大量繁殖。

abstract.en: Picture a pond in spring full of eggs and tiny fish.
abstract.cn: 想象春天的池塘满是鱼卵与小鱼。

abstract.en: Picture a gardener choosing which plants to let seed.
abstract.cn: 想象园丁挑选让哪些植物结籽。

abstract.en: Picture a person whose calm manners were formed at home.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人从容的举止是在家里养成的。

examples.en: Captive breeding saved the species from extinction.
examples.cn: 圈养繁殖把该物种从灭绝中救了回来。

examples.en: The breeding program selects for drought tolerance.
examples.cn: 这个育种计划选择耐旱性。

examples.en: The marsh is a breeding ground for thousands of birds.
examples.cn: 这片沼泽是成千上万只鸟的繁殖地。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「布里丁」——春天里忙着配对、下仔、育幼的那段事 → 繁殖、育种

root: breed（古英语 bredan「保暖、抚育、生育」）+ -ing；本族日耳曼词，与 brood「一窝幼仔」、broth「汤液」相关，无拉丁语来源。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one process: animals produce young, humans guide the process, and the same word extends to husbandry, manners, seasons and places where things multiply.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一个过程展开：动物产生后代，人类引导这个过程，同一个词再延伸到养殖、举止、季节以及事物大量滋生的地方。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a spring pond busy with eggs, fry and caretakers.
core.cn: 核心意象：春天的池塘里满是鱼卵、小鱼与忙碌的照料者。

branches.en: BIOLOGY AND SEASON: producing young, and the time and behaviour that surround it.
branches.cn: 生物学与季节：产生后代，以及围绕它的时期与行为。

branches.en: HUMAN GUIDANCE: selection, long variety development and specific pairing decisions.
branches.cn: 人类引导：选择、长期的品种培育，以及具体配对决定。

branches.en: HUSBANDRY: keeping and raising animals becomes an occupation.
branches.cn: 养殖：饲养与养育动物成为一种职业。

branches.en: UPBRINGING: cultivation as a metaphor for manners.
branches.cn: 教养：把栽培用作举止的隐喻。

branches.en: METAPHOR: a place where something multiplies.
branches.cn: 比喻：某事物大量滋生的地方。

intro.en: Breeding is breed plus -ing. Both elements are native English, so the word has no Latin affix, though it belongs to the same Germanic family as brood.
intro.cn: breeding 是 breed 加 -ing。两个成分都是英语本族成分，因此这个词没有拉丁词缀，但它与 brood 同属日耳曼词族。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin element in breeding: breed comes from Old English bredan, and -ing is a native suffix. Latin has no share in this word.
latinIntro.cn: breeding 中没有拉丁成分：breed 来自古英语 bredan，-ing 是本族后缀。拉丁语与这个词无关。

items.structure: Old English bredan (to warm, cherish, produce young)
items.example: The rabbits breed twice a year.
items.exampleCN: 这些兔子一年繁殖两次。

items.example: Breeding names the process.
items.exampleCN: breeding 命名这个过程。

items.example: The breeder keeps pedigree records.
items.exampleCN: 育种者保存谱系记录。

items.example: The birds were bred in captivity.
items.exampleCN: 这些鸟在圈养环境中繁育。

items.example: Breeding requires steady conditions.
items.exampleCN: 繁殖需要稳定的条件。

items.example: Crossbreeding adds new traits.
items.exampleCN: 杂交增添新性状。

items.example: Inbreeding lowers vigor.
items.exampleCN: 近交降低活力。

items.meaning: a place where animals breed or problems multiply
items.meaningCN: 动物繁殖或问题滋生的地方
items.example: Warm shallow water is a breeding ground.
items.exampleCN: 温暖的浅水是一处繁殖地。

definition_zh: n. 喷出；弹出；驱逐；弹射（逃生）
definition_en: the act of forcing something or someone out; escape from an aircraft by an explosive seat
core_image: 超声室屏幕上标着一个百分比，医生用笔点着它解释心脏每次收缩泵出的血量比例；座椅上方的黄色拉环与「弹射座椅」标牌；一封信被推到桌沿外
scene: 医院超声室里，屏幕上标着一个百分比，医生指着它说这是心脏每次收缩泵出的血量比例。 The report listed an ejection fraction of sixty per cent.
sceneCN: 这里 ejection 指「用突然推力把东西弄出去的动作」（第 1 个义项：喷出；弹出），医学上特指心脏泵血；句意是报告列出射血分数为百分之六十。图中可辨识物件：超声屏幕、百分比、医生的笔。

pos.zh: 喷出；弹出；驱逐；弹射（逃生）

senses.title: The act of forcing out
senses.definition: the act of forcing something out with a sudden push
senses.definitionCN: （名词）用突然推力把东西弄出去的动作
senses.example: The report listed an ejection fraction of sixty per cent.
senses.exampleCN: 报告列出射血分数为百分之六十。
senses.why: A percentage marked on an ultrasound screen with a pen tip pointing at it.
senses.whyCN: 超声屏幕上标着一个百分比，笔尖正指着它。

senses.title: The act of expelling
senses.definition: the act of forcing a person to leave a place
senses.definitionCN: （名词）强迫某人离开某地的行为
senses.example: The letter announced his ejection from the club after the third warning.
senses.exampleCN: 那封信宣布，第三次警告之后他将被逐出俱乐部。
senses.why: A formal letter pushed to the edge of a desk beside a membership card.
senses.whyCN: 一封正式信函被推到桌沿，旁边放着一张会员卡。

senses.title: Escape by ejection seat
senses.definition: the escape of a pilot from an aircraft by an explosive seat
senses.definitionCN: （名词）飞行员借爆炸座椅逃离飞机
senses.example: The yellow handle above the seat is the last step before ejection.
senses.exampleCN: 座椅上方那个黄色拉环，是弹射之前的最后一步。
senses.why: A yellow loop above a cockpit seat beside a printed warning plate.
senses.whyCN: 驾驶舱座椅上方一个黄色拉环，旁边一块印着警告的标牌。

intro.en: Ejection is Latin ejectio, a throwing out, built on ejectus from ejicere, which joins ex- meaning out to jacere meaning to throw.
intro.cn: ejection 就是拉丁语 ejectio（扔出去这件事），建立在 ejectus 之上，而 ejectus 来自 ejicere，它把 ex-（向外）与 jacere（投掷）结合。

items.en: Latin jacere means to throw.
items.cn: 拉丁语 jacere 意为投掷。

dict_mnemonic.text: ejection ＝ e-（向外）＋ ject（投掷，拉丁 jacere）＋ -ion（名词后缀，表动作）＝「往外扔这件事」。动词 eject 加 -ion 就成名词，同规律：reject → rejection 拒绝、inject → injection 注射、project → projection 投射、object → objection 反对。三个高频术语直接背：ejection seat 弹射座椅、ejection fraction 射血分数（心脏每次收缩泵出的血量比例）、ejection from a club 被逐出俱乐部。近义 expulsion 偏「开除、驱逐」，emission 偏「排放气体或光」，discharge 偏「排出、释放、出院」。注意 ejection 可数（一次弹射／一次驱逐），但射血分数语境里通常单数。

root: 拉丁语 ex-（向外）＋ jacere（投掷）→ ejectus（被扔出的）＋ -ion → ejection（喷出；驱逐）

definition_zh: 等位基因；同一基因位置上的一种替代版本
definition_en: one of two or more alternative forms of a gene at the same position on a chromosome
core_image: 同一把椅子上放着可替换的坐垫，位置不变，垫子的花色不同
scene: 遗传课上，同一朵花的花色由同一个位置上的两份遗传信息决定。老师说： This plant carries two different alleles for flower color.
sceneCN: 这里指「等位基因」（第 1 个义项：同一基因位置上的一种可替代版本）；句意为这株植物在花色这个基因上携带两个不同的等位基因。

pos.zh: 等位基因；同一基因座的替代版本（可数，复数 alleles）

senses.title: One version of a gene
senses.definition: one of the alternative forms that a gene can take at a fixed position on a chromosome
senses.definitionCN: 一个基因在染色体固定位置上可以采取的一种替代形式
senses.example: This plant carries two different alleles for flower color.
senses.exampleCN: 这株植物在花色这个基因上携带两个不同的等位基因。
senses.why: The word names a version, not a place: the locus stays the same, while the sequence at that locus differs.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名的是一个版本，而不是一个位置：基因座不变，该位置上的序列却不同。

senses.title: One member of a pair
senses.titleCN: 成对等位基因中的一方
senses.definition: one of the two copies of a gene that a diploid organism carries
senses.definitionCN: 二倍体生物携带的两份基因拷贝中的一份
senses.example: Each parent contributed one allele to the child.
senses.exampleCN: 每个亲代都向孩子贡献了一个等位基因。
senses.why: Because chromosomes come in pairs, alleles are usually discussed in pairs, one inherited from each parent.
senses.whyCN: 因为染色体成对存在，等位基因通常也成对讨论，一份来自一个亲代。

senses.title: Multiple alleles in a population
senses.definition: any of three or more alternative forms of the same gene found in a population
senses.definitionCN: 同一基因在群体中出现的三种或更多替代形式之一
senses.example: Human blood groups depend on multiple alleles at one locus.
senses.exampleCN: 人类血型取决于同一基因座上的复等位基因。
senses.why: A single individual carries two copies, but a whole population can hold many versions, so the noun extends beyond the pair.
senses.whyCN: 单个个体只携带两份，但整个群体可以拥有许多版本，因此这个名词超出成对的范围。

senses.title: A dominant allele
senses.definition: an allele whose effect is visible even when only one copy is present
senses.definitionCN: 只有一份拷贝也能表现出效果的等位基因
senses.example: The dominant allele produces a dark seed coat.
senses.exampleCN: 这个显性等位基因产生深色种皮。
senses.why: The allele itself is neutral; 'dominant' describes what happens when it meets a different version in the same cell.
senses.whyCN: 等位基因本身是中性的；「显性」描述的是它与另一版本在同一细胞中相遇时的结果。

senses.title: A recessive allele
senses.definition: an allele whose effect is hidden when a dominant allele is present
senses.definitionCN: 与显性等位基因同时存在时效果被掩盖的等位基因
senses.example: The recessive allele reappears in the next generation.
senses.exampleCN: 隐性等位基因在下一代重新出现。
senses.why: A recessive version is still present and still inherited; it is only its visible effect that is covered.
senses.whyCN: 隐性版本仍然存在、仍然可遗传，被盖住的只是它可见的效果。

senses.title: A mutant allele
senses.definition: an allele produced by a mutation and differing from the original sequence
senses.definitionCN: 由突变产生、与原始序列不同的等位基因
senses.example: The mutant allele removes one base from the sequence.
senses.exampleCN: 这个突变等位基因从序列中删去了一个碱基。
senses.why: New alleles arise by mutation, so the word is also used for the fresh version before it spreads in a population.
senses.whyCN: 新的等位基因由突变产生，因此这个词也用来指在群体中扩散之前的那个新版本。

senses.title: A wild-type allele
senses.definition: the allele regarded as the standard or original form in a population
senses.definitionCN: 在群体中被视为标准或原始形式的等位基因
senses.example: The wild-type allele restores the normal wing shape.
senses.exampleCN: 野生型等位基因恢复了正常的翅形。
senses.why: Once a mutant is known, the common version needs a name, and 'wild type' marks the reference against which change is measured.
senses.whyCN: 一旦已知某个突变，常见版本就需要一个名称，「野生型」标记出衡量变化的参照。

senses.title: Allele frequency
senses.titleCN: 等位基因频率（群体层面）
senses.definition: the proportion of a particular allele among all copies of that gene in a population
senses.definitionCN: 某一特定等位基因在群体中该基因全部拷贝里所占的比例
senses.example: The allele frequency rose after the drought.
senses.exampleCN: 干旱之后该等位基因的频率上升了。
senses.why: Population genetics turns the version into a share, which is why the word appears in frequency counts and not only in pedigrees.
senses.whyCN: 群体遗传学把这个版本变成一个占比，因此这个词不仅出现在系谱中，也出现在频率统计中。

intro.en: Allele is a shortened form of allelomorph, a term coined in the early twentieth century from Greek allelon 'one another' and morphe 'form'. It is Greek in origin, with no Latin source. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: allele 是 allelomorph 的缩短形式；后者于 20 世纪初由希腊 allelon「彼此」与 morphe「形式」构成。它源自希腊语，没有拉丁语来源。年代均为约数。

items.en: Allēlon means 'of one another, mutually'. It marks the relation between alternative versions that occupy the same place.
items.cn: allēlon 意为「彼此的、相互的」，标记占据同一位置的不同版本之间的关系。

items.en: Morphē meant 'form, shape'. In scientific compounds it names a physical or structural form.
items.cn: morphē 意为「形式、形状」，在科学复合词中命名物理或结构形式。

items.en: The compound allelomorph was coined in the early 1900s, generally associated with William Bateson, for alternative forms of a gene.
items.cn: 复合词 allelomorph 于 1900 年代初被造出，一般与 William Bateson 相关，用来指基因的替代形式。

items.en: Allele is the shortened form and became the standard term in genetics; the longer allelomorph survives mainly in historical writing.
items.cn: allele 是缩短形式，后来成为遗传学的标准术语；较长的 allelomorph 主要留在历史文献中。

items.en: Modern genetics extends the word to allele frequencies, multiple alleles and reference alleles such as the wild type.
items.cn: 现代遗传学把这个词扩展到等位基因频率、复等位基因以及野生型等参照版本。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates and root): the exact coinage date of allelomorph is not settled, and the deeper origin of Greek allos 'other' is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与词根）：allelomorph 的确切造词年代未有定论；希腊 allos「其他」的更深来源属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds forms built on the same Greek elements that are easily confused; group two holds neighbouring genetic terms for position and version.
note.cn: 第一组是同出希腊成分、容易混淆的形式；第二组是表示位置与版本的邻近遗传学术语。

entries.definition: The long historical word for an allele; it is the same concept, not a different kind of gene.
entries.definitionCN: 指等位基因的早期长词；是同一概念，而非另一类基因。

entries.definition: Relating to an allele; it describes a relationship, while allele names the version itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指与等位基因相关的；描述关系，而 allele 命名版本本身。

entries.definition: The state of existing as alternative forms at one locus; it is the abstract noun, not a countable allele.
entries.definitionCN: 指在同一基因座以替代形式存在的状态；是抽象名词，不是可数的等位基因。

entries.definition: The share of one allele among all copies in a population; it is a number, not the allele.
entries.definitionCN: 指某一等位基因在群体全部拷贝中的占比；是一个数值，不是等位基因本身。

entries.definition: A unit of inheritance at a locus; an allele is one version of that unit.
entries.definitionCN: 指一个基因座上的遗传单位；等位基因是该单位的一个版本。

entries.definition: The fixed position on a chromosome; alleles occupy a locus but are not the locus.
entries.definitionCN: 指染色体上的固定位置；等位基因占据基因座，但并不等于基因座。

entries.definition: The combination of alleles an individual carries; it is the pair, not either member.
entries.definitionCN: 指个体携带的等位基因组合；是成对的组合，而非其中一方。

entries.definition: Any differing version of a sequence; allele is its standard term when the version sits at a known gene locus.
entries.definitionCN: 指序列的任何不同版本；当该版本位于已知基因座时，标准术语就是等位基因。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: allelo- 'one another' + -morph 'form': alternative forms of one another.
normal.cn: allelo-「彼此」+ -morph「形式」：彼此替代的不同形式。

normal.en: The family runs allele, allelic, allelism, allelomorph, multiallelic.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 allele、allelic、allelism、allelomorph、multiallelic。

normal.en: Fixed phrases pair it with dominance: dominant allele, recessive allele.
normal.cn: 固定搭配把它与显隐性配对：显性等位基因、隐性等位基因。

normal.en: A gene is the position; an allele is one text written at that position.
normal.cn: 基因是位置，等位基因是写在该位置上的一版文字。

normal.en: Population genetics counts allele frequencies, not individual alleles alone.
normal.cn: 群体遗传学统计等位基因频率，而不只统计单个等位基因。

abstract.en: Picture one parking space where different cars can park.
abstract.cn: 想象同一个车位，可以停不同的车。

abstract.en: Picture one role in a play played by different actors on different nights.
abstract.cn: 想象同一出戏里的一个角色，不同夜晚由不同演员扮演。

abstract.en: Picture one socket that accepts several interchangeable parts.
abstract.cn: 想象同一个插口可以接上几种可互换的零件。

examples.en: A child inherits one allele from each parent.
examples.cn: 孩子从每个亲代各继承一个等位基因。

examples.en: The two alleles differ by a single base pair.
examples.cn: 这两个等位基因只差一个碱基对。

examples.en: Selection changed the allele frequencies within a decade.
examples.cn: 选择在十年内改变了等位基因频率。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿利尔」——同一个座位上轮流坐的另一个人 → 等位基因

root: 希腊 allelon「彼此」+ morphe「形式」，经早期术语 allelomorph 缩短而来；无拉丁语来源，属纯粹希腊来源的科学复合词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one position: a fixed locus accepts alternative versions, and those versions are then paired, counted across a population, and labelled by their effects.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一个位置展开：固定的基因座接受不同版本，这些版本再被成对讨论、在群体中计数，并按效果获得标签。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one seat with interchangeable cushions.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一个座位上放着可替换的坐垫。

branches.en: VERSION AND PAIR: one alternative form, and the two copies a diploid organism carries.
branches.cn: 版本与成对：一个替代形式，以及二倍体生物携带的两份拷贝。

branches.en: MANY VERSIONS: a population can hold more than two forms at one locus.
branches.cn: 多个版本：一个群体在同一基因座可以拥有两种以上的形式。

branches.en: EXPRESSION: dominant and recessive describe what happens when two versions meet.
branches.cn: 表现：显性与隐性描述两个版本相遇时发生什么。

branches.en: ORIGIN AND REFERENCE: mutant versions are new, wild-type versions are the standard.
branches.cn: 来源与参照：突变版本是新的，野生型版本是标准。

branches.en: POPULATION: the version becomes a share in a gene pool.
branches.cn: 群体：版本变成基因库中的一个占比。

intro.en: Allele is built from two Greek combining elements, allelo- 'one another' and -morph 'form'; it is a scientific compound, not a Latin root with suffixes.
intro.cn: allele 由两个希腊组合成分构成：allelo-「彼此」与 -morph「形式」；它是科学复合词，而非拉丁词根加后缀。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin element here: allēlon and morphē are Greek, and the word was coined inside modern genetics from Greek materials.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁成分：allēlon 与 morphē 都是希腊语，这个词是在现代遗传学内部用希腊语材料造出的。

items.structure: Greek allēlon (of one another) as a combining form
items.example: The element marks versions that stand in place of one another.
items.exampleCN: 这个成分标记彼此替代的版本。

items.example: The suffix also appears in polymorphic.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀也出现在 polymorphic 中。

items.meaning: an alternative form of a gene
items.example: Each allele sits at the same locus.
items.exampleCN: 每个等位基因都位于同一基因座。

items.example: Allelic variation is common in wild populations.
items.exampleCN: 等位变异在野生群体中很常见。

items.meaning: the state of being alternative forms
items.example: Allelism at one locus produces several phenotypes.
items.exampleCN: 同一基因座的等位性产生几种表型。

items.meaning: the older term for an allele
items.example: Allelomorph is now mainly historical.
items.exampleCN: allelomorph 现在主要见于历史文献。

items.example: Multiallelic loci complicate diagnosis.
items.exampleCN: 多等位基因的基因座使诊断复杂化。

items.meaning: the share of one allele in a population
items.meaningCN: 某一等位基因在群体中的占比
items.example: The allele frequency stayed near one half.
items.exampleCN: 该等位基因频率保持在二分之一附近。

definition_en: a broad area of land or space, an administrative division, a field of activity, or an approximate range
core_image: 一条线在地上画出的圈：圈内是一片地，圈外是别的世界
scene: 火车穿过山口之后，窗外的语言、屋顶和葡萄品种都变了。 The conductor said that they had entered another region, where the roofs and the grapes looked nothing like the ones at home.
sceneCN: 这里 region 是「地理区域」（第 2 个义项：世界或国土的一部分）；句意：列车员说他们已经进入另一个区域，那里的屋顶和葡萄都跟家乡完全不一样。场景要点：山口隧道、车窗外变换的屋顶样式、葡萄园、站牌上的地名。

pos.zh: 地区；区域；行政区；领域；部位

derivatives.zh: 地区的；区域性的；地方性的

senses.title: A broad tract of land
senses.definition: a broad area of land whose boundaries are not precisely fixed
senses.definitionCN: 一大片土地，其边界并不精确固定
senses.example: The northern region is mostly forest and thin soil.
senses.exampleCN: 北部地区主要是森林和贫瘠的土壤。
senses.why: Latin regio came from regere 'to direct, rule', and originally named a line or boundary. A region is land that has been marked off, even if the mark is only approximate.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 regio 来自 regere“引导、统治”，最初指一条线或边界。region 就是被划出来的一片地，即使那条线只是大致的。

senses.title: A part of the world
senses.definition: a part of the world or of a country, usually identified by climate, culture, or position
senses.definitionCN: 世界或国家的一个部分，通常以气候、文化或位置来识别
senses.example: Coffee grows best in tropical regions with steady rain.
senses.exampleCN: 咖啡在雨水稳定的热带地区长得最好。
senses.why: The bounded tract is scaled up to the map. Once the line is drawn on a map, the land inside is a region, and neighbouring regions acquire different climates and customs.
senses.whyCN: 被划出的地块放大到了地图上。一旦线被画在地图上，圈内的土地就是一个 region，相邻的区域也获得了不同的气候与习俗。

senses.title: An administrative division
senses.definition: a named administrative division of a country, with its own government or offices
senses.definitionCN: 国家的一个有名行政区划，拥有自己的政府或机构
senses.example: The region of Campania has its own governor and budget.
senses.exampleCN: 坎帕尼亚大区有自己的行政长官和预算。
senses.why: Here the boundary is legal rather than natural. The line is drawn by an authority, which is exactly what the root regere 'to rule' implies: the ruler's line makes the region.
senses.whyCN: 这里的边界是法律的，而不是自然的。线由权威画出，这正是词根 regere“统治”所暗示的：统治者的线造出了区域。

senses.title: The countryside around a city
senses.definition: the rural area lying around a city, used in contrast with the city itself
senses.definitionCN: 环绕城市的那片乡村地带，与城市本身相对
senses.example: The old nobility still owned estates in the region.
senses.exampleCN: 旧贵族仍在这一带拥有庄园。
senses.why: From the late 14th century the word also named the land outside the walls. The city is the centre, and the region is the ring of fields and villages around it.
senses.whyCN: 从 14 世纪晚期起，这个词也指城墙之外的土地。城市是中心，region 就是环绕它的那一圈田野与村庄。

senses.title: A part of the body
senses.definition: a defined part or zone of the body, especially in anatomy and medicine
senses.definitionCN: 身体的一个确定部位或区域，尤用于解剖学与医学
senses.example: The surgeon worked on the lumbar region of the spine.
senses.exampleCN: 外科医生在脊柱的腰部区域动手术。
senses.why: The line that marks off land is redrawn on the body. Anatomy divides the body into named regions, so the same word for a bounded tract now names a bounded part.
senses.whyCN: 划出土地的那条线被重新画在身体上。解剖学把身体分成有名字的区域，于是同一个表示“被划出的地块”的词，现在命名一个被划出的部位。

senses.title: A sphere of activity or thought
senses.definition: a field of activity, knowledge, or thought with its own boundaries
senses.definitionCN: 活动、知识或思想的一个领域，有自己的边界
senses.example: That question lies outside the region of physics.
senses.exampleCN: 那个问题落在物理学的领域之外。
senses.why: The boundary becomes invisible. What separates physics from poetry is not a fence but a limit of method, yet the mind still pictures a territory with an inside and an outside.
senses.whyCN: 边界变得看不见了。把物理学与诗歌分开的不是篱笆，而是方法的界限，但头脑仍然把它想象成一块有内有外的领地。

senses.title: An approximate range of a number
senses.definition: in the phrase in the region of, approximately or about a particular amount
senses.definitionCN: 用于 in the region of 这一短语，表示大约、在某个数量左右
senses.example: The repairs will cost in the region of ten thousand pounds.
senses.exampleCN: 维修费用大约在一万英镑左右。
senses.why: The bounded area becomes a bounded interval on a scale. A number 'in the region of' ten thousand is not exactly ten thousand; it is somewhere inside that neighbourhood.
senses.whyCN: 「某一范围」也可以表示大约的数量：介于两个界限之间，就像一大片区域围出的空间，引申为「约数」。英语里 in the region of 就是这个用法。

senses.title: A layer or zone of the atmosphere
senses.definition: one of the horizontal layers or zones of the atmosphere, oceans, or space
senses.definitionCN: 大气、海洋或空间中水平划分的一层或一个带
senses.example: Weather balloons climb into the upper region of the atmosphere.
senses.exampleCN: 气象气球升入大气的高层区域。
senses.why: Height is divided into horizontal bands the way land is divided into tracts. The upper region is not a place with a fence but a layer with a defined range.
senses.whyCN: 高度像土地被分成地块那样，被分成水平的带。高层区域不是有篱笆的地方，而是一个有确定范围的一层。

senses.title: A bounded area in computing
senses.titleCN: 计算机中的一个限定区域
senses.definition: a defined block of memory, or a selected area of a screen or map
senses.definitionCN: 一块被限定的内存区域，或屏幕、地图上被选定的区域
senses.example: The program copies the image into a separate memory region.
senses.exampleCN: 程序把图像复制到一个单独的内存区域。
senses.why: Software needs edges even when nothing physical is being divided. A memory region is a range with a start and an end, the same bounded tract expressed as two addresses.
senses.whyCN: 即使没有实体被分割，软件也需要边界。内存区域是一段有起点和终点的范围，也就是同一块被限定的地，用两个地址表达出来。

intro.en: Region looks as if it begins with re-, but it does not: the re- belongs to the root reg-, from Latin regere 'to direct, rule'. The word's core is a line drawn to bound a tract of land. That makes region unlike recover (capere 'take'), require (quaerere 'ask'), research (circare 'go about') and reside (sedere 'sit'), all of which carry a real re- prefix.
intro.cn: region 看起来像以 re- 开头，其实不是：它的 re- 属于词根 reg-，来自拉丁语 regere“引导、统治”。这个词的核心是一条画出来、把一片地围住的线。因此 region 与 recover（capere“拿取”）、require（quaerere“询问”）、research（circare“绕行”）、reside（sedere“坐”）都不同，后四个才带真正的前缀 re-。

items.en: First recorded as regioun, 'tract of land of a considerable but indefinite extent'. It also meant 'a kingdom, country, nation; the people of a country'.
items.cn: 最早记录为 regioun，意为“范围相当大但边界不定的一片土地”，同时也表示“王国、国家、民族；一国的人民”。

items.en: From Anglo-French regioun and Old French region 'land, region, province' (12c.), and directly from Latin regionem, nominative regio.
items.cn: 来自盎格鲁法语 regioun 与古法语 region“土地、地区、省份”（12 世纪），并直接来自拉丁语 regionem（主格 regio）。

items.en: Latin regio meant 'a district, portion of a country, territory; a direction, line; boundary line, limit'. It was a noun of state from the past-participle stem of regere.
items.cn: 拉丁语 regio 意为“区、国家的一部分、领土；方向、直线；边界线、界限”。它是 regere 过去分词词干的性状名词。

items.en: Regere means 'to direct, rule', from PIE *reg- 'move in a straight line', with derivatives meaning 'to direct in a straight line', hence 'to lead, rule'. A straight line is what makes a boundary.
items.cn: regere 意为“引导、统治”，来自原始印欧语 *reg-“沿直线移动”，其派生义为“沿直线引导”，进而表示“带领、统治”。正是直线构成了边界。

items.en: The sense 'a part of the world' appears in the late 14th century, as does 'the rural area around a city'. The word is now both a map unit and a city's hinterland.
items.cn: “世界的一个部分”这一义项出现于 14 世纪晚期，“城市周边的乡村地带”也在同一时期出现。这个词如今既是地图单位，也是城市腹地。

items.en: The phrase in the region of 'about' is recorded from 1961. Regional is from the early 15th century, and subregion from 1830. The Latin root also gives regal, regent, regime, regulate, direct, correct and rectangle.
items.cn: 短语 in the region of“大约”记录于 1961 年。regional 始于 15 世纪早期，subregion 始于 1830 年。同一拉丁词根还给出 regal、regent、regime、regulate、direct、correct、rectangle。

note.en: The first group separates the derived forms from the noun; the second compares the four area words learners mix up. Region is usually a large or officially bounded area, while its re- is part of reg- 'rule', not the prefix of recover, require, research or reside.
note.cn: 第一组把派生形式同名词分开；第二组比较学习者容易混用的四个“区域”词。region 通常指较大或官方划定的区域，而它的 re- 属于 reg-“统治”，不是 recover、require、research、reside 的那个前缀。

entries.definition: relating to a particular region. It describes something belonging to a region, while region names the area itself.
entries.definitionCN: 与某一地区有关的。它描述属于某个地区的事物，而 region 命名这个地区本身。

entries.definition: loyalty to one's own region, or a feature peculiar to it. It is an attitude or a local trait, not the area.
entries.definitionCN: 对本地区的忠诚，或本地区特有的特征。它是一种态度或地方特色，而不是地区本身。

entries.definition: in a regional way or at the regional level. It modifies an action, while region is a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 以地区方式，或在地区层面上。它修饰动作，而 region 是名词。

entries.definition: a smaller division inside a region. The sub- marks a region within a region.
entries.definitionCN: 一个地区内部的更小分区。sub- 标记“区域之中的区域”。

entries.definition: a part of a place or a measured surface. It is the most general word and can be as small as a room; region usually suggests a larger or more defined stretch.
entries.definitionCN: 一个地方的一部分，或一个被测量的表面。它是最通用的词，可以小到一个房间；region 通常暗示更大或更明确的一片。

entries.definition: an official division of a city, country, or organization for administration. It is usually smaller and more precisely defined than a region.
entries.definitionCN: 城市、国家或组织为行政而划分的正式区域。它通常比 region 更小、边界更精确。

entries.definition: an area marked off for a particular purpose, such as a climate zone or a no-parking zone. It stresses function or rule, while region stresses land or extent.
entries.definitionCN: 为特定目的划出的区域，如气候带或禁停区。它强调功能或规则，而 region 强调土地或范围。

entries.definition: a kingdom, or a sphere of activity. It is more literary and more abstract than region, and it comes from a different French source, not from the Latin reg- root.
entries.definitionCN: 王国，或活动的领域。它比 region 更文学化、更抽象，而且来自另一条法语来源，并非拉丁语 reg- 词根。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: Latin regere 'to rule, direct', regio 'a bounded district', the *reg- family, and the five derived forms regional, regionally, regionalism, regionalize and subregion.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：拉丁语 regere“统治、引导”、regio“被划定的区”、*reg- 词族，以及五个派生形式 regional、regionally、regionalism、regionalize、subregion。

normal.en: regere means 'to rule, direct', and a ruler draws straight lines. A region is the land inside one of those lines.
normal.cn: regere 意为“统治、引导”，而统治者画直线。region 就是其中一条线以内的土地。

normal.en: The same *reg- root gives regal, regent, regime, regulate, direct, correct and rectangle — all about straight lines and rule.
normal.cn: 同一 *reg- 词根给出 regal、regent、regime、regulate、direct、correct、rectangle——全都关于直线与统治。

normal.en: Region's re- is not a prefix: it is the start of reg-, so do not link it to recover or reside.
normal.cn: region 的 re- 不是前缀：它是 reg- 的开头，所以不要把它和 recover 或 reside 联系起来。

normal.en: in the region of means 'about': a number inside a small neighbourhood on a scale.
normal.cn: in the region of 意为“大约”：刻度上某个数附近的一小片邻域。

normal.en: Regional is the adjective, regionalism the attitude, and subregion a region inside a region.
normal.cn: regional 是形容词，regionalism 是态度，subregion 是区域内部的区域。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler drawing one straight line across a map. Everything on one side becomes a region; everything on the other side becomes somewhere else.
abstract.cn: 想象一把尺子在地图上画下一条直线。线这一侧的一切成为一个 region；另一侧的一切成为别处。

abstract.en: The line can be moved from land to the body, to thought, to numbers, to memory: wherever a boundary is drawn, there is a region inside it.
abstract.cn: 这条线可以从土地移到身体、思想、数字与内存：只要画下一条边界，界内就有一个 region。

abstract.en: A region is not the line itself but the inside it creates, which is why the word always implies both an edge and a stretch of ground.
abstract.cn: region 不是线本身，而是线所造成的内部，所以这个词总同时暗示一条边和一片地。

examples.en: The wine is grown in a cool region near the coast.
examples.cn: 这种葡萄酒产自沿海一个凉爽的地区。

examples.en: Damage to that region of the brain can affect speech.
examples.cn: 大脑那个区域受损可能影响言语能力。

examples.en: A new laptop will cost in the region of eight hundred dollars.
examples.cn: 一台新笔记本电脑大约要八百美元。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞金」——瑞金既是一座城，也是一片有名的地区 → region 地区；区域（只借音，不表词源）

root: 源自拉丁语 regio“被划定的区”，其词根 regere 意为“引导、统治”，可追溯到原始印欧语 *reg-“沿直线移动”，核心是“用一条线划出来的一片地”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of region, all from one act: drawing a line to bound a stretch. The stretch can be land, a part of the world, a province, a city's hinterland, a body part, a field of thought, a numeric neighbourhood, a layer of air, or a block of memory.
sensesIntro.cn: region 的九个义项都来自同一个动作：画一条线，把一片范围围起来。这片范围可以是土地、世界的一部分、省份、城市腹地、身体部位、思想领域、数值邻域、大气的一层，或一块内存。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a straight line drawn to enclose a stretch of ground.
core.cn: 核心意象：画下一条直线，把一片地圈在里面。

branches.en: LAND: an indefinite tract, a part of the world, and an administrative province are the same enclosed ground at three scales.
branches.cn: 土地：边界不定的一片地、世界的一部分、行政区划，是同一片被圈起来的土地在三种尺度上。

branches.en: AROUND THE CITY: the line is drawn at the city wall, and the fields outside become the region.
branches.cn: 城市周边：线画在城墙处，墙外的田野就成了 region。

branches.en: THE BODY: anatomy redraws the line inside a person and names the enclosed part.
branches.cn: 身体：解剖学把线画进人体内部，并给被围住的部位命名。

branches.en: THOUGHT: the boundary becomes invisible, marking what a discipline does and does not cover.
branches.cn: 思想：边界变得看不见，标记一门学科涵盖与不涵盖的范围。

branches.en: MEASURED RANGES: a numeric neighbourhood, a layer of atmosphere, and a block of memory are all bounded intervals rather than ground.
branches.cn: 可测的范围：数值邻域、大气的一层、一块内存，都是有界的区间，而不是土地。

intro.en: Region is not re- plus a root; it is the Latin stem reg- plus -ion. English adds -al, -ly, -ism, -ize and sub-. The same reg- root also supplies regal, regent, regime, regulate, direct, correct and rectangle.
intro.cn: region 不是 re- 加词根，而是拉丁词干 reg- 加 -ion。英语再加 -al、-ly、-ism、-ize 与 sub-。同一 reg- 词根还供应 regal、regent、regime、regulate、direct、correct、rectangle。

latinIntro.en: Latin regere 'to direct, rule' gives the noun regio 'a district, boundary line', the noun rex 'king', and the noun regula 'rule, straight stick'. The PIE root *reg- means 'move in a straight line', which links ruling to drawing a straight boundary.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 regere“引导、统治”给出名词 regio“区、边界线”、名词 rex“国王”与名词 regula“规则、直尺”。原始印欧语词根 *reg- 意为“沿直线移动”，把“统治”与“画一条笔直的边界”联系起来。

items.meaning: a district bounded by a line
items.meaningCN: 被一条线划定的区域（reg- 引导 + -ion 状态名词）
items.example: The region has been famous for its wool for centuries.
items.exampleCN: 这个地区几百年来以羊毛闻名。

items.meaningCN: 地区的；区域性的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: Regional differences in accent are still strong.
items.exampleCN: 口音的地区差异仍然很明显。

items.meaning: at the level of a region
items.meaningCN: 在地区层面上（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The paper is published regionally, not nationally.
items.exampleCN: 这份报纸在地区发行，而不是全国发行。

items.meaning: loyalty to a region, or a local feature
items.meaningCN: 地方主义；地方特色（-ism 构成主义或特征）
items.example: The novel is full of the regionalism of the northern coast.
items.exampleCN: 这部小说充满北部海岸的地方特色。

items.meaningCN: 按地区组织；使区域化（-ize 构成动词）
items.example: The company regionalized its supply chain last year.
items.exampleCN: 公司去年把供应链按地区重新组织。

items.meaning: a smaller division within a region
items.meaningCN: 亚区；分区（sub- 在下 + region）
items.example: Each subregion has a different rainfall pattern.
items.exampleCN: 每个分区都有不同的降雨模式。

items.meaning: belonging to a king or queen
items.meaningCN: 王室的；帝王般的（reg- 王 + -al 形容词）
items.example: The hall was decorated in regal red and gold.
items.exampleCN: 大厅以帝王般的红金两色装饰。

items.meaning: a person who rules during a monarch's absence or minority
items.meaningCN: 摄政者（reg- 统治 + -ent 行为者）
items.example: A regent governed the country while the king was abroad.
items.exampleCN: 国王出国期间由一位摄政者治理国家。

items.meaningCN: 管理；调节（regula 规则、直尺 + -ate 动词）
items.example: The agency regulates the safety of new drugs.
items.exampleCN: 该机构监管新药的安全。

items.meaningCN: 指导；导演（dis- + regere 使变直）
items.example: She directed the whole production herself.
items.exampleCN: 整场制作由她亲自执导。

items.meaningCN: 改正；正确的（com- 共同 + regere 使直）
items.example: He corrected the spelling on the label.
items.exampleCN: 他改正了标签上的拼写。

items.meaning: a four-sided shape with right angles
items.meaningCN: 长方形；矩形（rect- 直 + angle 角）
items.example: The garden is laid out as a long rectangle.
items.exampleCN: 花园被布置成一个狭长的矩形。

latinEntries.structure: Latin verb, from PIE *reg- 'move in a straight line'

definition_zh: 巨大的；沉重的；大量的；严重的；体格魁梧的；块状的（岩体）；大面积的（病变）；厚重的（建筑）
definition_en: very large in size, weight or amount, often so large that it is striking or hard to deal with
core_image: 港口边立着一整块从山体切下的石料，旁边的卡车小得像个玩具
scene: 港口入口立着一整块从山体切下的石料，旁边的卡车小得像个玩具。 A massive block of granite now stands at the harbour entrance.
sceneCN: 这里指体积巨大、分量惊人（第 1 个义项：形体或体量极大）；句意为一块巨大的花岗岩石料如今立在港口入口处；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 巨大的；大量的；严重的
厚重的；块状的

derivatives.zh: 直接来自拉丁 massa「团块」，是该形容词的词基，义为「团块；大量；群众的」
由该形容词加表示方式的副词后缀构成，义为「巨大地；极其」
由该形容词加表示性质的名词后缀构成，义为「巨大；沉重感」
由「团块」加表示动作或集合的名词后缀构成，义为「体量组合」，是建筑用语
由同一词根经法语进入英语，义为「山块；地块」，指连成整体的一组山体

senses.title: Very large in size
senses.definition: occupying far more space than ordinary objects of its kind, so that it dominates a view
senses.definitionCN: 占据的空间远大于同类常见物体，因而在视野中占主导
senses.example: A massive crane lifted the bridge section into place.
senses.exampleCN: 一台巨大的起重机把桥段吊装到位。
senses.why: The Latin noun meant a lump or a mass, so the adjective first describes sheer bulk.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁名词意为「团块、一堆」，因此这个形容词首先描述的是纯粹的体量。

senses.title: Heavy and solid
senses.definition: thick and weighty, made of material that feels hard to move
senses.definitionCN: 厚而重，由让人感到难以搬动的材料做成
senses.example: The altar is a massive slab of stone.
senses.exampleCN: 祭坛是一整块沉重的石板。
senses.why: A mass has weight as well as size, so the adjective carries both impressions at once.
senses.whyCN: 团块既有体积也有重量，因此这个形容词同时带着两种感受。

senses.title: Huge in amount
senses.definition: present in a very large quantity, said of data, sums, effort or numbers of people
senses.definitionCN: 以极大的数量存在，用于数据、金额、努力或人数
senses.example: The archive holds a massive amount of correspondence.
senses.exampleCN: 这间档案馆藏有大量往来信件。
senses.why: Amounts can pile up like material, and a heap that keeps growing becomes a mass.
senses.whyCN: 数量可以像材料一样堆积，越堆越高的那一堆就成了「团块」。

senses.title: Extremely serious in effect
senses.definition: very great in severity, so that recovery or repair is difficult
senses.definitionCN: 严重程度极大，以至于恢复或修复都很困难
senses.example: The earthquake caused massive damage to the old town.
senses.exampleCN: 地震给老城造成了严重破坏。
