senses.why: Damage has size too, and damage of enormous size is expressed with the word for bulk.
senses.whyCN: 破坏也有「大小」，巨大规模的破坏就用表示体量的词来表达。

senses.title: Broad and heavy in build
senses.definition: having a large, solid body, said of a person or animal
senses.definitionCN: 身体大而结实，用于人或动物
senses.example: A massive guard stood at the gate all night.
senses.exampleCN: 一名魁梧的守卫整夜站在门口。
senses.why: A body can have the same solid bulk as a stone block, and English applies the word to people.
senses.whyCN: 身体可以有和石块一样厚实的体量，英语便把这个词用在人身上。

senses.title: Formed as one unbroken rock body
senses.definition: in geology, said of rock that has no visible bedding or layering, appearing as one solid mass
senses.definitionCN: 地质学中用于看不出层理、呈一整块的岩石
senses.example: The cliff is cut into massive granite with no clear layers.
senses.exampleCN: 这面崖壁由无明显层理的整块花岗岩构成。
senses.why: Geology uses the word for rock that behaves as a single lump rather than as stacked sheets.
senses.whyCN: 地质学用这个词指表现得像一整块、而不是叠层薄片的岩石。

senses.title: Very extensive in medicine
senses.definition: said of a bleed, clot or infarct that covers a large part of an organ
senses.definitionCN: 用于覆盖器官很大一部分的出血、血栓或梗死
senses.example: He survived a massive heart attack last winter.
senses.exampleCN: 去年冬天他挺过了一次大面积心肌梗死。
senses.why: Clinical language measures lesions by extent, and an extent near the whole organ is massive.
senses.whyCN: 临床按范围量度病灶，范围接近整个器官的就称为「大面积」。

senses.title: Thick and plain in construction
senses.definition: built with heavy walls and simple, undecorated forms, often of stone
senses.definitionCN: 以厚重墙体与简洁无装饰的形式建造，常用石材
senses.example: The cathedral's massive walls were built to last centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 这座主教座堂的厚重墙体是为挺过数百年而建的。
senses.why: Architecture judges weight and simplicity together, and a building that shows its mass is called massive.
senses.whyCN: 建筑把重量与简洁一起评价，一座显露自身质量的建筑就被称为「厚重」。

intro.en: Massive comes from Latin massa 'lump, mass', itself from Greek maza 'barley cake', through French massif. English adopted it in the sixteenth century, and geology, medicine and architecture later gave it precise uses.
intro.cn: massive 来自拉丁 massa「团块、一堆」，后者源于希腊 maza「大麦饼」，经法语 massif 进入英语，十六世纪被采用；地质、医学与建筑后来赋予它精确用法。

items.en: Maza named a kneaded barley cake, a single shapeless lump of dough, and the image of one solid mass began there.
items.cn: maza 指揉成的大麦饼，是一团没有形状的面团，「一整块实体」的画面由此开始。

items.en: Massa meant a lump, a mass or a body of material, and it also gave English mass.
items.cn: massa 意为团块、一堆或一团材料，也给出英语的 mass。

items.en: French massif described something solid and bulky, and English took the adjective in that form.
items.cn: 法语 massif 形容坚实而笨重的东西，英语照这个形式引入形容词。

items.en: English massive first described heavy objects and bodies, then extended to amounts and effects.
items.cn: 英语的这个词先形容沉重的物体与身体，后扩展到数量与后果。

items.en: Geology uses massive for rock without bedding, and architecture for walls that display their weight.
items.cn: 地质学用这个词指无层理的岩石，建筑用指显露自身重量的墙。

items.en: Clinical writing measures an infarct or bleed by how much of an organ it covers, and a very large one is massive.
items.cn: 临床文字按覆盖器官的多少来量度梗死或出血，覆盖很大的就称为大面积。

note.en: The first group shares the lump stem; the second group holds size words that differ in scale, shape or tone.
note.cn: 第一组共享「团块」词干；第二组是表示大小的词，在规模、形状或语气上各有不同。

entries.definition: A quantity of matter, or a large number of people; the noun behind the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 一定量的物质，或一大群人；是形容词背后的名词。

entries.definition: To an enormous degree; it often modifies verbs such as increase or build.
entries.definitionCN: 达到巨大程度；常修饰「增加」「建造」一类动词。

entries.definition: The quality of being huge and heavy; a state noun used in description.
entries.definitionCN: 巨大而沉重的性质；是用于描写的状态名词。

entries.definition: The arrangement of volumes in a building; an architectural term from the same stem.
entries.definitionCN: 建筑中各体量的组合；同一词干来的建筑术语。

entries.definition: Very big; the general word, without the suggestion of solid weight.
entries.definitionCN: 非常大；通用词，不带「坚实沉重」的暗示。

entries.definition: Extremely large; it stresses scale beyond expectation rather than mass.
entries.definitionCN: 极大；强调超出预期的规模，而非质量。

entries.definition: Large and awkward to move because of shape; it adds inconvenience to size.
entries.definitionCN: 因形状而大得难以搬动；在「大」之外多了不便。

entries.definition: Astonishingly large, as a giant statue; it carries awe rather than weight.
entries.definitionCN: 大到惊人，如巨型雕像；带惊叹意味，而非重量感。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real derivatives and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实派生词与真实固定搭配，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The root means a lump: massive things come as one solid block.
normal.cn: 词根意为「团块」：巨大的东西是一整块实心的。

normal.en: The family runs mass, massively, massiveness and massing.
normal.cn: 同族词包括团块、巨大地、巨大、体量组合。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark quantity and severity: massive amount, massive damage.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出数量与严重程度：大量、严重破坏。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark science: massive rock, massive heart attack.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出科学用法：块状岩体、大面积心肌梗死。

normal.en: Its neighbours differ: huge is general, bulky adds awkwardness, colossal adds awe.
normal.cn: 近邻有别：huge 是通用词，bulky 多了笨重，colossal 多了惊叹。

abstract.en: Picture a single stone so large that a road bends around it.
abstract.cn: 想象一块大到公路要绕着走的石头。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd so thick that no one can cross it.
abstract.cn: 想象一群人多到没人能穿过去。

abstract.en: Picture a door whose frame alone weighs more than a car.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门，光是门框就比一辆车重。

examples.en: The company made a massive investment in new machinery.
examples.cn: 这家公司在新机器上投入了巨额资金。

examples.en: A massive storm shut down every ferry in the region.
examples.cn: 一场猛烈的风暴让该地区所有渡轮停运。

examples.en: The cathedral's massive walls have stood for six hundred years.
examples.cn: 这座主教座堂厚重的墙已经立了六百年。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马四伏」——四匹马伏在一起才拉得动，形容巨大沉重

root: 希腊 maza「大麦饼、一团面团」→ 拉丁 massa「团块」→ 法语 massif → 英语 massive；同族 mass、massif、massing。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe one solid bulk: an object in space, weight in the hand, a growing quantity, the scale of damage, a body, a rock body, a lesion, or a wall.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在描述同一团实在的体量：空间里的物体、手里的重量、不断增大的数量、破坏的规模、身体、岩体、病灶，或一堵墙。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one shapeless lump so big that it dominates whatever stands beside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一大团没有形状的实体，大到让它旁边的一切都显得渺小。

branches.en: THE PHYSICAL BASE: a large object and its solid weight.
branches.cn: 物理基础：庞大的物体与其坚实的重量。

branches.en: THE QUANTITATIVE FORM: a heap of data, money or people.
branches.cn: 数量形态：一堆数据、金钱或人。

branches.en: THE SEVERITY FORM: damage on a scale that is hard to repair.
branches.cn: 严重形态：难以修复的大规模破坏。

branches.en: THE HUMAN FORM: a broad, heavy body.
branches.cn: 人的形态：宽厚沉重的身体。

branches.en: THE TECHNICAL FORMS: rock without bedding, a lesion covering much of an organ, and walls that show their weight.
branches.cn: 技术形态：无层理的岩体、覆盖器官大部的病灶，以及显露重量的墙。

intro.en: Massive rests on Latin massa 'lump' and the adjective ending -ive; English adds endings for manner, state and architectural arrangement.
intro.cn: massive 建立在拉丁 massa「团块」与形容词词尾 -ive 之上；英语再加表示方式、状态与建筑组合的词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin massa 'lump' gives English mass directly; Medieval Latin massivus and French massif give the adjective massive.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 massa「团块」直接给出英语 mass；中世纪拉丁 massivus 与法语 massif 给出形容词 massive。

items.example: The noun is the origin of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是词族的来源。

items.meaning: a body of matter; a great number
items.example: The noun kept both the physical and social senses.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词同时保留物理与社会两义。

items.example: The ending makes a describing word of the noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把名词变成描述词。

items.example: The medieval form passed through French.
items.exampleCN: 这个中世纪形式经法语传下。

items.example: English extended it to amounts and severity.
items.exampleCN: 英语把它扩展到数量与严重程度。

items.example: The suffix gives the degree adverb.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀给出程度副词。

items.example: The suffix names the quality of bulk.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀命名「体量巨大」的性质。

items.example: The noun names a geological mass of rock.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词命名地质上的岩块。

items.example: The ending builds the architectural term massing.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀造出建筑术语「体量组合」。

items.example: The adverb modifies verbs of growth and spending.
items.exampleCN: 这个副词修饰「增长」「开支」类动词。

derivatives.zh: 直接来自拉丁 massa，义为「团块；大量」
由该形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「巨大地」
由该形容词加性质名词后缀构成，义为「巨大」
由词根加动作名词后缀构成，义为「体量组合」
由同一词根经法语进入英语，义为「山块」

definition_zh: 军事的；军队的；军用的；军人式的；军队；军方
definition_en: relating to soldiers, armed forces, or war; also, as a noun, the armed forces of a country taken as one body
core_image: 一队士兵踏着同一节奏行进，枪挎在肩，靴底压过碎石
scene: 天刚亮，一队士兵沿着山口悄悄行进，靴底踩得碎石作响。 At dawn the military column moved through the pass without a sound, rifles slung and boots crunching on the gravel.
sceneCN: 这里 military 是「军事的、军队的」（第 1 个义项：属于军队或战争的）；句意：黎明时分，这支军队的队伍悄无声息地穿过山口，枪挎在肩上，靴子踩得碎石作响。场景要点：天刚亮、狭窄山口、成列行进的士兵、肩上的步枪、碎石上传来的靴声；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 军事的；军队的；军用的；军人式的
军队；军方（与定冠词连用，the military）

collocations.zh: 军队；军方（作为一个整体）

senses.title: Of soldiers and war
senses.definition: relating to soldiers, armies, or the conduct of war in general
senses.definitionCN: 与士兵、军队或战争行为有关的
senses.example: The museum's new wing is devoted to military history.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆的新展区专门展示军事史。
senses.why: Latin militaris was simply the adjective of miles, 'soldier'. Anything it described belonged to the soldier's world, and that broad belonging is still the first sense in English.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 militaris 就是 miles（士兵）的形容词。它修饰的任何东西都属于士兵的世界，这种宽泛的归属至今仍是英语里的第一个义项。

senses.title: Done by soldiers, for soldiers
senses.titleCN: 由军人执行、供军队使用
senses.definition: carried out by soldiers or intended for the armed forces, rather than merely discussing them
senses.definitionCN: 由军人执行或供武装部队使用的，而不只是谈论军队
senses.example: The old airfield is now used for military training.
senses.exampleCN: 这座旧机场现在用于军事训练。
senses.why: The adjective does not only label a topic; it also marks who acts and who benefits. A military operation is planned and run by soldiers, so the word moves from 'about soldiers' to 'by and for soldiers'.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词不只标注话题，还标明谁在行动、谁在受益。军事行动由军人筹划和执行，于是这个词从“关于士兵”走到“由士兵做、为士兵做”。

senses.title: Soldier-like precision
senses.definition: used figuratively of behaviour that is as exact, orderly, and disciplined as a soldier's
senses.definitionCN: 比喻像军人一样精确、整齐、守纪律的行为
senses.example: She folded the map with military precision and handed it back.
senses.exampleCN: 她以军人般的精确折好地图，递了回去。
senses.why: Soldiers drill until every movement is measured and repeated. The adjective borrows that drilled exactness and lends it to civilian actions that have nothing to do with armies.
senses.whyCN: 士兵反复操练，直到每个动作都被量得准确、重复得整齐。这个形容词借来那种操练出来的精确，借给与军队无关的日常动作。

senses.title: By force, not by talk
senses.definition: describing a solution or spirit that relies on armed force or favours it
senses.definitionCN: 形容依靠武力或崇尚武力的解决办法与精神
senses.example: The dispute was settled by military means after talks failed.
senses.exampleCN: 谈判失败后，这场争端以军事手段解决。
senses.why: If the soldier's instrument is force, then calling a solution military announces that force will be used. The adjective shifts from describing an institution to recommending its method.
senses.whyCN: 如果士兵的工具是武力，那么把一个解决办法称为军事的，就是在宣告将动用武力。这个形容词从描述一种机构，转为推荐它的手段。

senses.title: The whole body of soldiers
senses.definition: with the definite article, the armed forces of a country considered as one collective body
senses.definitionCN: 与定冠词连用，指一国的武装力量整体
senses.example: The military were called in to clear the roads after the flood.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水过后，军队被调来清理道路。
senses.why: The adjective became a noun by taking 'the': the military, short for the military forces. A collective noun names all the soldiers as one thing, just as the column in the core image moves as one body.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词加上定冠词就变成了名词：“the military”，是“the military forces”的省略。集合名词把所有士兵命名成一个东西，正如核心意象里的队伍作为一个整体移动。

senses.title: The military as a power bloc
senses.titleCN: 军方：作为政治权力机构
senses.definition: the armed forces viewed as an institution that can act in politics and hold power
senses.definitionCN: 把武装部队看作能够在政治中行动、掌握权力的机构
senses.example: The military seized power overnight and closed the parliament.
senses.exampleCN: 军方一夜之间夺取政权，并关闭了议会。
senses.why: Once the column of soldiers acts as a single actor in public life, 'the military' stops meaning a crowd of men and starts meaning an institution with its own will and weight.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这支队伍在公共生活中作为一个单一行动者行事，the military 就不再指一群士兵，而开始指一个有自己的意志与分量的机构。

senses.title: One soldier, old-fashioned
senses.definition: in older usage, a soldier or a military man, countable and now rare
senses.definitionCN: 旧时用法，指一名军人或军事人员，可数，现已罕见
senses.example: The old novel describes a retired officer simply as 'a military'.
senses.exampleCN: 那本旧小说把一名退役军官径称为“一名军人”。
senses.why: The noun first named one person, 'a military man' (1736), before it named the whole body. The singular use survives only as an archaism, a fossil of the earlier step.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词先指一个人，即“a military man”（1736 年），后来才指整个群体。单数用法只作为古语残存下来，是较早那一步的化石。

senses.title: Service in the ranks
senses.definition: in phrases such as 'in the military', the state or career of serving in the armed forces
senses.definitionCN: 在“in the military”一类短语中，指在武装部队中服役的状态或经历
senses.example: He spent six years in the military before returning to the farm.
senses.exampleCN: 他服役六年，之后回到农场。
senses.why: To be in the military is to stand inside that collective body. The core image of a formed column becomes a place a person can enter, belong to, and leave.
senses.whyCN: 身处军队，就是站进那个集体之中。核心意象里列队成形的队伍，变成了一个人可以进入、归属并离开的地方。

senses.title: A field of study
senses.definition: used attributively to name an academic field whose subject is armies, wars, and defence
senses.definitionCN: 作定语，命名以军队、战争与防务为对象的学科领域
senses.example: She teaches military history at the war college.
senses.exampleCN: 她在军事学院教授军事史。
senses.why: The same adjective that marks soldiers' business can mark the study of that business. The object of the field is still the column, only now it is observed from a desk instead of a trench.
senses.whyCN: 标记士兵事务的同一个形容词，也可以标记对这一事务的研究。这个领域的对象仍是那支队伍，只是现在是从书桌前观察，而不是从战壕里。

intro.en: Military is a Latin adjective that English borrowed through French in the fifteenth century; the collective noun arrived three centuries later, and the origin of the Latin base is still unsettled. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: military 是 15 世纪经法语借入英语的拉丁语形容词；集合名词要晚三百年才出现，而拉丁语词根的来历至今没有定论。年代为大致估计。

items.en: First recorded in English as militari, 'pertaining to or befitting soldiers; used, done, or brought about by soldiers'. It came from Old French militaire (14c.) and directly from Latin militaris.
items.cn: 英语最早记录为 militari，意为“与士兵有关或适合士兵的；由士兵使用、完成或造成的”。它来自古法语 militaire（14 世纪），并直接来自拉丁语 militaris。

items.en: Latin militaris meant 'of soldiers or war, of military service, warlike'. It was formed from miles (genitive militis), 'soldier', a word of unknown origin.
items.cn: 拉丁语 militaris 意为“士兵的、战争的、兵役的、尚武的”。它由 miles（属格 militis）“士兵”构成，而这个词的来历不明。

items.en: The origin of miles is unsettled. It may be Etruscan, or it may mean 'one who marches in a troop', which would connect it to Sanskrit melah 'assembly' and Greek homilos 'assembled crowd'. De Vaan finds it tempting to link it to milia 'thousands', hence *mili-it- 'who goes with the thousand'. None of these is proved.
items.cn: miles 的来历没有定论。它可能来自伊特鲁里亚语，也可能意为“随队伍行进的人”，从而与梵语 melah“集会”、希腊语 homilos“聚集的人群”相联系。De Vaan 认为把它与 milia“数千”联系起来很诱人，即 *mili-it-“随千人同行的人”。这些说法都未被证明。

items.en: The noun first meant 'a military man' (1736). 'Soldiers generally' is recorded from 1757, and it is commonly used only with the definite article.
items.cn: 名词最初意为“军人”（1736）。泛指“士兵、军队”的用法记录于 1757 年，而且通常只与定冠词连用。

items.en: The adjective spreads into fixed phrases: military age, the age at which one becomes liable for service (1737); military police (1827); and military-industrial complex, coined in Eisenhower's farewell speech (1961).
items.cn: 这个形容词扩散到固定短语中：military age 指应服兵役的年龄（1737）；military police 即军事警察（1827）；military-industrial complex 即军工复合体，由艾森豪威尔在告别演说中铸成（1961）。

items.en: Militia is a separate borrowing: 1580s, 'system of military discipline', from Latin militia 'military service', and only from the 1690s 'citizen army'. Militarism (1841) came from French militarisme. Military is the adjective, militia the citizen body, militarism the ideology.
items.cn: militia 是另一次借入：16 世纪 80 年代指“军事训练制度”，来自拉丁语 militia“兵役”，到 17 世纪 90 年代才指“公民军队”。militarism（1841）来自法语 militarisme。military 是形容词，militia 是公民武装，militarism 是主义。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin miles stem but has drifted into different jobs; the second compares the ordinary words for organized fighters.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语 miles 词干，却各自漂向不同的职责；第二组比较表示有组织武装人员的常用词。

entries.definition: a body of citizens enrolled for military service in an emergency, not professional soldiers. It is a force, while military is the adjective of the professional institution.
entries.definitionCN: 紧急时征召服役的公民队伍，不是职业军人。它是一支力量，而 military 是职业军队的形容词。

entries.definition: willing to use strong or violent action for a cause, or a person who is. It describes a stance or a person, never an army as a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 愿意为某项事业采取强硬或暴力行动的，或指这样的人。它描述一种立场或一个人，从不指整支军队。

entries.definition: the belief that a country should keep a strong military and use it aggressively. It names a doctrine, not the forces themselves.
entries.definitionCN: 认为国家应保持强大军力并积极使用武力的信念。它命名一种主义，而不是军队本身。

entries.definition: organized and armed like an army but outside the official armed forces. The prefix para- 'beside' marks the difference from regular military bodies.
entries.definitionCN: 组织与武装像军队、却处于正规武装力量之外的。前缀 para-“在旁”标出它与正规军事组织的区别。

entries.definition: the branch of a country's forces that fights on land, or a large body of soldiers. It is one service, while the military can mean all services together.
entries.definitionCN: 一国武装力量中在陆地作战的分支，或一大群士兵。它是一个军种，而 the military 可指所有军种的整体。

entries.definition: the combined military forces of a country, including army, navy, and air force. It is the full official phrase for what 'the military' names in one word.
entries.definitionCN: 一国武装力量的总和，包括陆军、海军与空军。它是对 the military 一词所指对象的完整正式说法。

entries.definition: soldiers, especially those serving in a particular place or operation. It counts people, while the military names an institution.
entries.definitionCN: 士兵，尤指在某一地点或行动中服役的人。它数的是人，而 the military 命名的是一种机构。

entries.definition: organized groups of soldiers, often qualified as land, air, or naval forces. It is a flexible plural, close to 'the military' but usually needs a qualifier.
entries.definitionCN: 有组织的军人群体，常以陆地、空中或海上限定。它是灵活的复数，接近 the military，但通常需要限定语。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: Latin miles 'soldier', its adjective militaris, the -ary ending, and the separate but related borrowings militia and militarism.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：拉丁语 miles“士兵”、它的形容词 militaris、后缀 -ary，以及另行借入但相关的 militia 与 militarism。

normal.en: miles is Latin for 'soldier'; militaris is its adjective. Military begins as nothing more than 'of the soldier'.
normal.cn: miles 是拉丁语的“士兵”，militaris 是它的形容词。military 最初不过是“士兵的”。

normal.en: The adjective came first, in the fifteenth century; the noun 'the military' for soldiers as a body is recorded only in 1757.
normal.cn: 形容词先出现，在 15 世纪；把士兵作为整体来称的 the military 直到 1757 年才有记录。

normal.en: The -ary ending makes an adjective, so military, militarily, militarism and militarize all grow from the same stem with different endings.
normal.cn: -ary 结尾使它成为形容词，所以 military、militarily、militarism、militarize 都从同一词干加上不同词尾长出来。

normal.en: militia is a separate borrowing from Latin militia 'military service'; its 'citizen army' sense is only from the 1690s.
normal.cn: militia 是从拉丁语 militia“兵役”另行借入的词；它的“公民军队”义要到 17 世纪 90 年代才出现。

normal.en: The definite article matters: the military is the whole body, while a military is an old-fashioned way to say one soldier.
normal.cn: 定冠词很关键：the military 指整个军队，而 a military 是旧式说法，指一名军人。

abstract.en: Picture a column of boots striking gravel at the same instant. The sound is not many sounds but one sound repeated, and that is what makes it military.
abstract.cn: 想象一列靴子在同一瞬间踏在碎石上。那声音不是许多声音，而是一个声音的重复，正是这种重复使它成为“军事的”。

abstract.en: The adjective is a uniform that can be put on anything: a bridge, a budget, a history, a way of folding a map.
abstract.cn: 这个形容词是一套可以套在任何东西上的制服：一座桥、一份预算、一段历史、一种折地图的方式。

abstract.en: When the column stops marching and starts deciding, it becomes 'the military' — one actor with a will, not a crowd of men.
abstract.cn: 当这支队伍停止行进、开始作决定，它就变成了“军方”——一个有意愿的行动者，而不是一群士兵。

examples.en: Military spending rose for the third year in a row.
examples.cn: 军费开支连续第三年上升。

examples.en: The airfield is still under military control, and no civilian flights are allowed.
examples.cn: 这座机场仍处于军事管制之下，不允许民用航班起降。

examples.en: After the earthquake, the military was sent in to reopen the mountain roads.
examples.cn: 地震之后，军队被派去重新打通山路。

dict_mnemonic.text: “米里特力”——米里藏着一群特别有力气的壮汉，列队扛枪向前 → military 军事的；军队（只借音，不表词源）

root: 源自拉丁语 miles“士兵”的形容词 militaris，核心是“属于士兵与军队的”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of military, all growing from one picture: a body of soldiers moving as a single column, and then acting as a single institution.
sensesIntro.cn: military 的九个义项都长自同一幅画面：一队士兵作为一个整体行进，随后作为一个整体机构行动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a column of soldiers stepping as one body.
core.cn: 核心意象：一队士兵作为一个整体迈步。

branches.en: SOLDIER'S WORLD: the adjective first marks what belongs to soldiers, then what is done by them and for them.
branches.cn: 士兵的世界：这个形容词先标记属于士兵的东西，再标记由士兵做、为士兵做的事。

branches.en: BORROWED QUALITIES: drilled exactness is lent to civilian actions, and the soldier's instrument, force, is lent to solutions.
branches.cn: 借来的品质：操练出的精确被借给日常动作，士兵的工具即武力被借给解决办法。

branches.en: COLLECTIVE AND POLITICAL: 'the military' first names all soldiers as one body, then names that body as a power in politics.
branches.cn: 集体与政治：the military 先把所有士兵命名成一个整体，再把这个整体命名为政治中的一种权力。

branches.en: ONE MAN AND A CAREER: the old singular names a single soldier, while 'in the military' names service inside the body.
branches.cn: 个人与职业：旧式单数指一名军人，而 in the military 指在这个整体内部服役。

branches.en: THE STUDY: the same adjective marks the academic field that observes armies from a desk.
branches.cn: 研究领域：同一个形容词标记从书桌前观察军队的学科。

intro.en: Military is a Latin adjective ending in -ary; the stem milit- also carries -ia, -ism, -ist, -istic, -ize and -ation into English. The prefix para- in paramilitary is Greek, added later.
intro.cn: military 是带 -ary 后缀的拉丁语形容词；词干 milit- 还把 -ia、-ism、-ist、-istic、-ize 与 -ation 带进英语。paramilitary 里的前缀 para- 是后来加上的希腊语成分。

latinIntro.en: Three Latin words sit behind the family: miles 'soldier', its adjective militaris, and militia 'military service'. The origin of miles itself is disputed, so no deeper root can be stated as fact.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词族背后有三个拉丁词：miles“士兵”、它的形容词 militaris，以及 militia“兵役”。miles 本身的来历有争议，因此不能把更深的词根当作事实来陈述。

items.meaningCN: 士兵的；战争的（milit- 士兵 + -ary 形容词后缀）
items.example: The country keeps a large military budget.
items.exampleCN: 这个国家维持着庞大的军事预算。

items.meaning: in a military way; by military means
items.meaningCN: 在军事上；以军事手段（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The region is militarily important but economically poor.
items.exampleCN: 这个地区军事上重要，经济上却贫穷。

items.meaning: the belief in strong armed forces and their use
items.meaningCN: 军国主义；尚武精神（-ism 构成主义）
items.example: The book traces the rise of militarism before the war.
items.exampleCN: 这本书追溯了战前军国主义的兴起。

items.example: The general was widely seen as a militarist.
items.exampleCN: 这位将军被普遍看作军国主义者。

items.meaningCN: 军国主义的；黩武的（-ic 构成形容词）
items.example: The parade had a strongly militaristic tone.
items.exampleCN: 这场阅兵带有强烈的黩武色彩。

items.meaningCN: 使军事化（-ize 构成动词）
items.example: The island was militarized during the crisis.
items.exampleCN: 危机期间，这座岛屿被军事化了。

items.meaningCN: 军事化（-ation 构成过程名词）
items.example: People protested against the militarization of the police.
items.exampleCN: 人们抗议警察的军事化。

items.meaning: a citizen army called out in an emergency
items.meaningCN: 民兵组织；紧急时征召的公民武装（拉丁语“兵役”）
items.example: The local militia guarded the bridge.
items.exampleCN: 当地民兵守卫着那座桥。

items.meaningCN: 好战的；激进分子（-ant 构成形容词或指人）
items.example: A militant wing of the movement rejected the talks.
items.exampleCN: 这场运动的激进一派拒绝了谈判。

items.meaning: to work against something, as evidence or circumstance
items.meaningCN: 妨碍；起不利作用（-ate 构成动词）
items.example: The high cost militates against any quick repair.
items.exampleCN: 高昂的成本不利于任何快速修复。

items.meaning: armed like an army but outside it
items.meaningCN: 准军事的（para- 在旁 + military 军事的）
items.example: A paramilitary group controlled the border road.
items.exampleCN: 一个准军事组织控制着那条边境公路。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 士兵的；战争的（miles 士兵 + -aris 形容词后缀）
士兵（词源不明，可能来自伊特鲁里亚语）
兵役；战争（miles 士兵 + -itia 抽象名词后缀）

definition_zh: 指数的；指数式的；以指数函数表示的；急剧增长的
definition_en: relating to an exponent or an exponential function, or describing a rate of change that keeps multiplying by a fixed factor
core_image: 一条曲线在右端几乎竖直上冲，越走越陡
scene: 一张曲线图上，细线过了某一天后几乎竖直上冲。 The curve shows exponential growth after the first week of the outbreak.
sceneCN: 这里 exponential 指「按指数规律增长，即每过一段就乘上同一个倍数」（第 3 个义项：指数式增长）；句意为疫情第一周之后，曲线呈现指数增长。图中可辨识物件：坐标轴、向上弯的曲线、标尺、图钉。

pos.zh: 指数的；指数式的；急剧增长的
指数函数（数学中作名词用）

forms.label: 比较级（多音节，由前置程度词构成）
最高级（多音节，由前置程度词构成）

senses.title: Relating to an exponent
senses.definition: connected with an exponent, the raised number that shows a power
senses.definitionCN: 与幂指数那个抬高的数有关的
senses.example: The exponential notation places the power above the base.
senses.exampleCN: 指数记法把幂写底数上方。
senses.why: the adjective simply says 'of an exponent', and the base word is the Latin participle for setting something out.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只说「属于指数的」，而它的基词正是那个表示「摆出来」的拉丁分词。

senses.title: Having a variable in the exponent
senses.definition: describing an expression in which the variable appears in the exponent rather than the base
senses.definitionCN: 描述变量出现在指数位置而不是底数位置的表达式
senses.example: An exponential equation cannot be solved by simple factoring.
senses.exampleCN: 指数方程不能靠简单的因式分解来解。
senses.why: what makes such an equation exponential is precisely that the unknown has climbed into the exponent.
senses.whyCN: 这类方程之所以称为指数的，正因为未知数爬到了指数位置上。

senses.title: The exponential function
senses.definition: a function in which a fixed base is raised to a variable power
senses.definitionCN: 以固定底数取变量次幂的函数
senses.example: The exponential describes growth proportional to the current amount.
senses.exampleCN: 指数函数描述与当前数量成正比的增长。
senses.why: the function is named by the piece that varies, the exponent, rather than by the fixed base.
senses.whyCN: 这个函数以变化的那一部分命名，也就是指数，而不是固定的底数。

senses.title: Exponential growth
senses.definition: growth in which the amount keeps being multiplied by the same factor
senses.definitionCN: 每次都用同一个倍数乘上去的增长
senses.example: Bacteria in a warm dish show exponential growth at first.
senses.exampleCN: 温盘里的细菌起初呈指数增长。
senses.why: when each step multiplies by a constant factor, the exponent rises steadily, so the word for the exponent names the pattern.
senses.whyCN: 当每一步都乘上同一个常数倍数时，指数稳步上升，于是指数的名字成了这种模式的名字。

senses.title: Exponential decay
senses.definition: a fall in which the amount keeps being divided by the same factor
senses.definitionCN: 每次都被同一个倍数除下去、不断减少的过程
senses.example: The radioactivity of the sample follows exponential decay.
senses.exampleCN: 样品的放射性遵循指数衰减。
senses.why: decay mirrors growth: the exponent goes down at a steady rate, so the same adjective covers both directions.
senses.whyCN: 衰减是增长的镜像：指数按稳定速率下降，因此同一个形容词覆盖两个方向。

senses.title: The exponential distribution
senses.definition: a probability distribution that describes the waiting time between events occurring at a constant rate
senses.definitionCN: 描述以恒定速率发生的事件之间等待时间的概率分布
senses.example: The waiting times at the call centre fit an exponential distribution.
senses.exampleCN: 呼叫中心的等待时间符合指数分布。
senses.why: the distribution's curve falls away like an exponential decay, so statistics borrowed the adjective for it.
senses.whyCN: 这条分布的曲线像指数衰减一样往下掉，统计因此借用了这个形容词。

senses.title: Exponential smoothing
senses.definition: a forecasting method that gives recent observations exponentially greater weight
senses.definitionCN: 给近期观测值按指数递减的权重、用来预测的方法
senses.example: Exponential smoothing tracks the sales trend without chasing every spike.
senses.exampleCN: 指数平滑能跟踪销售趋势，又不去追每一个尖峰。
senses.why: the weights fall off in an exponential pattern, so the method is named after the shape of its weighting.
senses.whyCN: 权重按指数形态递减，这个方法便以其权重的形状命名。

senses.title: Exponential running time
senses.definition: describing an algorithm whose running time grows exponentially with the size of its input
senses.definitionCN: 描述运行时间随输入规模按指数增长的算法
senses.example: The brute-force search runs in exponential time on large inputs.
senses.exampleCN: 这种穷举搜索在大输入上以指数时间运行。
senses.why: computer science counts steps; when the count doubles with each added item, the growth is exponential.
senses.whyCN: 计算机科学数的是步数；每多一个数据步数就翻倍，这种增长就是指数的。

senses.title: The exponential as a noun
senses.definition: the exponential function itself, used as a noun in mathematics
senses.definitionCN: 数学中直接作名词用的指数函数
senses.example: The exponential turns addition into multiplication.
senses.exampleCN: 指数函数把加法变成乘法。
senses.why: mathematicians routinely drop the word function and let the adjective stand alone as a noun.
senses.whyCN: 数学家习惯省掉「函数」二字，让这个形容词直接当名词用。

intro.en: Exponential is English exponent plus the adjective suffix -al. The base goes back to Latin exponere 'to set forth', and the mathematical use dates from the age of calculus.
intro.cn: exponential 是英语 exponent 加形容词后缀 -al 构成。其基词上溯到拉丁 exponere「摆出来」，数学用法则始于微积分时代。

items.en: Ex- 'out' plus ponere 'to put' gave exponere 'to set out, explain'; the participle exponens became English exponent.
items.cn: ex-「出」加 ponere「放」构成 exponere「摆出来、解释」；分词 exponens 成为英语 exponent。

items.en: Exponent entered English as a noun for an explainer, and only later acquired the mathematical sense of a raised power.
items.cn: exponent 最初以「解释者」的名词身份进入英语，后来才获得「幂指数」的数学义。

items.en: The Latin adjective ending -alis, through French -al, turns a noun into an adjective of relation; exponent plus -al gives exponential.
items.cn: 拉丁形容词词尾 -alis 经法语 -al，把名词变成表示关系的形容词；exponent 加 -al 得 exponential。

items.en: From the late seventeenth and eighteenth centuries the adjective named functions and equations in which the variable sits in the exponent.
items.cn: 从十七世纪末到十八世纪，这个形容词用来指变量位于指数位置的函数与方程。

items.en: During the nineteenth and twentieth centuries the word spread to decay, probability distributions, forecasting and computing, always naming growth or fall by a constant factor.
items.cn: 在十九、二十世纪，这个词扩展到衰变、概率分布、预测与计算，始终指按固定倍数增长或下降。

items.en: The exact first date for each applied sense is approximate; the morphological pieces are fully attested.
items.cn: 每个应用义的确切首见年代都是约数；构词的两个部分则有充分记录。

note.en: The first group shares the exponent stem and is easily misread; the second group names other ways of describing rapid or steady change.
note.cn: 第一组共享 exponent 这个词干，容易被误读；第二组是描述快速或稳定变化的其他说法。

entries.definition: The raised number itself or an advocate; the adjective exponential adds the sense of a pattern of change.
entries.definitionCN: 指那个抬高的数，或指倡导者；形容词 exponential 则加上「变化模式」的意思。

entries.definition: The operation of raising to a power, not the shape of a growth curve.
entries.definitionCN: 指求幂这个运算，而非增长曲线的形状。

entries.definition: From expandere 'to spread out', built on pandere, not ponere: it means wide or open, not growing by a factor.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 expandere「铺开」，词根是 pandere 而非 ponere：意为宽广、开阔，不是按倍数增长。

entries.definition: From expendere 'to weigh out, pay', built on pendere: it means costly, not fast-growing.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 expendere「称出、支付」，词根是 pendere：意为昂贵，不是快速增长。

entries.definition: A rare word meaning able to be explained, from the same exponere; it has nothing to do with growth.
entries.definitionCN: 罕见词，意为「可解释的」，同出 exponere；与增长无关。

entries.definition: Simply fast; it says nothing about the rule by which the amount increases.
entries.definitionCN: 只表示快，不说明数量按什么规则增加。

entries.definition: Describes a sudden burst of growth; exponential describes a steady multiplication that eventually looks like a burst.
entries.definitionCN: 描述突然爆发的增长；exponential 描述一种稳定的倍数增长，最终看起来像爆发。

entries.definition: In growth language, geometric increase also multiplies by a fixed factor; the two terms often coincide, though geometric is the older label.
entries.definitionCN: 在增长语境里，几何增长同样按固定倍数相乘；两个说法常常重合，只是几何一词更老。

entries.definition: Speeding up in general; exponential growth is one specific rule that produces acceleration.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指越来越快；指数增长是产生加速度的一种具体规则。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real suffix, the real family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的后缀、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: Exponent plus -al: the adjective of the raised number, then the name of the curve it produces.
normal.cn: exponent 加 -al：先是指数这个数的形容词，再成为它所画出的曲线的名字。

normal.en: The family runs exponent, exponential, exponentially, exponentiation and exponentiate.
normal.cn: 同族词有 exponent、exponential、exponentially、exponentiation 与 exponentiate。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the applications: exponential growth, exponential decay, exponential distribution.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出应用场景：指数增长、指数衰减、指数分布。

normal.en: Exponential growth doubles, then doubles again; each doubling is short Scotch tape on the same stack.
normal.cn: 指数增长翻一倍，再翻一倍；每次翻倍都是往同一摞上再贴一层。

normal.en: Exponential decay is the same tape being peeled off at a steady fraction each step.
normal.cn: 指数衰减则是每一步都按固定比例撕掉一层同样的胶带。

abstract.en: Picture a curve that looks lazy for a long time, then suddenly stands up on its tail.
abstract.cn: 想象一条曲线长期懒洋洋地躺着，然后突然用尾巴立起来。

abstract.en: Picture a rumour that doubles its listeners every hour, until the room cannot hold them.
abstract.cn: 想象一个传闻每过一小时听众人数就翻倍，直到房间装不下。

abstract.en: Picture a cup of coffee cooling by the same fraction every minute, never quite reaching room temperature.
abstract.cn: 想象一杯咖啡每分钟按同一比例降温，永远差一点才到室温。

examples.en: The number of cases showed exponential growth before the restrictions began.
examples.cn: 限制措施开始前，病例数呈指数增长。

examples.en: The exponential decay of the signal made the far stations inaudible.
examples.cn: 信号的指数衰减让远处的台听不见了。

examples.en: That algorithm is exponential, so it is useless once the list gets long.
examples.cn: 那个算法是指数级的，列表一长就没用了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「往外放」的叠法——一层层往外翻上去 → 指数式的、急剧增长

root: 英语 exponent（指数，源自拉丁 exponens「摆出来的」）+ 形容词后缀 -al。拉丁词根为 exponere = ex-（出）+ ponere（放）。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one shape: a number placed above a base, then the function built from it, then the curve that doubles or halves by a fixed factor, and finally the places where that curve appears in data and machines.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项顺着同一个形状展开：一个数被放到基座上方，然后是由它构成的函数，再是那个按固定倍数翻倍或减半的曲线，最后是这条曲线在数据与机器里出现的地方。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a curve that looks almost flat and then stands up on its tail.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条起初几乎是平的，后来用尾巴立起来的曲线。

branches.en: THE RAISED NUMBER: the adjective belongs to the exponent, and to equations where the unknown sits there.
branches.cn: 抬高的数：这个形容词属于指数，也属于未知数坐在指数位置的方程。

branches.en: THE FUNCTION: the exponential function, whether named in full or shortened to a bare noun.
branches.cn: 函数本身：无论说全称还是缩成一个光秃秃的名词，指的都是指数函数。

branches.en: UP AND DOWN: growth and decay are the same fixed-factor rule running forward or backward.
branches.cn: 上升与下降：增长与衰减是同一条固定倍数规则的正向与反向。

branches.en: MEASURING TIME: waiting times and smoothed forecasts borrow the shape of the decay curve.
branches.cn: 计量时间：等待时间与平滑预测都借用了衰减曲线的形状。

branches.en: TIME THAT EXPLODES: in computing the step count doubles with every added item.
branches.cn: 爆炸的时间：在计算里，每多一个数据，步数就翻倍。

intro.en: Exponential is an English noun plus a Latin adjective suffix, and both parts are still productive.
intro.cn: exponential 是一个英语名词加拉丁形容词后缀构成，两部分至今都能产。

latinIntro.en: The base exponere also gives exponent, expound and expose; the suffix -alis, through French -al, builds adjectives of relation.
latinIntro.cn: 基词 exponere 还衍生 exponent、expound 与 expose；后缀 -alis 经法语 -al 构成表示关系的形容词。

items.example: The prefix puts the number out of the base's body.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把这个数放到基座之外。

items.example: The base verb supplies the placing.
items.exampleCN: 基词提供「放置」这个动作。

items.example: The participle became the noun exponent.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词成了名词 exponent。

items.example: The exponent rides above the base.
items.exampleCN: 指数骑在底数上方。

items.example: The adjective names the curve as well as the number.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词既指数，也指曲线。

items.example: Costs grew exponentially.
items.exampleCN: 成本呈指数增长。

items.meaning: the act of raising to a power
items.example: Exponentiation repeats multiplication.
items.exampleCN: 求幂把乘法重复起来。

items.example: The program exponentiated the matrix.
items.exampleCN: 程序对矩阵取了幂。

items.meaningCN: 表示关系的形容词后缀
items.example: It turns a noun into an adjective of belonging.
items.exampleCN: 它把名词变成表示归属的形容词。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 指数的（近代拉丁构成形式）

definition_zh: 保护的；防护的；保护性的
definition_en: giving protection from harm, damage or loss
core_image: 一双厚手套把易碎的玻璃杯包住，杯壁不再直接受力
scene: 野外摄影师在镜头前又加了一层薄膜。 A thin protective coating keeps the lens from scratching in the field.
sceneCN: 这里 protective 指「起防护作用、使对象免受损伤」（第 1 个义项：在物体表面加一层屏障以抵挡磨损）；句意为野外加的一层薄防护膜使镜片不被刮伤。图中可辨识物件：镜头、透明薄膜、沙砾、相机包；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 保护的；防护的；保护性的

senses.title: Shielding an object from damage
senses.definition: forming a barrier that keeps an object from being scratched, worn or broken
senses.definitionCN: 形成屏障，使物件不被刮伤、磨损或打破
senses.example: A thin protective coating keeps the lens from scratching in the field.
senses.exampleCN: 一层薄防护膜使镜片在野外不被刮伤。
senses.why: -ive marks function: the coating exists in order to protect, whether or not it is currently doing so.
senses.whyCN: -ive 标记功能：这层膜的存在目的就是保护，不论此刻是否正在受力。

senses.title: Careful in guarding people
senses.definition: used of a person who watches over others so closely that it limits their freedom
senses.definitionCN: 形容一个人过度看护他人，以至限制对方自由
senses.example: His protective manner kept his younger brother from making friends.
senses.exampleCN: 他那过度保护的态度让弟弟交不到朋友。
senses.why: Care can become a barrier, so the same adjective covers a parent's vigilance.
senses.whyCN: 照料可以变成屏障，因此同一个形容词也覆盖家长的警觉。

senses.title: Legal measure that keeps someone safe
senses.definition: a court order or legal status that shields a person from harm or harassment
senses.definitionCN: 使某人免受伤害或骚扰的法院命令或法律地位
senses.example: The court issued a protective order after the threat.
senses.exampleCN: 在威胁发生之后，法院发布了保护令。
senses.why: A court order is a legal coating around a person.
senses.whyCN: 法院命令是裹在人身上的一层法律涂层。

senses.title: Coloration that hides or warns
senses.titleCN: 起隐藏或警告作用的体色
senses.definition: used of colours that help an animal avoid detection or advertise a defence
senses.definitionCN: 形容帮助动物避免被发现或通告防御手段的颜色
senses.example: Protective coloration makes the nestlings nearly invisible.
senses.exampleCN: 保护色让雏鸟几乎看不见。
senses.why: Colour is the animal's own coating, grown instead of worn.
senses.whyCN: 体色是动物自带的涂层，长出来而非穿上去。

senses.title: Tariff that shields local industry
senses.definition: used of a tax on imports intended to raise the price of foreign competitors
senses.definitionCN: 形容旨在提高外国竞争者价格的进口税
senses.example: The protective tariff kept the mill open for another decade.
senses.exampleCN: 保护性关税让这家工厂又开了十年。
senses.why: A tariff is a wall placed around a domestic market.
senses.whyCN: 关税是围在国内市场外的一道墙。

senses.title: Custody for a person's safety
senses.definition: used of detention intended to keep a person from harm rather than to punish
senses.definitionCN: 形容旨在使某人免受伤害而非惩罚的拘留
senses.example: The witness was held in protective custody overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 那名证人被以保护性拘留关押了一夜。
senses.why: Custody keeps a person inside a legal shield.
senses.whyCN: 拘留把一个人留在法律盾牌之内。

senses.title: Factor that reduces risk
senses.definition: used of a condition or habit that lowers the chance of a bad outcome
senses.definitionCN: 形容降低不良结果几率的条件或习惯
senses.example: Regular sleep is a protective factor for adolescent mental health.
senses.exampleCN: 规律睡眠是青少年心理健康的保护因素。
senses.why: A habit acts before the harm, which is what a protective layer does.
senses.whyCN: 习惯在伤害之前起作用，这正是防护层的作用。

senses.title: Instinct to guard the young
senses.definition: used of an animal's instinctive readiness to defend its offspring
senses.definitionCN: 形容动物保护后代的本能反应
senses.example: The mother bear's protective instinct made the trail impassable.
senses.exampleCN: 母熊的护幼本能让那条小路无法通行。
senses.why: The instinct puts the parent's body between the danger and the young.
senses.whyCN: 本能把亲本的身体放在危险与幼体之间。

intro.en: Protective comes from protect, from Latin protegere 'to cover in front', built on pro- 'before' and tegere 'to cover'. The adjective protectivus is late Latin; English protective appears in the sixteenth century.
intro.cn: protective 来自 protect，后者出自拉丁 protegere「在前面遮盖」，由 pro-「在前」与 tegere「覆盖」构成。形容词 protectivus 为晚期拉丁；英语 protective 于 16 世纪出现。

items.en: Tegere 'to cover' supplies the core image of a roof or shield placed over something.
items.cn: tegere「覆盖」提供核心意象：把屋顶或盾牌置于某物之上。

items.en: Protegere joined pro- 'in front' to tegere, giving 'to cover in front, to shield'.
items.cn: protegere 把 pro-「在前」与 tegere 结合，意为「在前面遮盖、屏蔽」。

items.en: The noun protectio 'a covering, protection' supplied the action noun behind protect and protection.
items.cn: 名词 protectio「遮盖、保护」提供了 protect 与 protection 背后的动作名词。

items.en: French protectif carried the adjective into English, where protective is recorded from the 1500s.
items.cn: 法语 protectif 把这个形容词带入英语，protective 自 16 世纪有记录。

items.en: Protective tariff and protective custody are eighteenth- and nineteenth-century specializations.
items.cn: 保护性关税与保护性拘留是 18、19 世纪的特化用法。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the exact first English use of protective is unrecorded and the sixteenth-century date is approximate. The Latin protegere and tegere layers are secure.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：protective 的最早英语使用无记录，16 世纪之数为约数；拉丁 protegere 与 tegere 这两层可靠。

note.en: Group one separates the adjective from the verb, noun and adverb of the family; group two separates kinds of shielding by purpose.
note.cn: 第一组区分该形容词与同族动词、名词、副词；第二组按目的区分各类屏蔽。

entries.definition: The state or act of being protected; protective describes what provides it.
entries.definitionCN: 指被保护的状态或行为；protective 描述提供保护的事物。

entries.definition: A person or device that protects; protective is a quality, not an agent.
entries.definitionCN: 指起保护作用的人或装置；protective 是性质，不是施动者。

entries.definition: In a protecting manner; it modifies a verb rather than describing a thing.
entries.definitionCN: 指以保护的方式；修饰动词，而非描述事物。

entries.definition: The tendency to protect; the adjective describes, the noun names the trait.
entries.definitionCN: 指保护倾向；形容词描述，名词命名特质。

entries.definition: Oriented against an attack; protective need not imply any attacker.
entries.definitionCN: 指针对攻击的取向；protective 不一定暗示攻击者。

entries.definition: Acting before harm occurs; protective describes the barrier, preventive the timing.
entries.definitionCN: 指在伤害发生前行动；protective 描述屏障，preventive 描述时机。

entries.definition: Providing cover or refuge; protective is broader and includes coatings and laws.
entries.definitionCN: 指提供遮蔽或庇护；protective 更宽，包含涂层与法律。

entries.definition: The ongoing activity of keeping someone safe; protective is the quality of the measure.
entries.definitionCN: 指持续使某人安全的行动；protective 是措施的性质。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real pro- plus tegere structure, the real family, and the fixed phrases for clothing, law, trade and health.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的 pro- 加 tegere 结构、真实词族，以及衣物、法律、贸易与健康领域的固定搭配。

normal.en: pro- 'in front' + tegere 'cover' + -ive: tending to cover in front.
normal.cn: pro-「在前」+ tegere「覆盖」+ -ive：倾向于在前面遮盖。

normal.en: The family runs protect, protection, protective, protector, protectively.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 protect、protection、protective、protector、protectively。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: protective clothing, protective coating, protective order.
normal.cn: 固定搭配有 protective clothing、protective coating、protective order。

normal.en: The same adjective serves gloves, laws, tariffs and instincts.
normal.cn: 同一个形容词可用于手套、法律、关税与本能。

normal.en: Compare protection, the noun, and protector, the agent.
normal.cn: 比较名词 protection 与施动者 protector。

abstract.en: Picture thick gloves closed around a glass that must not break.
abstract.cn: 想象厚手套包住一只绝不能破的玻璃杯。

abstract.en: Picture a transparent film taking every scratch that the lens would have taken.
abstract.cn: 想象一层透明膜替镜片承受了每一道刮痕。

abstract.en: Picture a parent standing one step too close to a child's every decision.
abstract.cn: 想象一位家长站得离孩子的每个决定都太近。

examples.en: Workers wore protective masks around the solvent.
examples.cn: 工人在溶剂旁戴着防护口罩。

examples.en: The law provides protective measures for witnesses.
examples.cn: 法律为证人提供保护措施。

examples.en: Protective coloration kept the eggs hidden from above.
examples.cn: 保护色使这些卵从上方看不被发现。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「protect（保护）+ -ive（性质）」——带着保护性质的 → 防护的；保护性的

root: 拉丁 pro-「在前」+ tegere「覆盖」→ protegere「在前面遮盖」→ 晚期拉丁 protectivus → 法语 protectif → 英语 protective。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one covering: a film over a lens, a parent over a child, a court over a witness, colour over a nest, a tariff over a mill, custody over a witness, a habit over health, and an instinct over cubs.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享同一层覆盖：薄膜覆镜片、家长护孩子、法院护证人、体色护巢、关税护工厂、拘留护证人、习惯护健康、本能护幼崽。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: thick gloves closed around a fragile glass, taking the force instead of it.
core.cn: 核心意象：厚手套包住易碎玻璃，替它承受力量。

chain: THE LAYER IS MADE A RULE

branches.en: PHYSICAL COVER: coatings and body colour absorb damage or hide the young.
branches.cn: 物理覆盖：涂层与体色吸收损伤或藏住幼体。

branches.en: CARE: a person or animal stands between danger and the one guarded.
branches.cn: 看护：人或动物站危险与被护者之间。

branches.en: LAW: orders and custody replace the body with legal walls.
branches.cn: 法律：命令与拘留用法律墙壁替代身体。

branches.en: TRADE: a tariff is a wall around a domestic industry.
branches.cn: 贸易：关税是围住本国产业的一道墙。

branches.en: HEALTH: a habit lowers risk before harm appears.
branches.cn: 健康：习惯在伤害出现前降低风险。

intro.en: Protective is a Latin verb stem plus -ive; the Latin family of protegere supplies the verb, the action noun and the agent.
intro.cn: protective 是拉丁动词词干加 -ive；protegere 的拉丁词族提供动词、动作名词与施动者。

latinIntro.en: Latin protegere, protectio and tectus supply the idea of covering something in front.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 protegere、protectio 与 tectus 提供「在前面覆盖某物」的意思。

items.example: The wall protects the village from wind.
items.exampleCN: 这堵墙保护村庄免受风。

items.example: Protection from rain was the first concern.
items.exampleCN: 首先考虑的是防雨。

items.example: The coating is protective, not decorative.
items.exampleCN: 这层涂层是防护性的，不是装饰性的。

items.example: A surge protector guards the equipment.
items.exampleCN: 浪涌保护器保护设备。

items.example: She stood protectively between them.
items.exampleCN: 她护在两人中间。

items.example: His protectiveness became a burden.
items.exampleCN: 他的过度保护成了负担。

items.example: Protective clothing is required near acid.
items.exampleCN: 在酸附近必须穿防护服。

items.example: The protective tariff raised import prices.
items.exampleCN: 保护性关税抬高了进口价格。

items.example: The child was placed in protective custody.
items.exampleCN: 那名儿童被置于保护性拘留。

definition_zh: 蚊子；蚊虫滋扰；蚊媒疾病的传播者；蚊的幼虫（作定语）；蚊帐等防蚊用品（作定语）；小型舰艇编队（蚊队）；蚊叮的小伤；被当作猎物的小飞虫（如蚊鹰）
definition_en: a small two-winged fly whose female bites and sucks blood, often carrying disease; also used of the nuisance, the diseases it spreads and small craft fleets
core_image: 水面上倒立着一只细腿小虫，口器像一根细针，背后是静止的池水与一圈涟漪
scene: 池塘边，一只蚊子把细长的口器刺进人的前臂。 A mosquito pierces the skin of a sleeper's forearm with its needle-like mouthparts.
sceneCN: 这里 mosquito 指「吸血的小型双翅目昆虫」（第 1 个义项：蚊）；句意为一只蚊子用针状口器刺入睡者前臂的皮肤。可辨识物件：细长口器、透明翅膀、前臂、池水；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 蚊子；蚊虫
蚊的；防蚊用的（作定语）

senses.title: A small blood-sucking fly
senses.titleCN: 蚊子：吸血的小型双翅目昆虫
senses.definition: a small two-winged fly whose female pierces skin and takes blood
senses.definitionCN: 雌虫刺穿皮肤吸血的细小双翅目昆虫
senses.example: A mosquito pierces the skin of a sleeper's forearm with its needle-like mouthparts.
senses.exampleCN: 一只蚊子用针状口器刺入睡者前臂的皮肤。
senses.why: Only the female bites, because she needs blood protein for her eggs; the everyday word still names the whole insect.
senses.whyCN: 只有雌虫叮咬，因为它需要血液中的蛋白质来产卵；日常用词仍指整个虫体。

senses.title: A biting nuisance
senses.definition: mosquitoes treated collectively as an irritating swarm that drives people indoors
senses.definitionCN: 把蚊虫看成一群扰人的飞虫，能把人赶进屋里
senses.example: The mosquitoes drove the whole camp indoors before dusk.
senses.exampleCN: 蚊群还没到黄昏就把整个营地的人赶进了屋。
senses.why: When the plural is used this way, the word names an annoyance rather than a species.
senses.whyCN: 复数这样用时，词指的是扰人的麻烦，而不是某个物种。

senses.title: A disease vector
senses.definition: the insect understood as the carrier that passes malaria, dengue or other infections between people
senses.definitionCN: 被理解为在人与人之间传递疟疾、登革热等感染的媒介昆虫
senses.example: Mosquitoes carry malaria in lowland regions.
senses.exampleCN: 蚊子在低地地区传播疟疾。
senses.why: Public health shifted the emphasis from the bite to the transmission chain, and this sense now dominates medical writing.
senses.whyCN: 公共卫生把重点从叮咬转到传播链，这一义如今在医学写作中占主导。

senses.title: The aquatic young stage
senses.definition: the larval form that hangs at the water surface, usually named in the compound mosquito larva
senses.definitionCN: 倒悬在水面的幼虫，通常以「mosquito larva」这一复合形式出现
senses.example: Mosquito larvae hang head-down just beneath the surface film.
senses.exampleCN: 孑孓头朝下挂在表面水膜之下。
senses.why: The adult name is reused as a modifier for its own young, a common pattern in entomology.
senses.whyCN: 成虫名被复用作自身幼期的修饰语，这是昆虫学中常见的模式。

senses.title: Protective gear against mosquitoes
senses.definition: the equipment named after the insect, such as a mosquito net, coil or repellent
senses.definitionCN: 以这种昆虫命名的防护用品，如蚊帐、蚊香或驱蚊剂
senses.example: A mosquito net over the bed is the cheapest protection.
senses.exampleCN: 床上挂一顶蚊帐是最便宜的防护。
senses.why: The word marks what the object is used against, so the insect name becomes a label for the defence.
senses.whyCN: 这个词标出物件用来对付什么，昆虫名于是成了防护手段的标签。

senses.title: A fleet of small craft
senses.definition: a group of tiny, fast boats or warships, historically called a mosquito fleet
senses.definitionCN: 一群小而快的船或军舰，历史上称作蚊队
senses.example: A mosquito fleet of wooden gunboats patrolled the river.
senses.exampleCN: 一支由木制炮艇组成的蚊队巡弋河面。
senses.why: The metaphor compares small, numerous, stinging craft to a swarm of biting insects.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻把数量多、体量小、能刺痛人的舰艇比作一群叮人的虫。

senses.title: A small irritating wound
senses.definition: the itchy swelling left by a bite, commonly called a mosquito bite
senses.definitionCN: 叮咬留下的发痒肿块，通常说成「mosquito bite」
senses.example: A mosquito bite on his ankle kept him awake.
senses.exampleCN: 脚踝上的蚊叮让他一夜没睡好。
senses.why: Metonymy moves the name from the biter to the mark it leaves, a very common shift in medical everyday speech.
senses.whyCN: 转喻把名字从叮咬者移到留下的痕迹，这是医学口语中极常见的转移。

senses.title: A tiny flying prey
senses.titleCN: 被当作猎物的小飞虫（如蚊鹰）
senses.definition: a small flying insect understood as food for a predator, as in the folk name mosquito hawk
senses.definitionCN: 被看作捕食者食物的小飞虫，如俗称蚊鹰的蜻蜓
senses.example: Children call the dragonfly a mosquito hawk because it catches small flies.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们把蜻蜓叫作蚊鹰，因为它捕食小飞虫。
senses.why: Here mosquito names the prey, and the compound tells what the larger insect feeds on.
senses.whyCN: 此处 mosquito 指猎物，复合词说明那种更大的昆虫吃什么。

intro.en: Mosquito is a Spanish and Portuguese diminutive of mosca 'fly', from Latin musca. English borrowed it in the sixteenth century during exploration of the Americas.
intro.cn: mosquito 是西班牙语与葡萄牙语中 mosca「苍蝇」的指小形式，源自拉丁 musca。英语在 16 世纪探索美洲期间把它借入。

items.en: Latin musca meant 'fly'; its own deeper origin is not settled, and the Indo-European forms sometimes cited for it are reconstructions.
items.cn: 拉丁 musca 意为「苍蝇」；它更深的来源并无定论，偶尔为其引用的印欧形式属重构。

items.en: Spanish and Portuguese added the diminutive suffix -ito to mosca, giving mosquito 'little fly', the form English borrowed.
items.cn: 西班牙语与葡萄牙语给 mosca 加上指小后缀 -ito，构成 mosquito「小苍蝇」，英语借的就是这一形式。

items.en: English recorded mosquito in the late sixteenth century in travel accounts of the Caribbean and South America.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪后期的加勒比与南美游记中记录了 mosquito。

items.en: After the discovery that the insect transmits malaria and yellow fever, the word moved into public health vocabulary in the late nineteenth century.
items.cn: 在发现这种昆虫传播疟疾与黄热病之后，这个词于 19 世纪后期进入公共卫生词汇。

items.en: Both mosquitoes and mosquitos are accepted plurals; the longer form follows the older English habit of doubling the final consonant before -es.
items.cn: mosquitoes 与 mosquitos 两种复数都被接受；较长的一种沿用英语在 -es 前双写末尾辅音的老习惯。

items.en: Source uncertain (detail and first date): the deeper origin and the exact first citation are not settled, so any pre-Latin form offered here is a reconstruction and competing hypotheses are left side by side.
items.cn: 来源不确定（细节与首见年代）：更深的来源与确切最早书证均无定论，此处给出的拉丁语之前形式属重构形式，并列假说一并保留、不作定论。

note.en: Group one collects words that look or sound close but come from other roots; group two collects the small biting flies people mix up with mosquitoes.
note.cn: 第一组收形近音近但来源不同的词；第二组收人们常与蚊子混淆的小型叮咬蝇类。

entries.definition: Mosque comes from Arabic masjid, a place of prostration; the resemblance to mosquito is accidental.
entries.definitionCN: mosque 来自阿拉伯语 masjid，意为叩拜之处；与 mosquito 的相似纯属偶然。

entries.definition: Miskito names a people and a coast of Central America and is spelled with a k; it is not the insect.
entries.definitionCN: Miskito 指中美洲的一个民族与一片海岸，拼写带 k，不是这种昆虫。

entries.definition: This plural is a spelling variant of mosquitoes, not a different word with a different meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 这个复数只是 mosquitoes 的拼写变体，并非意义不同的另一个词。

entries.definition: The compound names the bed net, so the insect word is working as a modifier rather than as the subject.
entries.definitionCN: 这个复合词指床上用的蚊帐，昆虫词在此作修饰语而非主语。

entries.definition: A gnat is a very small biting fly, often a midge; it bites but does not transmit malaria.
entries.definitionCN: gnat 指极小的叮咬蝇，常为蠓；会叮人但不传播疟疾。

entries.definition: A midge is a minute two-winged fly, some species of which bite in swarms near water.
entries.definitionCN: midge 是极小的双翅目蝇，有些种类在水边成群叮人。

entries.definition: Fly is the general name for the order, of which the mosquito is one family.
entries.definitionCN: fly 是这一目的通称，蚊子只是其中一科。

entries.definition: A flea is a wingless jumping insect that bites; it belongs to a different order entirely.
entries.definitionCN: flea 是无翅跳跃的叮咬昆虫，属于完全不同的目。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Spanish mosca 'fly' plus the diminutive -ito gives mosquito, literally 'little fly'.
normal.cn: 西班牙语 mosca「苍蝇」加指小后缀 -ito 构成 mosquito，字面就是「小苍蝇」。

normal.en: The family runs mosquito, mosquitoes, mosquitos, mosquitofish and mosquitocide.
normal.cn: 词族包括 mosquito、mosquitoes、mosquitos、mosquitofish 与 mosquitocide。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: mosquito net, mosquito coil, mosquito-borne disease.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：蚊帐、蚊香、蚊媒疾病。

normal.en: Only the female bites; males feed on nectar.
normal.cn: 只有雌虫叮咬，雄虫吸食花蜜。

normal.en: The larval stage is the wriggler that hangs at the water surface.
normal.cn: 幼虫期就是倒悬在水面的孑孓。

abstract.en: Picture a needle so fine that the sleeper never feels it enter.
abstract.cn: 想象一根细到睡者完全察觉不到的针。

abstract.en: Picture a whole village sleeping under white gauze, one net per bed.
abstract.cn: 想象整个村子睡在白纱之下，每张床一顶帐。

abstract.en: Picture a hundred small boats stinging a harbour like a swarm.
abstract.cn: 想象上百条小船像虫群一样刺痛一座港口。

examples.en: The mosquito net was treated with insecticide and hung over both beds.
examples.cn: 蚊帐经杀虫剂处理，挂在两张床的上方。

examples.en: Mosquitoes breeding in standing water made the drainage project urgent.
examples.cn: 蚊子在积水中繁殖，使排水工程变得紧迫。

examples.en: A mosquito bite on her wrist swelled into a hard red lump.
examples.cn: 她手腕上的蚊叮肿成了一个硬红的包。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「mosquito（莫斯基托）」——在池边「莫」名其妙被叮一口的小虫 → 蚊子

root: 西班牙语/葡萄牙语 mosquito「小苍蝇」= mosca「苍蝇」+ 指小后缀 -ito；mosca 源自拉丁 musca「苍蝇」。拉丁 musca 更早来源不确定，所引印欧形式属重构形式。与 mosque（阿拉伯语 masjid）无关。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses start from the biting insect, spread to the swarm, the disease chain, its water-borne young, the gear used against it, small warships, the mark it leaves and the prey it becomes.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从叮人的昆虫出发，扩展到虫群、疾病链、水中幼期、对付它的器物、小型舰艇、留下的包以及它作为猎物的一面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a needle-thin mouthpart breaking the skin while a gauze net hangs above the bed.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根细如针的口器刺破皮肤，床的上方挂着纱帐。

branches.en: THE BITE: the insect and the itchy mark it leaves are two ends of one act.
branches.cn: 叮咬：昆虫与它留下的痒包是同一动作的两端。

branches.en: THE SWARM: the nuisance and the wriggling young both present the insect in numbers.
branches.cn: 虫群：扰人的成蚊与扭动的幼虫都以数量呈现这种昆虫。

branches.en: TRANSMISSION: the bite becomes a link in a chain between patients.
branches.cn: 传播：叮咬成为病人之间链条上的一环。

branches.en: DEFENCE AND METAPHOR: nets and coils answer the bite, and small fast boats borrow it.
branches.cn: 防护与比喻：蚊帐蚊香回应叮咬，小而快的船借用了它。

branches.en: THE PREY: the name finally marks a food item for a larger hunter.
branches.cn: 猎物：名字最后标出一种更大捕食者的食物。

intro.en: Mosquito is a Spanish diminutive built on a Latin root; its English derivatives are compounds, while the Latin family supplies the technical terms.
intro.cn: mosquito 是在拉丁词根上构成的西班牙语指小词；英语派生词多为复合，技术术语则来自拉丁词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin musca 'fly' gives muscid and musciform in zoology; the Spanish diminutive is the branch that produced the English noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 musca「苍蝇」在动物学中给出 muscid 与 musciform；产生英语名词的是西班牙语指小这一支。

items.example: A mosquito rests on the shaded wall.
items.exampleCN: 一只蚊子在背阴的墙上停歇。

items.example: Mosquitoes breed wherever water stands.
items.exampleCN: 凡有积水处蚊子就能繁殖。

items.meaning: a net hung over a bed
items.example: The mosquito net kept the room quiet at night.
items.exampleCN: 蚊帐让夜里屋里安静下来。

items.example: A mosquito coil smoked in the corner.
items.exampleCN: 角落里点着一盘蚊香。

items.meaning: a substance that keeps the insect off
items.example: The mosquito repellent smelled of lemon grass.
items.exampleCN: 驱蚊剂有柠檬草的味道。

items.meaning: a small fish that eats larvae
items.example: Mosquitofish were introduced to clear the ponds.
items.exampleCN: 人们引入食蚊鱼来清理池塘。

items.meaning: a substance that kills the insect
items.example: The spray is a mosquitocide for drains.
items.exampleCN: 这种喷雾是用于排水沟的灭蚊剂。

items.example: A mosquito hawk hovered over the path.
items.exampleCN: 一只蚊鹰在小径上方悬停。

items.example: Malaria is a mosquito-borne infection.
items.exampleCN: 疟疾是一种蚊媒感染。

definition_zh: 加密；把可读信息转成只有持钥匙者才能还原的编码形式的过程
definition_en: the process of turning readable information into a coded form that only the holder of the key can turn back
core_image: 一封写好的信被锁进铁盒，盒面只剩谁也读不懂的乱码，钥匙挂在大门看守人的腰上
scene: 机房里的灯一直亮着，操作员把钥匙插进读卡器，屏幕上滚过一串谁也读不懂的字符。 Before sending the file, she switched on encryption so that anyone intercepting it would see only random characters.
sceneCN: 这里 encryption 指把可读信息转成密文的过程（第 1 个义项：把明文变成密文的动作）；句意：发送文件之前她开启了加密，中途截获的人只会看到乱码。

pos.zh: 加密；密文化过程；加密方式

derivatives.zh: 加密技术的主张者（罕用）

senses.title: The act of turning plain text into code
senses.titleCN: 把明文变成密文的动作
senses.definition: the act of converting readable information into a coded form by a fixed procedure
senses.definitionCN: 用固定程序把可读信息转换成编码形式的动作
senses.example: Encryption takes place before the message leaves the phone.
senses.exampleCN: 消息离开手机之前就完成了加密。
senses.why: the -tion ending names an action and its result, so the word first denotes the doing of the transformation itself.
senses.whyCN: 词尾表示动作及其结果，因此这个词首先指「做转换」这件事本身。

senses.title: The coded output itself
senses.definition: the unreadable text or data produced by the transformation
senses.definitionCN: 由转换产生、无法直接读懂的文字或数据
senses.example: The intercepted file was pure encryption and told them nothing.
senses.exampleCN: 截获的文件全是密文，他们什么也看不出。
senses.why: the same action noun came to stand for the thing the action leaves behind, the way a building can name the act of building.
senses.whyCN: 同一个动作名词也指动作留下的东西，就像「建筑」既可指建造也可指楼房。

senses.title: The field of study and practice
senses.definition: the branch of cryptography that designs and applies such transformations
senses.definitionCN: 密码学中设计并使用这类转换的分支
senses.example: She teaches encryption alongside authentication and key exchange.
senses.exampleCN: 她把加密与身份认证、密钥交换放在一起讲授。
senses.why: a repeated practice becomes a named discipline, and the action noun is reused for the whole field.
senses.whyCN: 反复进行的实践会变成一个有名目的学科，动作名词就被用来指整个领域。

senses.title: Protection of stored data
senses.definition: the encoding of files or disks so that a lost device does not expose its contents
senses.definitionCN: 对文件或磁盘进行编码，使设备丢失时内容不外泄
senses.example: Full-disk encryption saved the company when a laptop was stolen.
senses.exampleCN: 一台笔记本被盗时，全盘加密救了这家公司。
senses.why: data that sits still has no channel to protect, so the word shifted from sending to keeping.
senses.whyCN: 静止的数据没有传输通道可保护，于是这个词从「发送」转向「保存」。

senses.title: Protection of a live connection
senses.definition: the encoding of traffic while it travels between two parties or devices
senses.definitionCN: 数据在两方或两台设备之间传输时进行的编码
senses.example: The chat app applies encryption to every message in transit.
senses.exampleCN: 这款聊天应用对传输中的每条消息都进行加密。
senses.why: the oldest use of secret writing was to guard a message on the road, and networks repeat that situation exactly.
senses.whyCN: 秘密书写最古老的用途就是在路上保护消息，网络只是原样重演了这个场景。

senses.title: Secret writing in history
senses.definition: the old practice of hiding a written message by substitution or transposition
senses.definitionCN: 用替换或换位把书面消息藏起来的古老做法
senses.example: Court letters relied on encryption long before electric machines.
senses.exampleCN: 早在电气机器出现之前，宫廷信件就依赖密文书写。
senses.why: the modern noun inherits a centuries-old craft, so historical ciphers are still called encryption.
senses.whyCN: 现代名词继承了一门数百年的手艺，因此历史密码也仍被称为加密。

senses.title: The mechanism of key and algorithm
senses.definition: the paired rule and secret value that make the transformation reversible
senses.definitionCN: 使这种转换可以逆转的成对规则与秘密数值
senses.example: Weak encryption here means a short key, not a short message.
senses.exampleCN: 这里说的加密强度不足，指的是密钥太短，而不是消息太短。
senses.why: people speak of the machinery by the name of its effect, so a strong key is praised as strong encryption.
senses.whyCN: 人们习惯用效果之名来指机器本身，于是强密钥被称赞为强加密。

senses.title: Deliberate obscurity of meaning
senses.definition: the figurative use for language made needlessly hard to understand
senses.definitionCN: 转指被人为弄得难以理解的语言
senses.example: The report's encryption of plain facts fooled nobody.
senses.exampleCN: 那份报告把简单事实写得晦涩，谁也没被唬住。
senses.why: coded writing is unreadable by design, and dull prose that hides its meaning borrows the same image.
senses.whyCN: 密文因设计而不可读，故意掩盖意思的晦涩文章便借用了同一个意象。

intro.en: Encryption joins an English prefix and a Greek root: en-, into, plus kryptos, hidden. The noun ending came through Latin. The machine age gave the old idea of secret writing a technical name.
intro.cn: encryption 由英语前缀与希腊词根拼成：en- 表示「进入」，kryptos 表示「隐藏」，名词词尾经拉丁语而来。机器时代给古老的秘密书写取了一个技术名称。

items.en: Greek kryptos meant hidden or covered, from kryptein, to hide. It described a thing put out of sight, not yet a method of writing.
items.cn: 希腊语 kryptos 意为「隐藏的、被遮盖的」，来自动词 kryptein「隐藏」。它描述的是被藏起来的东西，还不是一种书写方法。

items.en: Latin crypta, borrowed from Greek, named a covered vault or underground chamber. English crypt still means such a chamber.
items.cn: 拉丁语 crypta 借自希腊语，指有顶的地下室或拱形地窖。英语 crypt 至今仍指这种地窖。

items.en: English took crypt for a vault and cryptic for something deliberately obscure, keeping the sense of concealment without any computing meaning.
items.cn: 英语以 crypt 指地窖，以 cryptic 指故意晦涩的事物，保留了「藏」的意思，与计算毫无关系。

items.en: The verb encrypt puts en-, into, before the old root, and the noun adds the Latin ending -tion, so the word literally says putting something into hiding.
items.cn: 动词 encrypt 在旧词根前加 en-「进入」，名词再加拉丁词尾 -tion，字面意思就是「把东西放进隐藏状态」。

items.en: From the twentieth century the word settled on mathematical transformation with a key, first in military signalling and later in computing.
items.cn: 二十世纪起，这个词固定指使用密钥的数学变换，先用于军事通信，后来进入计算机领域。

items.en: Source uncertain: the deeper origin of Greek kryptein is not settled, and the older forms sometimes compared with it are reconstructions rather than attested words.
items.cn: 来源不确定：希腊语 kryptein 更早的来源没有定论，常被拿来比较的更古形式属于重构形式，而非有记载的词。

note.en: The first group shares the hidden-root; the second group names neighbouring ways of protecting information.
note.cn: 第一组共享「隐藏」这一词根；第二组是与保护信息相邻的其他说法。

entries.definition: The action itself: to turn readable text into code. Encryption is the name of that action or of its result.
entries.definitionCN: 指动作本身：把可读文本变成代码。encryption 则是这个动作或其结果的名称。

entries.definition: The same root with the reversing prefix: the act of turning the code back into readable form.
entries.definitionCN: 同一词根加表示反向的前缀：把代码还原成可读形式的行为。

entries.definition: Hidden in meaning rather than in code; a cryptic remark puzzles the listener without any cipher.
entries.definitionCN: 指意思难解，而不是被编码；cryptic 的话让人费解，却并没有使用密码。

entries.definition: The old concrete sense of the root: a covered underground room, especially beneath a church.
entries.definitionCN: 词根古老的实体义：有顶的地下室，尤指教堂地下墓室。

entries.definition: Changing data into another representation that anyone with the rule can read; secrecy is not required.
entries.definitionCN: 把数据换成另一种表示，任何人知道规则都能读，并不要求保密。

entries.tag: the old word for the method
entries.definition: A rule for substituting symbols; encryption is the modern technical name for applying such a rule with a key.
entries.definitionCN: 替换符号的规则；encryption 是用密钥执行这类规则的现代技术名称。

entries.definition: Turning data into a fixed-length fingerprint that cannot be turned back; it checks integrity rather than hiding content for later reading.
entries.definitionCN: 把数据变成定长指纹且不可逆，用于校验完整性，而不是隐藏内容供日后阅读。

entries.definition: The broad act of keeping something out of sight; encryption is concealment carried out by a mathematical rule.
entries.definitionCN: 把东西藏起来的泛称；encryption 是用数学规则完成的隐藏。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Greek pieces, the real family and the real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊语构件、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: kryptos means hidden, so encryption is literally a putting-into-hiding.
normal.cn: kryptos 意为「隐藏」，encryption 字面上就是「放进隐藏状态」。

normal.en: The family lines up neatly: encrypt, encrypted, encryption, decryption.
normal.cn: 同族词排列整齐：encrypt、encrypted、encryption、decryption。

normal.en: Fixed phrases locate the word: encryption key, data encryption, end-to-end encryption.
normal.cn: 固定搭配给它定位：加密密钥、数据加密、端到端加密。

normal.en: The ending marks a process noun, like protection and inspection.
normal.cn: 词尾标记过程名词，与 protection、inspection 同类。

normal.en: Encryption hides the message; decryption brings it back with the key.
normal.cn: 加密把消息藏起来，解密用钥匙把它带回来。

abstract.en: Picture a letter locked in a box whose lid is carved with random grooves, and the grooves are the letter.
abstract.cn: 想象一封信锁进盒子，盒盖刻满看似随机的沟槽，而那些沟槽就是信本身。

abstract.en: Picture a key that is also a sentence, and only the reader who knows the sentence can read the door.
abstract.cn: 想象一把钥匙同时也是一句话，只有知道这句话的人才能读懂那扇门。

abstract.en: Picture noise on a wire that is perfectly orderly if you stand at the right end of it.
abstract.cn: 想象线路上的噪声乱作一团，可只要站在正确的一端，它其实井然有序。

examples.en: Modern encryption depends on keys that are hard to guess and easy to replace.
examples.cn: 现代加密依赖难以猜测、又便于更换的密钥。

examples.en: The archive keeps its files under encryption so that a lost disk reveals nothing.
examples.cn: 档案馆把文件加密保存，磁盘丢失也不会泄露内容。

examples.en: Without encryption, a public network is simply a room with no walls.
examples.cn: 没有加密，公共网络就是一间没有墙的房间。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因（en）刻（cry）扑（pt）」——把内容刻进乱码里扑住，就是加密

root: 希腊 kryptos「隐藏的」← kryptein「隐藏」→ 拉丁 crypta「地窖」→ 英语 crypt / cryptic；加前缀 en-「进入」与拉丁词尾 -tion 构成 encryption，二十世纪固定为密钥变换的术语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one line: readable text is put out of sight, then the hidden text, the trade, the stored copy, the travelling message, the old craft, the key mechanism and finally the obscure style.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一条线展开：可读文本先被藏起来，接着是被藏起来的文本、这门行业、静止的副本、传输中的消息、古老手艺、密钥机制，最后是晦涩的文风。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a written sheet locked in a box whose lid carries meaningless grooves, with one key in the world able to open it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张写满字的纸锁在盒里，盒盖刻着无意义的沟槽，世上只有一把钥匙能打开。

branches.en: ACT AND PRODUCT: the doing of the conversion and the unreadable result it leaves behind.
branches.cn: 动作与成品：转换这件事本身，以及它留下的不可读结果。

branches.en: DISCIPLINE AND MECHANISM: the field that studies the method, and the rule-and-key pair that carries it out.
branches.cn: 学科与机制：研究这套方法的领域，以及执行它的规则与密钥。

branches.en: TWO SITUATIONS: data standing still on a disk, and data moving along a connection.
branches.cn: 两种场景：静止在磁盘上的数据，以及沿连接传输中的数据。

branches.en: OLD CRAFT: substitution and transposition by hand, the ancestor of the technical procedure.
branches.cn: 古老手艺：手工的替换与换位，是这套技术程序的前身。

branches.en: FIGURATIVE OBSCURITY: language made hard to read without any cipher at all.
branches.cn: 比喻性的晦涩：并没有使用密码，却把语言写得难以读懂。

intro.en: Encryption is assembled from an English prefix, a Greek root and a Latin noun ending; English later added -ed and -ing forms to the verb.
intro.cn: encryption 由英语前缀、希腊词根与拉丁名词词尾拼成；英语后来又给动词加了 -ed、-ing 形式。

latinIntro.en: The Latin contribution is the ending -tion, from -tionem, which turns an action verb into a noun of action; crypta is a Greek loan in Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的贡献是词尾 -tion（来自 -tionem），把动作动词变成动作名词；crypta 则是拉丁语中的希腊借词。

items.example: The prefix says the message is put into a hidden state.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀表示消息被放进隐藏状态。

items.example: The adjective describes what cannot be seen.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述看不见的东西。

items.example: The verb is the action behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是整个词族背后的动作。

items.example: Latin kept the covered-place sense and passed it to English.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语保留了「有顶之处」的意思，并传给英语。

items.example: The ending makes the verb into a name for a process.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把动词变成过程的名字。

items.example: The verb is the base from which the noun is formed.
items.exampleCN: 动词是构成该名词的基础。

items.example: An encrypted file has already gone through the steps.
items.exampleCN: 已加密的文件已经走完了这些步骤。

items.example: Encrypting names the work while it is being done.
items.exampleCN: encrypting 指正在进行的工作。

items.example: The same root with de- names the way back.
items.exampleCN: 同一词根加 de- 指回去的路。

definition_zh: 考试；检查；审查；诊察；质证
definition_en: a formal test of knowledge, or a careful inspection of something
core_image: 天平中央那根指针：一边放砝码，一边放待称的东西，指针偏转就说明重量。
scene: 考场上，学生翻开试卷，计时器开始走动；同一周里，医生也在给另一位病人做检查。 In the hall a student opens the paper as the timer starts, and that same week a doctor carries out an examination of another patient.
sceneCN: 这里 examination 同时体现「考试」和「医学检查」两个意思（考场用第 1 个义项，身体检查用第 3 个义项）；句意：考场里学生翻开试卷、计时器开始走动；同一周里，医生也在给另一位病人做检查。

pos.zh: 考试；检查；审查；诊察；（法律）质证；检验

senses.title: A formal test
senses.titleCN: 考试：用题目测知识或能力
senses.definition: a formal test of knowledge or ability, usually written or spoken
senses.definitionCN: 对知识或能力的正式测试，通常为笔试或口试
senses.example: The final examination covers everything from the first term.
senses.exampleCN: 期末考试覆盖第一学期以来的全部内容。
senses.why: A test is a weighing: the candidate's knowledge is placed against a fixed standard, and the mark records the difference.
senses.whyCN: 考试就是一次称重：考生的知识被放到固定标准旁，分数记录了两者的差距。

senses.title: Close inspection
senses.definition: a careful look at something in order to find out its condition or details
senses.definitionCN: 为查明状况或细节而仔细查看某物
senses.example: A close examination showed a hairline crack in the frame.
senses.exampleCN: 仔细检查发现框架上有一条细裂缝。
senses.why: The original image is a balance pointer: examination is the act of bringing something under scrutiny so that its hidden weight shows.
senses.whyCN: 原意象是天平的指针：examination 就是把东西放到审视之下，让隐藏的‘重量’显现。

senses.title: Medical examination
senses.titleCN: 医学检查：把身体放到诊断标准下
senses.definition: a physical or clinical check of a patient's body or health
senses.definitionCN: 对病人身体或健康状况进行的体格或临床检查
senses.example: The doctor began the examination with the patient's breathing.
senses.exampleCN: 医生从病人的呼吸开始检查。
senses.why: The body becomes the object weighed against normal signs; the examination looks for what departs from the expected range.
senses.whyCN: 身体成为对照正常体征被称量的对象；检查寻找的是偏离预期范围的部分。

senses.title: Cross-examination
senses.titleCN: 法律质证：用问题检验证词
senses.definition: the questioning of a witness by the opposing side in a legal case
senses.definitionCN: 法律案件中由对方对证人进行的提问与检验
senses.example: Cross-examination exposed a contradiction in the witness's account.
senses.exampleCN: 交叉质证暴露了证人陈述中的矛盾。
senses.why: A witness's story is put on the scale of other evidence; each question tests whether it still balances.
senses.whyCN: 证人的说法被放到其他证据的天平上；每个问题都在检验它是否仍然平衡。

senses.title: Official inquiry
senses.titleCN: 官方审查：对事件与账目立案调查
senses.definition: a formal investigation by an authority into an event or a set of records
senses.definitionCN: 权威机构对事件或记录进行的正式调查
senses.example: The committee's examination of the accounts lasted six months.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会对账目的审查持续了六个月。
senses.why: An authority sets the standard and compels the records to be produced; the examination is the forced comparison.
senses.whyCN: 权威设定标准并强制调取记录；examination 就是这场强制性的对照。

senses.title: Academic scrutiny
senses.titleCN: 学术审查：把论文与证据逐条核对
senses.definition: the critical review of a scholarly claim, text, or body of evidence
senses.definitionCN: 对学术主张、文本或证据体系进行的批判性审查
senses.example: The theory did not survive examination by later researchers.
senses.exampleCN: 该理论没能经受后来研究者的审查。
senses.why: In scholarship the balance is evidence: a claim is examined by asking whether the evidence outweighs the objections.
senses.whyCN: 学术里的天平是证据：审查一个主张，就是问证据是否压过反方意见。

senses.title: Laboratory test
senses.titleCN: 化验：把样本放到仪器里检验
senses.definition: a laboratory procedure that tests a sample for particular substances or conditions
senses.definitionCN: 在实验室检验样本中特定物质或状况的程序
senses.example: Examination of the water sample revealed high lead levels.
senses.exampleCN: 对水样的化验显示铅含量偏高。
senses.why: Here the instrument replaces the human eye; the sample is examined because its contents are not visible without a test.
senses.whyCN: 这里仪器替代了眼睛；样本之所以被检验，是因为不测试就看不见其中的成分。

senses.title: Testing a hypothesis
senses.definition: the process of testing a hypothesis, idea, or method against evidence
senses.definitionCN: 用证据对假设、观点或方法进行检验的过程
senses.example: The proposal came under examination during the trial.
senses.exampleCN: 该方案在试验期间受到了检验。
senses.why: An idea is examined by putting it in a situation where it could fail. Passing the examination is not proof, only survival so far.
senses.whyCN: 检验一个想法，就是把它放进可能失败的处境。通过检验不是证明，只是截至目前还活着。

intro.en: Examination comes from Latin examen, the tongue or pointer of a balance, and examinare, to weigh or test. The weighing image is older than the school sense.
intro.cn: examination 来自拉丁 examen（天平的指针）与 examinare（称量、检验）。‘称重’的意象比‘考试’义更古老。

items.en: The pointer or tongue of a balance, hence a means of weighing. The word names the instrument that reveals weight, not the weight itself.
items.cn: 天平的指针或舌，因而指称量的手段。这个词命名的是显示重量的器具，而不是重量本身。

items.en: To drive out, to demand, to weigh. Many sources connect examen with exigere, but the link is reconstructed rather than directly attested; it is best marked as generally accepted, not certain.
items.cn: 驱出、索取、称量。许多来源把 examen 与 exigere 联系起来，但这是重构而非直接可证的联系；宜标为“一般认为是”，不是确定结论。

items.en: To weigh, test, or examine. The verb extends the balance image to any careful assessment of a thing's value or truth.
items.cn: 称量、检验、审查。该动词把天平意象扩展到对事物价值或真实性的任何仔细评估。

items.en: Old French passed the noun to English. The French form kept both the legal and the scholarly possibilities of the Latin verb.
items.cn: 古法语把该名词传给英语。法语形式同时保留了拉丁动词的法律与学术两种可能。

items.en: English examination is recorded from the 14th century, first in legal and religious inquiry, then in academic testing.
items.cn: 英语 examination 自 14 世纪有记录，先用于法律与宗教调查，后用于学业测试。

items.en: The school examination became fixed in the 19c as public education expanded. Medicine and science kept the older sense of inspecting a body or a sample.
items.cn: 19 世纪公共教育扩张，学校‘考试’义固定下来；医学与科学则保留更古老的‘检查身体或样本’义。

note.en: The first group is the examine family; the second compares kinds of checking, from a scored test to a broad inquiry.
note.cn: 第一组是 examine 词族；第二组比较各种‘检查’，从计分考试到广泛调查。

entries.definition: to inspect or test something carefully. It is the action behind examination.
entries.definitionCN: 仔细检查或检验；是 examination 背后的动作。

entries.definition: a person who sets or marks an examination, or who inspects something officially.
entries.definitionCN: 出题或评卷的人，或进行官方检查的人。

entries.definition: a person who is being examined, especially in a test. The suffix -ee marks the receiver.
entries.definitionCN: 接受考试或检查的人；后缀 -ee 标记接受者。

entries.definition: the informal short form of examination in the school sense. It is not used for medical inspection.
entries.definitionCN: 学校义项中 examination 的非正式缩略；不用于医学检查。

entries.definition: a procedure that measures ability or quality, often with a score. It is the everyday word for a school examination.
entries.definitionCN: 测量能力或质量的程序，常带分数；是学校考试的日常用词。

entries.definition: an official or careful look at something to check its condition. It stresses seeing rather than questioning.
entries.definitionCN: 为核查状况而进行的官方或仔细查看；强调‘看’，而非‘问’。

entries.definition: a judgement of quality, ability, or risk. It is broader than a single examination.
entries.definitionCN: 对质量、能力或风险的判断；比单次考试更宽泛。

entries.definition: a formal or systematic investigation into a question. It emphasizes seeking facts, not grading.
entries.definitionCN: 对某个问题的正式或系统调查；强调寻找事实，而非评分。

entries.definition: a quick check to identify cases that need closer attention. It is an examination used as a filter.
entries.definitionCN: 为找出需要进一步关注的对象而做的快速检查；是作为筛选器的 examination。

normalIntro.en: Real parts only: Latin examen, the pointer of a balance, plus -ation. The word asks what something weighs when placed against a standard.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：拉丁 examen‘天平指针’加 -ation。这个词问的是：把某物放到标准旁，它有多重。

normal.en: A balance pointer is the original examination: it shows the hidden weight.
normal.cn: 天平指针就是最初的 examination：它让隐藏的重量显形。

normal.en: An exam paper is a balance: your answer on one side, the mark scheme on the other.
normal.cn: 试卷就是天平：一边你的答案，一边评分标准。

normal.en: A doctor's examination puts your body beside normal ranges.
normal.cn: 医生的 examination 把身体放到正常范围旁边。

normal.en: Cross-examination weighs one story against other evidence.
normal.cn: 交叉质证用其他证据来称量一个说法。

normal.en: A lab examination reveals what the eye cannot weigh.
normal.cn: 实验室检查揭示眼睛称不出来的东西。

abstract.en: To examine is to risk an answer, not to confirm one.
abstract.cn: 审查是让答案承担风险，而不是确认答案。

abstract.en: Every examination chooses its instrument, and the instrument decides what can be found.
abstract.cn: 每次检查都选择自己的仪器，而仪器决定了能发现什么。

abstract.en: A test measures the answer, not the person; the confusion between them is a social fact.
abstract.cn: 考试测量的是答案，不是人；把两者混为一谈是一种社会事实。

examples.en: The examination was moved online after the snow closed the school.
examples.cn: 大雪停课后，考试改到了线上。

examples.en: A second examination of the manuscript found a date written in a later hand.
examples.cn: 对抄本的再次检查发现了一个后来补写的日期。

examples.en: Under examination, the witness admitted he had not seen the car.
examples.cn: 在质证中，证人承认他并没有看见那辆车。

dict_mnemonic.text: “一个贼，没捏住”——考试时想作弊，被老师“捏住”检查：examination 检查、考试。

root: 源自拉丁 examen（天平指针）与 examinare（称量、检验），经古法语 examinacion 进入英语；核心是“把对象放到标准上称一称”。
