sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of examination, one gesture: place something against a standard and see how it weighs. The standard can be a mark scheme, a normal range, another witness, an authority's rule, a body of evidence, or an instrument.
sensesIntro.cn: examination 的八个义项共用一个动作：把对象放到标准上，看它有多重。标准可以是评分方案、正常范围、另一份证词、权威规则、证据体系或仪器。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the pointer of a balance swinging as a weight is placed on one side.
core.cn: 核心意象：砝码放上一边时，天平指针摆动。

branches.en: TESTING CLAIMS: a school paper and a scholarly thesis are both weighed against a standard.
branches.cn: 检验主张：试卷与学术论文都被放到标准上称量。

branches.en: BRINGING TO LIGHT: close inspection and hypothesis testing reveal what was hidden.
branches.cn: 让隐者显形：仔细检查与假设检验都揭示隐藏的东西。

branches.en: READING THE BODY OR SAMPLE: the clinic and the laboratory use instruments to weigh what the eye cannot see.
branches.cn: 读取身体或样本：诊所与实验室用仪器称量眼睛看不见的东西。

branches.en: QUESTIONING A WITNESS: cross-examination weighs one account against other evidence.
branches.cn: 质询证人：交叉质证用一个说法对账其他证据。

branches.en: INVESTIGATING RECORDS: an authority compels documents into the open for comparison.
branches.cn: 调查记录：权威强制把文件摆出来做对照。

intro.en: Examination is examin- plus -ation. English also has the verb examine, the person nouns examiner and examinee, and the clipped form exam.
intro.cn: examination 是 examin- 加 -ation。英语还有动词 examine、人物名词 examiner 与 examinee，以及缩略形式 exam。

latinIntro.en: The Latin forms are examen, examinare, and exigere. The connection between examen and exigere is generally accepted but reconstructed, so it should not be presented as certain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁形式是 examen、examinare、exigere。examen 与 exigere 的联系被普遍接受，但属于重构，不应说成确定事实。

items.example: The panel examined every page of the report.
items.exampleCN: 专家组审查了报告的每一页。

items.example: The examination lasted three hours.
items.exampleCN: 考试持续了三个小时。

items.example: The examiner checked the seal on each sample.
items.exampleCN: 审查员检查了每个样本上的封条。

items.example: Each examinee received a numbered desk.
items.exampleCN: 每位应试者拿到一张编号课桌。

items.example: She has three exams next week.
items.exampleCN: 她下周有三场考试。

items.meaning: to question a witness for the opposing side
items.example: The lawyer cross-examined the witness for an hour.
items.exampleCN: 律师盘问证人一个小时。

items.meaning: the questioning of a witness by the other side
items.example: Cross-examination is limited to the scope of direct testimony.
items.exampleCN: 交叉质证限于直接证词的范围。

items.meaning: precise, or to demand and obtain
items.meaningCN: 精确的；强求；源自 exigere‘驱出、索取’
items.example: The exact wording of the clause matters.
items.exampleCN: 该条款的精确措辞很重要。

items.meaningCN: 紧急的；迫切需要处理的
items.example: The exigent circumstances justified a late-night call.
items.exampleCN: 紧急情况使得深夜致电成为正当。

items.example: The budget was cut in response to a fiscal exigency.
items.exampleCN: 为应对财政紧急状况，预算被削减。

latinEntries.meaning: the tongue or pointer of a balance; a weighing

latinEntries.meaningCN: 驱出；索取；称量（与 examen 的联系属一般认为）

definition_zh: n. 毛毛雨；细雨 v. 下毛毛雨；（烹饪）淋；洒
definition_en: very fine rain in tiny drops, to fall as such rain, or to pour a thin stream of liquid over food
core_image: 灰蒙蒙的天里飘着几乎看不见的细水珠，眼镜片蒙上一层小点，路面只发亮却不积水；另一头一只手把瓶子倾斜，橄榄油从瓶口拉成一条细线淋在沙拉上
scene: 天空灰得像蒙了纱，细水珠落在镜片上变成一层小点，路面只发亮却不积水。 A cold drizzle fell on the town all afternoon.
sceneCN: 这里 drizzle 是「毛毛雨」（第 1 个义项：极细小水珠的雨）；句意是冰冷的细雨整个下午落在镇上。图中可辨识物件：灰纱般的天空、蒙雾的镜片、发亮而无水洼的路面。

pos.zh: 毛毛雨；细雨
下毛毛雨；（烹饪）淋；洒

derivatives.zh: 细雨蒙蒙的；潮湿阴沉的

senses.title: Very fine rain
senses.definition: rain falling in many very small drops
senses.definitionCN: （名词）以极细小水珠落下的雨
senses.example: A cold drizzle fell on the town all afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 冰冷的细雨整个下午落在镇上。
senses.why: Grey air full of tiny beads that fog a pair of glasses instead of splashing.
senses.whyCN: 灰色的空气里满是细小水珠，把眼镜蒙上一层雾而不是溅起水花。

senses.title: To rain lightly
senses.definition: to rain lightly and steadily in very small drops
senses.definitionCN: （动词）以极细小水珠轻而持续地下雨
senses.example: It had been drizzling since dawn, so the pitch stayed soft.
senses.exampleCN: 从黎明起就一直下毛毛雨，所以球场一直是软的。
senses.why: A pavement that only shines, with no puddle anywhere on it.
senses.whyCN: 路面只是发亮，上面一处水洼也没有。

senses.title: Pour a thin thread
senses.definition: to pour a thin stream of liquid over food
senses.definitionCN: （动词）把液体成细线淋在食物上
senses.example: Drizzle the warm dressing over the leaves just before serving.
senses.exampleCN: 上桌前把温热的调味汁淋在菜叶上。
senses.why: A bottle tipped so that oil leaves the mouth as one thin shining thread.
senses.whyCN: 瓶子倾斜，油从瓶口拉成一条细亮的线。

intro.en: Drizzle is a frequentative built on an old verb meaning to fall: the ending repeats the action, so drizzle is falling again and again in the smallest drops.
intro.cn: drizzle 是在一个意为「落下」的古老动词上加反复体构成的：这个词尾让动作反复，所以 drizzle 就是以最细小的水珠一次次落下。

items.en: Old English dreosan means to fall.
items.cn: 古英语 dreosan 意为落下。

items.en: Middle English drusen means to fall in drops.
items.cn: 中古英语 drusen 意为成滴落下。

items.en: The frequentative form drizzle appears for very fine rain.
items.cn: 反复体形式 drizzle 出现，指极细的雨。

items.en: The adjective drizzly describes weather of fine steady rain.
items.cn: 形容词 drizzly 用来描述细雨连绵的天气。

items.en: Cookery books use drizzle for pouring a thin stream over a dish.
items.cn: 烹饪书用 drizzle 表示把细流淋在菜上。

items.en: The word stays the standard term for the lightest kind of rain.
items.cn: 这个词仍是最轻一类雨的标准说法。

note.en: Drizzle shares its busy ending with dazzle and grizzle, while its neighbours name other light ways of wetting a surface.
note.cn: drizzle 与 dazzle、grizzle 共用那个细碎的词尾，而它的近义词则是别的把表面弄湿的轻方式。

entries.definition: to blind someone briefly with a very bright light
entries.definitionCN: 用强光使人短暂目眩

entries.definition: silly or meaningless talk, or to talk in that way
entries.definitionCN: 胡话；说胡话

entries.definition: to whine fretfully, or in older use to make grey
entries.definitionCN: 烦躁地抱怨；旧时指使变灰

entries.definition: very fine rain mixed with mist
entries.definitionCN: 夹着雾的蒙蒙细雨

entries.definition: to scatter small drops or pieces over a surface
entries.definitionCN: 把小水滴或碎屑洒在表面

entries.definition: a short period of rain, heavier than drizzle
entries.definitionCN: 一阵短时的雨，比毛毛雨大

normalIntro.en: Five pictures of water arriving in the smallest possible pieces.
normalIntro.cn: 五个「水以最细小的形态到来」的画面。

normal.en: Grey air full of tiny beads that fog a pair of glasses instead of splashing.
normal.cn: 灰色的空气里满是细小水珠，把眼镜蒙上一层雾而不是溅起水花。

normal.en: A pavement that only shines, with no puddle anywhere on it.
normal.cn: 路面只是发亮，上面一处水洼也没有。

normal.en: A bottle tipped so that oil leaves the mouth as one thin shining thread.
normal.cn: 瓶子倾斜，油从瓶口拉成一条细亮的线。

normal.en: A window beaded with dots too small to run down.
normal.cn: 窗玻璃上缀满小到不会往下流的水点。

normal.en: A hand pulling a thread of honey across a bowl of yoghurt.
normal.cn: 一只手把一缕蜂蜜拉过一碗酸奶。

abstract.en: Grey air full of tiny beads that fog a pair of glasses instead of splashing.
abstract.cn: 灰色的空气里满是细小水珠，把眼镜蒙上一层雾而不是溅起水花。

abstract.en: A pavement that only shines, with no puddle anywhere on it.
abstract.cn: 路面只是发亮，上面一处水洼也没有。

abstract.en: A bottle tipped so that oil leaves the mouth as one thin shining thread.
abstract.cn: 瓶子倾斜，油从瓶口拉成一条细亮的线。

examples.en: A cold drizzle fell on the town all afternoon.
examples.cn: 冰冷的细雨整个下午落在镇上。

examples.en: It had been drizzling since dawn, so the pitch stayed soft.
examples.cn: 从黎明起就一直下毛毛雨，所以球场一直是软的。

examples.en: Drizzle the warm dressing over the leaves just before serving.
examples.cn: 上桌前把温热的调味汁淋在菜叶上。

dict_mnemonic.text: drizzle ＝ 古英语 drēosan（落下）＋ 反复后缀 -le ＝「一次次细细地落」。所以它不是 shower（阵雨）也不是 downpour（暴雨），而是几乎看不见水珠、只把路面弄亮的毛毛雨。厨房里的 drizzle with oil 是同一画面：把油拉成一条细线淋下去。同族的 mizzle 是「雾＋细雨」，形容词 drizzly 说的是那种整天阴湿的天气。

root: 古英语 drēosan（落下）→ 中古英语 drusen（成滴落下）→ 反复体 drizzle（毛毛雨）

sensesIntro.en: Water in the smallest pieces: beads that fog glasses, a road that only shines and oil pulled into one thin thread over a salad.
sensesIntro.cn: 最细小形态的水：蒙住镜片的细珠、只发亮的路面，以及拉成一条细线淋在沙拉上的油。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: grey air full of tiny beads fogging a pair of glasses while a bottle pulls oil into one thin shining thread
core.cn: 核心意象：灰色空气里满是细小水珠蒙住镜片，同时一只瓶子把油拉成一条细亮的线

branches.en: Rain made of very small drops.
branches.cn: 由极小水珠组成的雨。

branches.en: The act of falling so lightly.
branches.cn: 如此轻地落下的动作。

branches.en: A thin thread poured over food.
branches.cn: 淋在食物上的一条细线。

branches.en: The same fine rain as thing and as act.
branches.cn: 同一种细雨，一作事物一作动作。

branches.en: Liquid arriving in threads, not in drops.
branches.cn: 液体成线到来，而不是成滴。

intro.en: Drizzle is built with the frequentative ending -le; -y makes drizzly, and Latin still- and gutt- both mean a drop while plu- means rain.
intro.cn: drizzle 用反复后缀 -le 构成；-y 造出 drizzly，而拉丁语 still- 与 gutt- 都意为「滴」，plu- 意为「雨」。

latinIntro.en: Latin stilla and gutta mean a drop, pluere to rain and spargere to scatter.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 stilla 与 gutta 意为滴，pluere 意为下雨，spargere 意为洒。

definition_zh: 流域；河流盆地；以分水岭为界的汇水区域
definition_en: the whole area drained by a river and its tributaries, bounded by divides
core_image: 两条支流在谷口汇成一条大河，远处分水岭像碗沿一样把水收拢
scene: 两条支流在谷口汇成一条大河，远处分水岭像碗沿一样把水收拢。 A river basin gathers every drop that falls between its divides and carries it down one channel.
sceneCN: 这里取第 1 个义项（流域）；句意为流域收拢分水岭之间的每一滴水，并把它送进同一条河道。

pos.zh: 名词短语：流域；河流盆地；汇水区域

derivatives.zh: 由「河流」加形容词词尾构成，义为「河流的；河岸的」
由「河流盆地」中的中心名词独立使用，义为「盆地；水盆」
由表示「在下、次级」的前缀加「盆地」构成，义为「子流域」
由「盆地」与「范围广阔的」复合而成，义为「全流域的」
由表示「之间」的前缀加「盆地」构成，义为「跨流域的」

senses.title: The area drained by one river system
senses.definition: all the land whose runoff reaches a single river and its tributaries
senses.definitionCN: 指径流最终汇入同一条河及其支流的全部陆地
senses.example: The river basin covers a fifth of the country.
senses.exampleCN: 这个流域覆盖全国五分之一的土地。
senses.why: The phrase starts as a shape on a map: everything that drains through one outlet.
senses.whyCN: 这条短语最初是地图上的一个形状：凡经同一出口排出的地方都算在内。

senses.title: A bowl-shaped lowland holding a river
senses.definition: a broad depression between higher ground through which a river and its tributaries flow
senses.definitionCN: 指高地之间、有河流及支流穿过的宽阔低地
senses.example: The river basin lies between two mountain chains.
senses.exampleCN: 这个河流盆地位于两条山脉之间。
senses.why: The container word supplies the image of a bowl, and relief supplies the walls.
senses.whyCN: 「盆」这个词提供碗的意象，地形则提供碗壁。

senses.title: A unit of water management
senses.definition: the basin treated as one administrative unit for allocation, pollution control and flood planning
senses.definitionCN: 指把流域作为分配、治污与防洪规划的一个行政单元
senses.example: The river basin is managed by a single agency.
senses.exampleCN: 这个流域由一家机构统一管理。
senses.why: Water crosses many jurisdictions, so managers redraw the basin as one budget line.
senses.whyCN: 水跨越许多辖区，管理者便把流域重画为一条预算线。

senses.title: A basin crossing political borders
senses.definition: a basin shared by two or more countries or provinces
senses.definitionCN: 指由两个或更多国家、省份共享的流域
senses.example: The river basin crosses three national borders.
senses.exampleCN: 这个流域跨越三条国界。
senses.why: Water ignores borders, so the map unit and the political map rarely agree.
senses.whyCN: 水不理睬边界，因此流域单元与政区图很少吻合。

senses.title: A closed basin with no sea outlet
senses.definition: a basin whose water ends in an inland lake or evaporates rather than reaching the ocean
senses.definitionCN: 指水最终进入内陆湖或蒸发、而不流入海洋的流域
senses.example: The river basin has no outlet to the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 这个流域没有通向海洋的出口。
senses.why: An enclosed basin is a bowl with no drain hole, and salts accumulate inside it.
senses.whyCN: 封闭流域像一个没有排水孔的碗，盐分因此在里面累积。

senses.title: A legal planning district
senses.definition: a basin defined by law for water-quality targets and permits
senses.definitionCN: 指为水质目标与许可证管理而依法划定的流域
senses.example: The river basin district must meet its water quality targets.
senses.exampleCN: 这个流域区必须达到其水质目标。
senses.why: Regulation needs fixed lines, so the natural basin is redrawn as a legal district.
senses.whyCN: 监管需要固定界线，自然的流域因此被重画为法定区。

senses.title: A sedimentary basin filled by river deposits
senses.definition: a depression progressively filled with sand, mud and gravel brought by the river
senses.definitionCN: 指被河流带来的砂、泥与砾石逐渐填满的低地
senses.example: The river basin filled with sand and mud over millennia.
senses.exampleCN: 这个盆地历经千年被砂与泥填满。
senses.why: The bowl collects sediment as well as water, and geology reads the fill as a record.
senses.whyCN: 这个碗既收水也收沉积物，地质学把填充物读作记录。

senses.title: A region of shared water dependence
senses.definition: the community of users, farms and cities that depend on the same river system
senses.definitionCN: 指依靠同一河系的水的用户、农田与城市群体
senses.example: Farmers and cities in the river basin depend on the same snowmelt.
senses.exampleCN: 流域内的农民与城市依靠同一份融雪水。
senses.why: A basin is also a set of claimants, and the phrase can name them rather than the land.
senses.whyCN: 流域也是一群用水者，这个词因此可以指人而不指地。

intro.en: River came from Latin ripa, a bank, through the Vulgar Latin adjective riparia, land along a bank, and Old French rivere. Basin came through Old French bacin from Medieval Latin bacinus, a word of uncertain ultimate origin, possibly Gaulish.
intro.cn: 「河流」出自拉丁语 ripa「河岸」，经通俗拉丁语形容词「沿岸的土地」与古法语进入英语。「盆地」经古法语来自中世纪拉丁语 bacinus，其最终来源不确定，可能出自高卢语。

items.en: Ripa meant the bank of a river, the edge rather than the water.
items.cn: 这个词意为河岸，指水边而非水本身。

items.en: The adjective named land along a bank, and it became the Romance word for a river.
items.cn: 这个形容词指沿岸的土地，后来成为罗曼语中表示「河流」的词。

items.en: Old French rivere carried the word into English as river.
items.cn: 古法语把这个词带进英语，成为「河流」。

items.en: The word for a basin or bowl is of uncertain origin; a Gaulish source has been suggested but not established.
items.cn: 表示盆、碗的词来源不确定；有人提出高卢语来源，但未得到确证。

items.en: Old French bacin named a wide shallow vessel.
items.cn: 古法语中这个词指宽而浅的容器。

items.en: English took the vessel word and later applied it to bowl-shaped land.
items.cn: 英语借入这个容器词，后来用它指碗状的地形。

note.en: The first group shares the river or basin element; the second group names the technical equivalents and the lines between them.
note.cn: 第一组共享「河流」或「盆地」的成分；第二组是技术同义词与它们之间的界线。

entries.definition: A bowl or a bowl-shaped area of land.
entries.definitionCN: 指盆、碗，或碗状的地形区域。

entries.definition: A large natural stream flowing to the sea or a lake.
entries.definitionCN: 指流入海洋或湖泊的大天然水道。

entries.definition: Relating to a river or its banks.
entries.definitionCN: 指与河流或其河岸有关的。

entries.definition: A smaller basin within a larger one.
entries.definitionCN: 指大流域内部较小的流域。

entries.definition: Extending across the whole basin.
entries.definitionCN: 指遍及整个流域的。

entries.definition: The technical synonym for the area drained by a river system.
entries.definitionCN: 指一条河系所排水区域的技术同义词。

entries.definition: The area from which water is collected, common in British usage.
entries.definitionCN: 指集水区域，英国用法中常见。

entries.definition: In American usage the basin itself; in British usage the divide.
entries.definitionCN: 美国用法指流域本身，英国用法指分水岭。

entries.definition: The ridge of high ground separating two basins.
entries.definitionCN: 指分隔两个流域的高地脊线。

entries.definition: The flat land beside a river that floods periodically.
entries.definitionCN: 指河边周期性泛滥的平地。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations follow the bowl and the bank: water collected inside a rim and led out by one channel.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想沿着「碗」与「岸」展开：水被收在碗沿之内，再由一条河道送出。

normal.en: Think of a bowl: the rim is the divide, the bottom is the outlet.
normal.cn: 想一只碗：碗沿是分水岭，碗底是出水口。

normal.en: Everything inside the rim drains through the same river.
normal.cn: 碗沿以内的水都经同一条河流出。

normal.en: A closed basin is a bowl with no drain hole; salt stays inside.
normal.cn: 闭流流域是没有排水孔的碗，盐分留在里面。

normal.en: Water ignores borders, so a basin often crosses several countries.
normal.cn: 水不理睬国界，所以流域常跨越数国。

normal.en: A basin district is the legal redrawing of a natural bowl.
normal.cn: 流域区是把自然碗形改画成法定界线。

abstract.en: A catchment is a lesson in dependence: every slope sends its water to the same place.
abstract.cn: 流域是一堂关于依存的课：每道坡都把水送往同一处。

abstract.en: The same shape can be a physical bowl, a budget unit and a community.
abstract.cn: 同一个形状可以是物理的碗、预算单元，也可以是一个共同体。

abstract.en: Lines drawn on water are always negotiations, not facts.
abstract.cn: 画在水上的界线永远是协商，而不是事实。

examples.en: The river basin supplies water to more than thirty million people.
examples.cn: 这个流域为三千多万人供水。

examples.en: A transboundary river basin needs an agreement between the states that share it.
examples.cn: 跨界流域需要共享它的各州达成协议。

examples.en: Sediment cores show how the river basin filled over ten thousand years.
examples.cn: 沉积柱样显示这个盆地在一万年间如何被填满。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「瑞弗·贝森」——一条河被装进一只大碗（贝森），碗沿就是分水岭：流域

root: 「河流」出自拉丁语 ripa「河岸」，经通俗拉丁语「沿岸土地」与古法语进入英语；「盆地」经古法语来自中世纪拉丁语 bacinus，最终来源不确定，可能出自高卢语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses treat one catchment as a mapped area, a physical bowl, a management unit, a border case, a closed bowl, a legal district, a sediment trap and a community.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把同一片集水区分别看作地图区域、物理碗形、管理单元、跨界案例、封闭盆地、法定区、沉积陷阱与依存共同体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two tributaries meeting at a valley mouth, with a rim of hills holding the water in.
core.cn: 核心意象：两条支流在谷口相会，一圈丘陵像碗沿把水收住。

branches.en: THE SHAPE: the drained area and the lowland that holds it.
branches.cn: 形状：被排水的区域，以及容纳它的低地。

branches.en: THE UNIT: a management area and a district fixed by law.
branches.cn: 单元：管理区域与依法划定的区。

branches.en: THE BORDER CASE: a basin shared by states that do not share a map.
branches.cn: 跨界案例：被不同国家共享、却不共享一张地图的流域。

branches.en: THE CLOSED BOWL: no outlet, so water and salt stay.
branches.cn: 封闭的碗：没有出口，水与盐都留下。

branches.en: THE FILL AND THE PEOPLE: sediment building the basin, and users sharing one snowmelt.
branches.cn: 填充与人：沉积物造出盆地，用户共享同一份融雪。

intro.en: One half names the bank, the other names the bowl; together they name a bowl of land drained by one river.
intro.cn: 一半说「岸」，一半说「碗」；合起来就是被一条河排水的一只陆地大碗。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies the bank and the adjective of land along a bank; the bowl word reached Latin from an uncertain source, possibly Gaulish.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供「河岸」与「沿岸土地」的形容词；「碗」这个词进入拉丁语的来源不确定，可能出自高卢语。

items.example: It is the source of river and riparian.
items.exampleCN: 它是「河流」与「河岸的」等词的来源。

items.example: It became the Romance word for river.
items.exampleCN: 它成为罗曼语中表示河流的词。

items.example: Old French passed it to English.
items.exampleCN: 古法语把它传给英语。

items.example: The English word keeps the bank at its root.
items.exampleCN: 英语这个词的词根仍保留「岸」的意思。

items.example: It gave English basin.
items.exampleCN: 它构成英语中的「盆地」。

items.example: Its ultimate source is uncertain.
items.exampleCN: 其最终来源不确定。

items.example: English extended the vessel to land.
items.exampleCN: 英语把这个容器词扩展到地形。

items.example: It forms subbasin, a smaller basin inside a larger one.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「子流域」，即大流域内的小流域。

items.example: It forms basinwide, covering the whole basin.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「全流域的」。

derivatives.zh: 由「河流」加形容词词尾构成，义为「河流的」
由短语中心名词独立使用，义为「盆地；水盆」
由次级前缀加「盆地」构成，义为「子流域」
由「盆地」与「遍及」成分复合而成，义为「全流域的」
由「之间」前缀加「盆地」构成，义为「跨流域的」

definition_zh: 解释；说明；占比例；报账；对行为负责；清点；计入
definition_en: to explain or answer for something, to form a part of a total, or to give a reckoning of money, goods or conduct
core_image: 账房桌上摊开一本账簿，左页记进项，右页记去向，掌柜用笔逐条对上
scene: 月底账房把账簿摊在桌上，左边记进项，右边记去向，掌柜用笔逐条对上。 The manager must account for every sum in the ledger.
sceneCN: 这里指对每一笔款项作出说明（第 1 个义项：解释原因）；句意为经理必须对账簿里的每一笔金额作出交代。图中可辨识物件：账簿、毛笔、封存的票据。

pos.zh: 解释；说明；占比例；报账；负责

derivatives.zh: 短语的核心名词兼动词，义为「账目；说明」
由短语核心词加形容词尾构成，义为「负有交代责任的」
由该形容词加名词尾构成，义为「问责；责任」
由核心动词加名词尾构成，义为「会计；记账」
由核心词加表示施动者的名词尾构成，义为「会计员」

senses.title: To explain a cause
senses.definition: to give a reason or explanation for something that happened
senses.definitionCN: 为已经发生的事给出理由或解释
senses.example: The engineer can account for the delay in the schedule.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师能够解释进度延误的原因。
senses.why: The word began as a reckoning of money, and a reckoning is first of all a statement that answers a question.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指银钱的清算，而清算首先就是一份回答问题的交代。

senses.title: To explain a difference or phenomenon
senses.definition: to show why two things differ or why an observed fact is as it is
senses.definitionCN: 说明两件事为何不同，或说明观察到的现象为何如此
senses.example: The new model will account for the gap between the two readings.
senses.exampleCN: 新模型将说明两次读数之间差距的由来。
senses.why: An account must balance two sides, so the phrase naturally covers explaining a gap rather than only naming a cause.
senses.whyCN: 账目必须两边对得上，因此这个短语自然可以说明差距的由来，而不只是指出一个原因。

senses.title: To form a share of a total
senses.definition: to be a particular part of a whole, usually expressed as a number or percentage
senses.definitionCN: 构成整体中的某个部分，通常用数字或百分比表示
senses.example: Renewable sources may account for a third of the grid.
senses.exampleCN: 可再生能源可能占电网供应的三分之一。
senses.why: In a ledger each entry has a size, and that size as a share of the total became the modern statistical sense.
senses.whyCN: 账簿里每一笔都有大小，而它占总数的份额就成了现代统计义。

senses.title: To make up a total
senses.definition: to be the substance or component of a whole, considered as one of its parts
senses.definitionCN: 作为一个部分，构成整体的实质或成分
senses.example: Small firms can account for most of the new jobs.
senses.exampleCN: 小企业可能构成大部分新增岗位。
senses.why: The same arithmetic picture is read from the other side: the part does not merely occupy a share, it makes up the whole.
senses.whyCN: 同一幅算术图从另一侧读：部分不只是占了份额，而是把整体组成起来。

senses.title: To give a reckoning of money
senses.definition: to record and explain how money received or spent has been used
senses.definitionCN: 记录并说明收到或花出的钱是如何使用的
senses.example: The treasurer must account for the funds received in March.
senses.exampleCN: 财务主管必须说明三月收到的资金去向。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense: an account is a written reckoning presented to someone who has the right to check it.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项：账目就是呈交给有权核查者的一份书面清算。

senses.title: To answer for one's conduct
senses.definition: to take responsibility for an action and accept that one may be questioned or blamed for it
senses.definitionCN: 对某一行为承担责任，并接受因此受到质询或责备
senses.example: The officer will account for his decision to the board.
senses.exampleCN: 这名官员将向董事会为自己的决定作出交代。
senses.why: Money and conduct are both things that can be rendered up to another person, so the financial phrase extended to moral duty.
senses.whyCN: 钱和行为都是可以向他人交出的东西，因此这个财务短语扩展到了道义责任。

senses.title: To check goods one by one
senses.definition: to list and check every item or unit so that the record matches what is present
senses.definitionCN: 逐项列出并核对每个物品或单位，使记录与实际相符
senses.example: Two clerks can account for every item in the store.
senses.exampleCN: 两名职员能够把仓库里的每件物品清点清楚。
senses.why: A shopkeeper counts stock before writing the account, so counting and accounting share one verb.
senses.whyCN: 店主先清点存货再记账，因此清点与记账共用同一个动词。

senses.title: To include in a calculation or plan
senses.definition: to include something as a factor when judging, planning or calculating
senses.definitionCN: 在判断、计划或计算时把某事物作为一个因素纳入
senses.example: The budget should account for the rise in fuel costs.
senses.exampleCN: 预算应当把燃料成本上升计入考虑。
senses.why: The modern planning sense treats every relevant factor as an entry that must appear on the ledger.
senses.whyCN: 现代规划义把每个相关因素都当作账簿上必须出现的一笔。

intro.en: Account comes through Old French acont, a reckoning, from the verb conter, to count, which goes back to Latin computare, to reckon together, formed from com-, together, and putare, to reckon or estimate. For is a native English preposition, and the phrase settled in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.
intro.cn: 这个词经古法语「acont」「算账」而来，源头是动词「conter」「计数」，再往前是拉丁语「computare」「一起清算」，由「com-」「一起」和「putare」「清算、估算」构成。「for」是英语本族介词，这个短语在十六至十七世纪固定下来。

items.en: The verb meant to reckon, to estimate and also to prune, and the reckoning image runs through the whole family.
items.cn: 这个动词意为清算、估算，也有修剪之意，清算的意象贯穿整个词族。

items.en: With com-, together, the verb meant to reckon things up together, the source of count, compute and account.
items.cn: 加上表示「一起」的「com-」，动词意为把各项一起清算，是「count」「compute」「account」的共同来源。

items.en: French kept the counting sense and used it both for numbers and for telling a story.
items.cn: 法语保留了计数义，既用于数字，也用于讲述一件事。

items.en: The noun meant a reckoning or a statement of what was owed, and English borrowed it as account.
items.cn: 这个名词意为清算或应付账款的说明，英语把它借入为「account」。

items.en: English used the noun for a financial record and the verb for giving an explanation or a report.
items.cn: 英语把这一名词用于财务记录，把动词用于作出解释或报告。

items.en: From the sixteenth century, account for was used for answering for money and conduct, and by the seventeenth century for explaining and for forming a share.
items.cn: 自十六世纪起，「account for」用于为钱财和行为作出交代，到十七世纪又用于解释原因和构成比例。

note.en: The first group gathers forms built on the same counting word; the second group gathers verbs that explain, compose or answer.
note.cn: 第一组收录建立在同一个计数词上的形式；第二组收录表示解释、构成或交代的动词。

entries.definition: A record of money, or a spoken report; the core noun and verb behind the phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 指账目或口头说明；是该短语背后的核心名词与动词。

entries.definition: Required to explain and answer for one's actions.
entries.definitionCN: 指有责任为自己的行为作出解释与交代的。

entries.definition: The work of keeping and checking financial records.
entries.definitionCN: 指记录与核查财务账目的工作。

entries.definition: A reduction in price; the opposite prefix pulls the counting word in another direction.
entries.definitionCN: 指价格减免；相反的前缀把计数词引向另一方向。

entries.definition: To say numbers in order or to find how many there are.
entries.definitionCN: 指按顺序数数，或求出一共有多少。

entries.definition: To make something clear by giving details or reasons.
entries.definitionCN: 指通过给出细节或理由使某事物清楚。

entries.definition: To be the parts that make up a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 指构成整体的各部分。

entries.definition: To consist of or be made up of particular parts.
entries.definitionCN: 指由某些部分构成。

entries.definition: To show that an action or claim has a good reason.
entries.definitionCN: 指证明某一行为或说法有正当理由。

entries.definition: To give a formal spoken or written account of something.
entries.definitionCN: 指对某事作正式的口头或书面报告。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the ledger behind the word, its counting family, and the real phrases of money and share.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用这个词背后的账簿、它的计数词族，以及钱财与比例的真实搭配。

normal.en: An account is first a ledger, and to account for is to make the ledger balance.
normal.cn: 账目首先是一本账簿，而「account for」就是让账簿对得上。

normal.en: Count, compute, account and accountant all descend from the same Latin reckoning word.
normal.cn: 「count」「compute」「account」与「accountant」都出自同一个拉丁清算词。

normal.en: To account for money is to say where it went; to account for a delay is to say why it happened.
normal.cn: 为钱财作出交代是说钱去了哪里；为延误作出交代是说明它为何发生。

normal.en: In a report, a group that accounts for a third is one of three equal parts.
normal.cn: 在报告里，占三分之一的群体就是三等份中的一份。

normal.en: Account for every item is the stocktaker's phrase: nothing may be left off the list.
normal.cn: 「把每件物品都清点清楚」是盘点人的说法：清单上不能漏掉任何一项。

abstract.en: Every explanation is a small ledger: cause on one side, effect on the other, and the two must balance.
abstract.cn: 每一种解释都是一本小账簿：一边是原因，一边是结果，两边必须对得上。

abstract.en: A share is a number with a seat in the whole; accounting for it is giving that seat a name.
abstract.cn: 份额是整体中占一个位置的数字；说明它，就是给那个位置一个名字。

abstract.en: Responsibility begins when someone asks you to account for what you did, not for what you meant.
abstract.cn: 责任始于别人要求你交代做了什么，而不是交代你想做什么。

examples.en: The audit must account for the missing fuel.
examples.cn: 审计必须说明缺失燃料的去向。

examples.en: Women can account for nearly half of the workforce.
examples.cn: 女性可能占劳动力的近一半。

examples.en: He could not account for the broken seal.
examples.cn: 他无法解释封条为何破损。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「阿康特·佛」——账要对得上，原因要说得出：解释、占比、报账

root: 古法语「acont」「算账」←「conter」「计数」← 拉丁语「computare」「一起清算」=「com-」「一起」+「putare」「清算、估算」；「for」为英语本族介词，短语于十六至十七世纪固定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses fan out from the ledger: explaining a cause, explaining a difference, taking a share, making up a total, reporting money, answering for conduct, checking stock, and including a factor in a plan.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从账簿向外展开：解释原因、说明差异、占比例、构成总量、报账、为行为负责、清点存货、把因素计入计划。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ledger lies open, entries on both sides, and a brush moves down the column until the sums agree.
core.cn: 核心意象：账簿摊开，两边都是条目，笔沿着栏目往下走，直到数目相符。

branches.en: THE EXPLANATION: a cause is named, and a puzzling difference is made to balance.
branches.cn: 解释：指出一个原因，并让令人困惑的差异对得上。

branches.en: THE SHARE: a part is measured against the whole, and then treated as what makes the whole up.
branches.cn: 份额：部分被放在整体中衡量，随后又被视为构成整体的成分。

branches.en: THE RECKONING: money is reported and stock is counted until the record matches the shelf.
branches.cn: 清算：报告款项并清点存货，直到记录与货架相符。

branches.en: THE ANSWER: conduct is handed over to someone with the right to question it.
branches.cn: 交代：行为被交给有权质询的人。

branches.en: THE FACTOR: a future cost or condition becomes an entry that the plan must include.
branches.cn: 因素：未来的成本或条件成为计划必须列入的一笔。

intro.en: The phrase is built from a Latin counting word and a native English preposition, and its family is full of money words.
intro.cn: 这个短语由一个拉丁计数词和一个英语本族介词构成，其词族里满是与钱有关的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies putare and computare; Old French shortened the verb to conter and the noun to acont before English took them.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了「putare」与「computare」；古法语把动词缩短为「conter」、名词缩短为「acont」，英语随后借用。

items.example: The prefix gathers separate sums into one total.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把分开的数目聚成一个总数。

items.meaning: to reckon, to estimate, to prune
items.example: The verb is the seed of the whole counting family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是整个计数词族的种子。

items.structure: Latin verb from com- and putare
items.example: It is the source of count and compute.
items.exampleCN: 它是「count」与「compute」的来源。

items.example: French used one verb for numbers and for narrative.
items.exampleCN: 法语用同一个动词表示数字与叙述。

items.meaning: a reckoning, a statement of what is owed
items.example: The noun came into English as account.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词进入英语成为「account」。

items.meaning: with respect to, on behalf of
items.example: The native preposition marks what the account is about.
items.exampleCN: 这个本族介词标出账目所涉及的对象。

items.meaning: a record of money; to explain
items.example: English split the borrowed noun and verb.
items.exampleCN: 英语把借来的名词与动词兼用。

items.example: It forms the word for being answerable.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示「应被交代」的词。

items.example: It names the work of keeping books.
items.exampleCN: 它指记账这项工作。

Latin verb from in- and putare

derivatives.zh: 由短语核心词加形容词尾构成，义为「负有交代责任的」
由该形容词加名词尾构成，义为「问责；责任」
由核心动词加名词尾构成，义为「会计；记账」
由核心词加表示施动者的名词尾构成，义为「会计员」
短语核心词的名词形式，义为「账目；说明」

definition_zh: 威权的；专制的；要求服从的；威权主义者；家长式的
definition_en: demanding obedience and allowing little freedom, or relating to a system that concentrates power in an authority
core_image: 办公桌后坐着一位上司，桌上立着一块牌写着「照我说的做」，门外的人排队等候批准
scene: 新经理上任后，所有决定都要经他一人签字，员工连改一行文案也要等批准。 The new manager ran an authoritarian office where no one dared to disagree.
sceneCN: 新经理上任后，所有决定都要经他一人签字，员工连改一行文案也要等批准；句中这个词指「要求服从、几乎不容自由的」（第 1 个义项：以权威为中心、限制异议与自主的制度或作风）。句意为新经理把一个办公室管成威权式的，没人敢表示不同意见。可辨识物件：签字笔、审批单、门口排队的人、写有命令的牌子。

pos.zh: 威权的；专制的；要求服从的
家长式的；管得过严的（口语）
威权主义者；主张集中权力的人

senses.title: Demanding obedience
senses.definition: expecting people to comply without question and treating disagreement as a problem
senses.definitionCN: 要求人们无条件服从，并把异议视为问题
senses.example: The new manager ran an authoritarian office where no one dared to disagree.
senses.exampleCN: 新经理把一个办公室管成威权式的，没人敢表示不同意见。
senses.why: The suffix -arian forms an adjective of adherence, so the word describes a way of holding authority rather than an office.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -arian 构成表示信奉的形容词，因此这个词描述握有权威的方式，而非某个职位。

senses.title: Relating to authoritarian government
senses.definition: belonging to a system in which power is concentrated and elections, if held, are not competitive
senses.definitionCN: 属于权力集中、即使有选举也缺乏竞争的体制
senses.example: The regime was authoritarian but kept elections for show.
senses.exampleCN: 这个政权是威权式的，却保留选举作为门面。
senses.why: Political science needed a word for systems that are neither democratic nor fully totalitarian, and this adjective filled the gap.
senses.whyCN: 政治学需要一个词来描述既非民主、也非完全极权的体制，这个形容词填补了空缺。

senses.title: A person who favours such rule
senses.definition: someone who believes order requires concentrated, unchallenged authority
senses.definitionCN: 认为秩序需要集中而不容挑战的权威的人
senses.example: Authoritarians distrust open debate.
senses.exampleCN: 威权主义者不信任公开辩论。
senses.why: One form serves as adjective and person-noun, so the believer and the belief look identical.
senses.whyCN: 同一个形式兼作形容词与指人的名词，因此信徒与信条看起来一样。

senses.title: A parenting style
senses.definition: raising children with strict rules and little room for discussion or autonomy
senses.definitionCN: 以严格规则养育孩子，很少给讨论或自主空间
senses.example: Authoritarian parents set rules without discussion.
senses.exampleCN: 专制型父母立规矩而不讨论。
senses.why: The political word is borrowed for the family, the smallest place where unchecked authority is exercised.
senses.whyCN: 这个政治词被借来描述家庭，也就是行使不受制约权威的最小场所。

senses.title: A management style
senses.definition: running a workplace by centralised approval and one-way instruction
senses.definitionCN: 靠集中审批与单向指令运行工作场所
senses.example: An authoritarian boss centralises every approval.
senses.exampleCN: 威权式上司把每一项批准都集中到自己手里。
senses.why: Workplaces reproduce the state in miniature, so the same adjective describes a chain of approvals.
senses.whyCN: 工作场所是国家的缩小复制，因此同一个形容词可描述审批链。

senses.title: A personality trait
senses.definition: a disposition that prefers rigid order, hierarchy and submission to authority
senses.definitionCN: 偏好僵化的秩序、等级与服从权威的性情
senses.example: His authoritarian streak showed in small rules.
senses.exampleCN: 他的威权倾向体现在一条条小规矩里。
senses.why: Twentieth-century psychology turned a political adjective into a measurable trait, which is why questionnaires use the word.
senses.whyCN: 二十世纪心理学把这个政治形容词变成可测量的特质，因此问卷会用到这个词。

senses.title: An institutional culture
senses.definition: a habit inside an organization that punishes criticism and rewards deference
senses.definitionCN: 机构内部惩罚批评、奖励顺从的习惯
senses.example: The university's authoritarian culture discouraged criticism.
senses.exampleCN: 这所大学的威权文化压制了批评。
senses.why: Culture is authority without a visible ruler, so the word can describe an atmosphere rather than a person.
senses.whyCN: 文化是没有可见统治者的权威，因此这个词可描述氛围，而非某个人。

senses.title: Order valued above liberty
senses.definition: characteristic of an ideology that treats stability and obedience as higher goods than freedom
senses.definitionCN: 把稳定与服从视为高于自由的价值的意识形态特征
senses.example: The party's authoritarian ideology valued order over liberty.
senses.exampleCN: 这个政党的威权意识形态把秩序看得高于自由。
senses.why: The adjective also marks a value ranking, which is the ideological core behind the institutional forms.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词也标出一种价值排序，而那正是制度形式背后的意识形态核心。

intro.en: Authoritarian is authority plus the suffix -arian, modelled on French autoritaire. English used it from the nineteenth century for systems that concentrate power, and the twentieth century extended it to personalities and management.
intro.cn: authoritarian 是 authority 加后缀 -arian，仿法语 autoritaire 构成。英语从十九世纪起用它指集中权力的体制，二十世纪又扩展到人格与管理。

items.en: Augere meant 'to increase, to grow'. Its Indo-European source is reconstructed, so the older root is a reconstruction rather than an attested form.
items.cn: augere 意为「增加、生长」。它的印欧来源是重构的，因此更早的词根是重构形式，而非有书证的形式。

items.en: Auctor meant 'originator, promoter, author', the person who makes something grow or brings it about. The word began with creation, not with command.
items.cn: auctor 意为「发起者、推动者、作者」，即使某物生长或促成其事的人。这个词从创造开始，而非从命令开始。

items.en: Auctoritas meant 'advice, influence, prestige, command'. Roman authority rested on recognized standing as much as on force, a nuance the modern adjective tends to flatten.
items.cn: auctoritas 意为「建议、影响、威望、命令」。罗马的权威既靠公认地位，也靠武力，现代形容词往往抹平这一细微差别。

items.en: English authority is recorded from the Middle Ages, first for a right to command and later for an expert source. The noun still carries both readings.
items.cn: 英语 authority 自中世纪起有书证，先指发令的权利，后指专家性来源。这个名词至今兼有这两种读法。

items.en: The suffix -arian marks a person or thing that adheres to a principle, as in egalitarian and vegetarian. Added to authority it names adherence to concentrated authority.
items.cn: 后缀 -arian 标出信奉某一原则的人或事物，如 egalitarian 与 vegetarian。加在 authority 上，它指对集中权威的信奉。

items.en: The adjective fixed as a technical term for non-democratic but not fully totalitarian systems in the twentieth century, and psychology applied it to personalities after 1950. Source uncertain (first date): the earliest technical citation is not fixed.
items.cn: 到二十世纪，这个形容词固定为指「非民主但未达完全极权」体制的术语；心理学在 1950 年之后把它用于人格。首见年代不确定：最早的技术性书证并无定论。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same Latin auctor root or with a confusingly similar shape; group two holds adjectives for neighbouring kinds of concentrated rule.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁 auctor 词根或外形近似到易混的词；第二组是描述相邻集中统治类型的形容词。

entries.definition: The right or power to command, or an expert body. Authoritarian is the adjective for a way of using that power.
entries.definitionCN: 指发令的权利或权力，或专家机构。authoritarian 是描述使用这种权力方式的形容词。

entries.definition: Trustworthy and expert, as in an authoritative account. It is often confused with authoritarian, but it praises reliability rather than obedience.
entries.definitionCN: 指可信且有专家根据，如权威性的记述。它常与 authoritarian 混淆，但它赞扬可靠性，而非要求服从。

entries.definition: The doctrine or regime; authoritarian is the adjective or the person who supports it.
entries.definitionCN: 指学说或政权；authoritarian 是形容词或支持者。

entries.definition: A person who writes or creates something, from the same Latin root. The word began with making, not with ruling.
entries.definitionCN: 指写作或创造某物的人，同出拉丁词根。这个词始于创造，而非统治。

entries.definition: From Greek authentikos 'original, genuine', not from Latin auctor. It means real or genuine and has no connection with authority.
entries.definitionCN: 出自希腊 authentikos「原本的、真正的」，并非拉丁 auctor。它意为真实、真品，与权威无关。

entries.definition: Relating to rule by one person with sole authority; it stresses the number of rulers, while authoritarian stresses the demand for obedience.
entries.definitionCN: 与一人独掌权威的统治相关；它强调统治者人数，而 authoritarian 强调要求服从。

entries.definition: Like a dictator: unchecked and often arbitrary. Authoritarian can describe a legal system with elections, so it is sometimes softer.
entries.definitionCN: 像独裁者一样：不受制约且往往任意。authoritarian 可描述带选举的法律制度，因此有时语气较缓。

entries.definition: Exercising power at a ruler's whim; the word judges the rule harshly, while authoritarian is a cooler analytical label.
entries.definitionCN: 按统治者心意行使权力；这个词严厉评判统治，而 authoritarian 是较冷静的分析标签。

entries.definition: Seeking control over every part of life, including private thought; it is a stronger claim than authoritarian, which can allow a private sphere.
entries.definitionCN: 试图控制生活的每一部分，包括私人思想；它比 authoritarian 是更强的断言，后者可允许私人领域存在。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: a real Latin root, a real suffix of adherence and real social-science phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁词根、真实的表信奉后缀与真实的社会科学用语。

normal.en: Authority plus -arian: the ending means adherence, so the word names those who cling to concentrated authority.
normal.cn: authority 加 -arian：词尾意为信奉，因此这个词指紧抓集中权威的人。

normal.en: The family runs authority, authorize, authoritative, authoritarian, authoritarianism.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 authority、authorize、authoritative、authoritarian、authoritarianism。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: an authoritarian regime, authoritarian personality, authoritarian parenting.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：威权政权、威权人格、专制型教养。

normal.en: Do not confuse authoritative with authoritarian: one means reliable, the other means bossy.
normal.cn: 不要把 authoritative 与 authoritarian 混淆：一个意为可信，一个意为专横。

normal.en: The root began with growth and creation, not with command.
normal.cn: 这个词根最初表示生长与创造，而非命令。

abstract.en: Picture a door with a sign that says do as I say, and no handle on your side.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门，挂着「照我说的做」的牌子，你这一侧没有门把手。

abstract.en: Picture a ladder where every rung is an approval stamp.
abstract.cn: 想象一架梯子，每一级都是一个审批印章。

abstract.en: Picture a room where the thermostat is locked behind glass.
abstract.cn: 想象一间屋子，恒温器被锁在玻璃后面。

examples.en: The country moved from an authoritarian regime to a fragile democracy.
examples.cn: 这个国家从威权政权走向脆弱的民主。

examples.en: Authoritarian management drove away the most experienced staff.
examples.cn: 威权式管理赶走了最有经验的员工。

examples.en: The study measured authoritarian attitudes among first-year students.
examples.cn: 这项研究测量了一年级学生的威权态度。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「权威」加「信奉」：信奉集中权威、要求服从；这属构词说明，并非谐音联想

root: 拉丁 augere「增加、生长」（更早词根为重构形式）→ auctor「发起者、作者」→ auctoritas「建议、影响、命令」→ 英语 authority；加后缀 -arian（信奉……的，仿法语 autoritaire）构成 authoritarian（十九世纪）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from a way of holding power to a way of ranking values: obedience demanded, a regime, a believer, a parent, a boss, a personality, a culture and an ideology that prefers order to liberty.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从握权方式走向价值排序：要求服从、政权、信奉者、父母、上司、人格、文化，以及把秩序置于自由之上的意识形态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a desk with a sign reading do as I say, a pen for every approval, and a queue waiting outside the door.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张桌子，牌子上写着「照我说的做」，每份批准都要用那支笔，门外排着等候的人。

branches.en: The demand for obedience and the ranking of order above liberty are one preference seen as habit and as doctrine.
branches.cn: 要求服从与把秩序置于自由之上，是同一偏好在习惯与教义两个层面的呈现。

branches.en: A regime is the demand written into law, with elections kept only as a façade.
branches.cn: 政权是把这一要求写进法律，选举只留作门面。

branches.en: A believer and the belief share one form, which is why the adjective can also name a person.
branches.cn: 信徒与信条共用同一个形式，因此这个形容词也能指人。

branches.en: The family and the university are the same authority at two sizes, one with children and one with colleagues.
branches.cn: 家庭与大学是同一权威的两种尺寸，一个面对孩子，一个面对同事。

branches.en: A boss and a personality are the same trait seen from outside and from inside.
branches.cn: 上司与人格是同一特质从外部与内部看到的两种样子。

intro.en: Authoritarian is a Latin noun of authority plus a suffix of adherence, so it reads as 'one who holds to concentrated authority'.
intro.cn: authoritarian 是表示权威的拉丁名词加表信奉的后缀，因此可读作「信奉集中权威者」。

latinIntro.en: Latin auctor and auctoritas supply the base; auctor comes from augere 'to increase', whose older Indo-European root is reconstructed rather than attested.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 auctor 与 auctoritas 提供基础；auctor 出自 augere「增加」，其更早的印欧词根是重构的，而非有书证的。

items.example: The root begins with growth, not with command.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根始于生长，而非命令。

items.example: The person-word names one who brings something about.
items.exampleCN: 这个指人的词指促成某事的人。

items.example: The abstract noun adds standing and weight to the person.
items.exampleCN: 抽象名词在个人之上加上了地位与分量。

items.meaning: the right to command; an expert body
items.example: English took the noun in the Middle Ages.
items.exampleCN: 英语在中世纪借入这个名词。

items.example: The suffix marks adherence to a principle.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀标出对某一原则的信奉。

items.example: English formed the adjective in the nineteenth century.
items.exampleCN: 英语在十九世纪构成这个形容词。

items.example: A true friend of the word, often mistaken for the other.
items.exampleCN: 这是这个词真正的近亲，却常被误认作另一词。

items.example: The verb names the act of granting authority.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词指授予权威的行为。

items.example: The oldest sense is creation, not rule.
items.exampleCN: 最古老的含义是创造，而非统治。

definition_zh: 价格；代价；给…定价；报价
definition_en: the amount of money for which something is sold, or what must be given up to obtain something
core_image: 货架上一枚小小的价签，数字不大，却决定了谁会拿起这件商品
scene: 货架前，顾客翻过价签看背面，又把商品放回原位，转身走向更便宜的一排。 The price of the coat was reduced twice before it sold.
sceneCN: 这里 price 指「商品的售价」（第 1 个义项：出售商品所要求的金额）；句意为这件外套的价格降了两次才卖出去。图中可辨识物件：货架价签、翻看标签的顾客、更便宜的一排商品、被放回的外套；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 价格；代价；报价
给…定价；标价（动词重音不变）

senses.title: The money asked for a good
senses.definition: the amount of money a seller asks for an item or service
senses.definitionCN: 卖方为某件商品或服务索要的金额
senses.example: The price of the coat was reduced twice before it sold.
senses.exampleCN: 这件外套的价格降了两次才卖出去。
senses.why: the core sense is a stated amount, which is what a price tag shows.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是一个被标出的金额，也就是价签所显示的内容。

senses.title: What must be given up
senses.titleCN: 为得到某物必须付出的代价
senses.definition: the cost in effort, risk or lost alternatives of obtaining something
senses.definitionCN: 为获得某物而在努力、风险或放弃的其他选择上付出的代价
senses.example: The price of success was three years without weekends.
senses.exampleCN: 成功的代价是三年没有周末。
senses.why: the word extends from money to any scarce thing given up, because both are what one pays.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从金钱延伸到任何被放弃的稀缺之物，因为两者都是所付出的东西。

senses.title: To set a price on something
senses.definition: to decide and mark the amount to be charged for an item
senses.definitionCN: 决定并标出某项商品的收费金额
senses.example: They priced the tickets at twenty pounds.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把票价定为二十英镑。
senses.why: the verb is the noun turned into an act of assigning the amount.
senses.whyCN: 动词是名词转为「指派金额」的动作。

senses.title: The general level of prices
senses.definition: the average level of charges across an economy at a given time
senses.definitionCN: 某一时期一个经济体中收费的平均水平
senses.example: Prices rose faster than wages for a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 有十年时间，物价涨得比工资快。
senses.why: in the plural the word often means the general level rather than one tag.
senses.whyCN: 用复数时，这个词常指总体水平，而非一张价签。

senses.title: A reward offered for a capture
senses.titleCN: 为缉拿或寻回而设的赏金
senses.definition: a sum offered to anyone who finds a person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 向找到某人或某物者提供的金额
senses.example: A price was put on the fugitive's head.
senses.exampleCN: 有人为这名逃犯的人头设了赏金。
senses.why: the older sense treats a reward as the amount paid for a result.
senses.whyCN: 较旧的义项把赏金看作「为某个结果所付的金额」。

senses.title: A quoted buying or selling rate
senses.definition: the rate at which a dealer will buy or sell in a financial market
senses.definitionCN: 交易商在金融市场愿意买进或卖出的价位
senses.example: The bond price fell after the announcement.
senses.exampleCN: 公告之后债券价格下跌。
senses.why: financial markets quote two prices, a bid and an offer, so the noun names a rate rather than a tag.
senses.whyCN: 金融市场报出买价与卖价两个价位，因此这个名词指一个比率，而非标签。

senses.title: Odds in racing or betting
senses.definition: the odds offered on a horse or outcome, expressed as a price
senses.definitionCN: 对某匹马或某个结果开出的赔率，以价位表示
senses.example: The bookmaker shortened the price on the favourite.
senses.exampleCN: 博彩商调低了热门马匹的赔率。
senses.why: betting calls odds a price because the stake buys a chance at a return.
senses.whyCN: 博彩把赔率称作 price，因为赌注买到的是一次回报机会。

senses.title: Any scale of worth
senses.titleCN: 衡量与交换的价值尺度（抽象义）
senses.definition: the measure by which a society or person values something
senses.definitionCN: 社会或个人用来衡量某物价值的尺度
senses.example: Health has no price in the ordinary market sense.
senses.exampleCN: 健康在普通市场意义上没有价格。
senses.why: the word generalizes once value itself is what is being measured, not only goods.
senses.whyCN: 当被衡量的是价值本身而非仅商品时，这个词就一般化了。

intro.en: Price comes through Old French pris from Latin pretium 'price, value, reward'. It is a doublet of prize in the sense of value, but not of prize meaning an award. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: price 经古法语 pris 上溯拉丁 pretium「价格、价值、报酬」。它与表示「价值」的 prize 是对偶词，但与表示「奖赏」的 prize 不是。年代均为约数。

items.en: Pretium covered price, value and reward, so the Latin word already contained both the commercial and the figurative seeds.
items.cn: pretium 兼指价格、价值与报酬，因此这个拉丁词已同时含商业义与比喻义的种子。

items.en: Old French pris meant the amount asked or the worth of a thing, and passed both senses to English.
items.cn: 古法语 pris 指索要的金额或某物的价值，并把这两层意思都传给英语。

items.en: English price appears in the thirteenth century; the plural came to mean the general cost of living.
items.cn: 英语 price 出现于 13 世纪；其复数后来指一般生活成本。

items.en: Prize meaning value is a variant of price; prize meaning an award came from Old French prise 'a capture', from prendre 'to take', a different root.
items.cn: 表示「价值」的 prize 是 price 的变体；表示「奖赏」的 prize 来自古法语 prise「捕获」，再上溯 prendre「拿取」，词根不同。

items.en: The figurative price of success and the betting price of a horse extend the same core: something must be paid for an outcome.
items.cn: 「成功的代价」与赛马的「赔率」都延伸同一核心：为了某个结果必须付出某物。

items.en: The exact first English citation is approximate. Latin pretium and Old French pris are well documented.
items.cn: 最早的英语书证年代只是约数。拉丁 pretium 与古法语 pris 都有充分书证。

note.en: Group one holds words that look like price or share its root but differ in sense; group two holds near terms for an amount charged.
note.cn: 第一组是形似 price 或与其同根、但意义不同的词；第二组是表示「所收金额」的近义词。

entries.definition: As value, it is a doublet of price; as an award, it descends from prendre 'to take'. Only the first sense is etymologically the same word.
entries.definitionCN: 作「价值」解时，它是 price 的对偶词；作「奖赏」解时，上溯 prendre「拿取」。只有前一义在词源上是同一个词。

entries.definition: From Latin pretiosus 'costly', built on pretium; it describes worth, not the amount charged.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 pretiosus「贵重」，建于 pretium 之上；它描述价值，而非所收金额。

entries.definition: From ad- plus pretiare 'to value'; it means to estimate worth, not to set a selling price.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 ad- 加 pretiare「估价」；意为估算价值，而非设定售价。

entries.definition: Built on price with -y, meaning expensive; it describes the level, not the amount itself.
entries.definitionCN: 由 price 加 -y 构成，意为昂贵；它描述水平，而非金额本身。

entries.definition: The expense of making or obtaining something; price is what the buyer pays, and the two need not be equal.
entries.definitionCN: 制作或取得某物的支出；price 是买主所付，两者不必相等。

entries.definition: The amount a provider demands for a service; it is close to price but more common for services and fees.
entries.definitionCN: 服务提供者索要的金额；与 price 接近，但更常用于服务与费用。

entries.definition: A fixed payment for a professional service or privilege; it is a kind of price with a narrower setting.
entries.definitionCN: 为专业服务或特权支付的固定款项；它是范围更窄的一类价格。

entries.definition: The worth of something to a person; price is what is asked, while value is what is judged.
entries.definitionCN: 某物对某人的价值；price 是所要之数，value 是被判断的价值。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin pretium 'value': the same root runs through price, precious and appraise.
normal.cn: 拉丁 pretium「价值」：同一词根贯穿 price、precious 与 appraise。

normal.en: The family runs price, pricing, priced, pricey, priceless, overprice, underprice.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 price、pricing、priced、pricey、priceless、overprice、underprice。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the commercial sense: market price, price tag, price increase.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出商业义：市场价格、价签、价格上涨。

normal.en: The figurative sense is marked by of: the price of success, the price of silence.
normal.cn: 比喻义由 of 标出：成功的代价、沉默的代价。

normal.en: Betting uses price for odds, because a stake buys a chance at a return.
normal.cn: 博彩用 price 指赔率，因为赌注买到的是一次回报机会。

abstract.en: Picture a tiny tag that decides whether a hand reaches out or moves on.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚小小的价签，决定一只手是伸出去还是走开。

abstract.en: Picture a coin placed on one side of a scale and a thing on the other.
abstract.cn: 想象天平一边放硬币，另一边放物品。

abstract.en: Picture a finish line with a toll booth in front of it.
abstract.cn: 想象一条终点线前面立着一个收费亭。

examples.en: The price of the ticket includes the ferry crossing.
examples.cn: 票价包含渡船费用。

examples.en: They paid a high price for ignoring the warning.
examples.cn: 他们因忽视警告付出了高昂代价。

examples.en: The dealer quoted a price for the old car.
examples.cn: 经销商为这辆旧车报了价。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「price（价格）」——货架上那个决定买不买的数字 → 价格、代价

root: 拉丁 pretium「价格、价值、报酬」→ 古法语 pris → 英语 price；与表示「奖赏」的 prize 不同源，但与表示「价值」的 prize 属对偶词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one number: a seller states what a thing costs, and that number is then read as a tag, a sacrifice, a verb, a general level, a reward, a quoted rate, betting odds, and finally any scale of worth.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个数字展开：卖方说出某物要多少钱，这个数字再被读作价签、牺牲、动词、总体水平、赏金、报价、赔率，最后是任何价值尺度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one small tag whose number decides whether a hand reaches out.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚小价签，其数字决定一只手是否伸出。

branches.en: AMOUNT AND ACT: the number on the tag, and the act of putting it there.
branches.cn: 金额与动作：价签上的数字，以及把数字放上去的动作。

branches.en: SACRIFICE AND SCALE: what must be given up, and the wider measure of worth it implies.
branches.cn: 牺牲与尺度：必须放弃的东西，以及它所含的更广价值尺度。

branches.en: THE GENERAL LEVEL: prices in the plural become the cost of living.
branches.cn: 总体水平：复数的 prices 成为生活成本。

branches.en: REWARD AND QUOTE: a sum offered for a capture, and a rate quoted in a market.
branches.cn: 赏金与报价：为缉拿所设的金额，以及市场中报出的价位。

branches.en: BETTING ODDS: the stake buys a chance, so the odds are called a price.
branches.cn: 博彩赔率：赌注买到机会，因此赔率被称作价格。

intro.en: Price is a borrowed Latin noun that English has turned into a verb, an adjective and an action noun, so the family spreads in several directions.
intro.cn: price 是借入的拉丁名词，英语把它变成动词、形容词与动作名词，因此词族向多个方向展开。

latinIntro.en: Latin pretium, pretiosus and pretiare supply price, precious, appraise and appreciate; English suffixes supply pricing, priced, pricey and priceless.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 pretium、pretiosus 与 pretiare 提供 price、precious、appraise 与 appreciate；英语后缀提供 pricing、priced、pricey 与 priceless。

items.example: The root carries both money and worth.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根兼含金钱与价值。

items.structure: Latin pretium via Old French pris
items.example: The price held steady all year.
items.exampleCN: 价格全年保持稳定。

items.example: Prices fell in the autumn.
items.exampleCN: 物价在秋季下降。

items.example: The book is priced at twelve pounds.
items.exampleCN: 这本书标价十二英镑。

items.example: Pricing is handled centrally.
items.exampleCN: 定价由总部统一处理。

items.example: The seats were pricey but comfortable.
items.exampleCN: 座位很贵，但很舒适。

items.example: The diary is priceless to historians.
items.exampleCN: 这本日记对历史学者而言无价。

items.example: The seller overpriced the flat.
items.exampleCN: 卖方把这套房子定价过高。

items.example: They underpriced the tickets and sold out.
items.exampleCN: 他们把票价定得过低，结果售罄。

items.example: A valuer appraised the painting.
items.exampleCN: 一位估价师为这幅画估了价。

latinEntries.meaning: to value, set a price on

definition_zh: 自豪；骄傲；傲慢；自尊（心）；狮群；以……为荣
definition_en: a warm feeling about one's own or another's achievement; an excessive sense of one's own importance; self-respect; a group of lions; and, as a verb, to feel proud about something one has
core_image: 胸膛往上一提，下巴微微抬起的那一瞬
scene: 毕业典礼上，主持人念到儿子的名字，母亲坐在观众席里，背一下子挺直了。 Her face shone with pride as her son walked across the stage to take his diploma.
sceneCN: 这里 pride 指「自豪、骄傲」（第 1 个义项：因自己或亲近的人取得成绩而心里发亮）；句意为儿子走上台领取毕业证书时，她脸上泛着自豪的光。图中可辨识物件：毕业证书、观众席、被念到名字的学生。

pos.zh: 自豪；骄傲；傲慢；自尊；狮群
以……为荣（用于 pride oneself on）

derivatives.zh: 与 pride 同属古英语 prūd 词族，但不是由 pride 加后缀得来：pride 是名词，proud 是形容词，义为「自豪的；骄傲的」
由 pride 加形容词后缀 -ful 构成，义为「自负的；傲慢的」
由形容词 proud 加 -ly 构成，义为「自豪地；得意地」，与 pride 同源而词形不同

senses.title: A warm feeling about one's own or another's success
senses.definition: a feeling of deep pleasure and satisfaction that comes from what you or people close to you have done or possess
senses.definitionCN: 因自己或亲近的人所做成、所拥有的事而感到的深切愉快与满足
senses.example: She looked at her finished painting with quiet pride.
senses.exampleCN: 她带着平静的自豪看着自己画完的画。
senses.why: The Old English noun first named the bare quality of being proud, and English kept its warmer half: the lift a person feels when something of theirs turns out well.
senses.whyCN: 古英语名词最早只指「骄傲」这种性质，英语留下了它温暖的一半：当自己这边的事情做成了，人心里往上一提，这就是自豪。

senses.title: An exaggerated belief in one's own importance
senses.definition: an unreasonable feeling that you are better or more important than other people
senses.definitionCN: 毫无道理地觉得自己比别人强、比别人重要
senses.example: It was pride, not principle, that stopped him from admitting the mistake.
senses.exampleCN: 让他不肯认错的是自大，而不是原则。
senses.why: The same self-regard that lifts a person up can also close the ears: once the good opinion of oneself grows past what the facts support, the word slides into the vice that preachers warn against.
senses.whyCN: 同一种自我看重既能让人挺起胸，也能堵住耳朵：当一个人对自己的好评超过了事实能撑住的分量，这个词就滑向传道者所警告的那种恶。

senses.title: The respect a person keeps for themselves
senses.definition: a proper sense of one's own worth that keeps a person from doing something shameful
senses.definitionCN: 对自己价值的正当意识，使人不肯做出丢脸的事
senses.example: He had too much pride to ask for help with the rent.
senses.exampleCN: 他的自尊心太强，不肯开口求人帮忙付房租。
senses.why: Between the warm sense and the arrogant one lies a third: pride as the floor a person refuses to sink below, the line kept even when nobody is watching.
senses.whyCN: 在「暖」和「傲」之间还有第三层：pride 是一个人拒绝再往下退的那块地板，即使没人看着也不肯越过的界线，所以是自尊。

senses.title: A group of lions living and hunting together
senses.definition: a group of lions that live and hunt together, usually led by related females
senses.definitionCN: 共同生活、共同捕猎的一群狮子，通常由有亲缘关系的母狮带领
senses.example: A pride of lions lay in the shade, waiting for the heat to pass.
senses.exampleCN: 一群狮子卧在树荫里，等暑气过去。
senses.why: This sense comes from medieval hunting language, where each kind of animal was given its own company name; naming a band of lions was one entry in that list, and only this one survived in everyday use.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项来自中世纪的狩猎用语，当时人们给每一种动物的群体都起一个专门的集合名，狮子那一栏就是 pride，而这一栏是唯一留到日常英语里的。

senses.title: To feel proud about a skill or possession of one's own
senses.definition: to feel a strong, often slightly self-satisfied pleasure about a skill, quality, or possession of one's own
senses.definitionCN: 对自己拥有的本领、品质或东西感到强烈的、常带点自得的满意
senses.example: The old chef prides himself on never using a shortcut.
senses.exampleCN: 这位老厨师最得意的是自己从不走捷径。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb inside the pattern to pride oneself on, where oneself is the person being lifted and the preposition on names the thing that does the lifting.
senses.whyCN: 名词套进 to pride oneself on 这个句式后就当动词用：oneself 是被抬起来的那个自己，介词 on 后面则是抬人的理由，也就是凭什么觉得自己了不起。

intro.en: Pride is an Old English noun built on the adjective proud, and that adjective is generally traced through French to a Late Latin word for profit; the word therefore began as a judgement of worth before it split into warm and cold senses.
intro.cn: pride 是古英语里由形容词 proud 造出的名词，而那个形容词一般认为经法语上溯到晚期拉丁语中表示「有好处」的词；所以它最初是对「有没有价值」的判断，之后才分成暖、冷两路。

items.en: The Latin verb prodesse meant to be of use or of advantage, and its stem prōd- is the base that later Romance forms are usually traced to.
items.cn: 拉丁语动词 prodesse 意为「有用、有好处」，一般认为后来的罗曼语词形都追到它的词干 prōd-。

items.en: The Late Latin form prode meant useful or profitable, and in the spoken Latin of the provinces it also took on the colour of brave or worthy.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语的 prode 意为「有用的、有利的」，在各省的口语拉丁语里又沾上了「勇敢、可敬」的色彩。

items.en: Old French prud or prod described a man who was brave and worthy, a sense still visible in the modern French preux.
items.cn: 古法语 prud、prod 形容人勇敢可敬，这层意思在今天的法语 preux 里还能看到。

items.en: English borrowed the adjective as prūd, which in Old English already meant proud, arrogant, and splendid at the same time; from it the noun prȳde was formed.
items.cn: 英语借入这个形容词，写作古英语 prūd，当时就同时表示「骄傲的、傲慢的、华贵的」三面；名词 prȳde 正是由它造出来的。

items.en: Middle English prede or pride settled on the spelling pride, and the old single quality divided into praise-worthy self-respect and blame-worthy conceit, with the lion sense added from hunting vocabulary.
items.cn: 中古英语的 prede、pride 最终定为 pride 这个拼写，原本混在一起的性质分成值得称赞的自尊与该受责备的自负，狮群一义则从狩猎词汇补进来。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the adjective that pride was built from and the words closest to it in spelling; the near-meaning group holds words for self-regard, both deserved and inflated.
note.cn: 形近组收了 pride 借以构成的那个形容词及拼写最接近的几个词；近义组收表示自我看重的词，既有应得的，也有膨胀的。

entries.definition: Feeling pleased about one's own or another's achievements; the adjective that English used to build the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 为自己或他人的成就感到高兴的；英语正是用它造出了名词 pride。

entries.definition: Showing too high an opinion of oneself; built on the noun with the suffix -ful.
entries.definitionCN: 过于自负的；由名词加后缀 -ful 构成。

entries.definition: A person who is easily shocked by matters of the body; it comes from a French word for a modest woman, so the similarity is only in spelling.
entries.definitionCN: 对身体方面的事容易大惊小怪的人；来自法语中表示「端庄女子」的词，只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: To push someone or something with a finger or a stick; a different word with a different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 用手指或棍子捅；另一个词，来源不同。

entries.definition: An unpleasant belief that one is better than everyone else.
entries.definitionCN: 令人反感的、认为自己高于所有人的信念。

entries.definition: The calm, serious quality of deserving respect.
entries.definitionCN: 值得尊重的沉稳庄重。

entries.definition: The good opinion a person has of their own character.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人对自身品格的正面评价。

entries.definition: The pleasant feeling of having got what one wanted.
entries.definitionCN: 得到想要之物后的愉快感觉。

normalIntro.en: The noun was grown from an adjective that English borrowed from French, so the family keeps one ancient stem but two different shapes.
normalIntro.cn: 这个名词是从英语借自法语的形容词上长出来的，所以同族词共用一个古老词干，却有两种不同词形。

normal.en: Pride is the noun and proud is the adjective: English formed prȳde from prūd, which is why the two never look alike today.
normal.cn: pride 是名词，proud 是形容词：古英语从 prūd 造出 prȳde，所以今天两者词形完全不同。

normal.en: The -ful in prideful turns the noun into an adjective, the same -ful that appears in careful and hopeful.
normal.cn: prideful 里的 -ful 把名词变成形容词，和 careful、hopeful 里的 -ful 是同一个后缀。

normal.en: Swallow one's pride is a picture of forcing something down the throat: the feeling is still there, only hidden.
normal.cn: swallow one's pride 是一幅把东西硬咽下去的画：情绪还在，只是藏起来了。

normal.en: A pride of lions follows the old hunting habit of giving every kind of animal its own collective name.
normal.cn: a pride of lions 沿用古老的狩猎习惯：给每一种动物的群体都起一个专门的集合名。

normal.en: Pride oneself on needs the reflexive pronoun because the one who boasts is also the one being lifted.
normal.cn: pride oneself on 必须带反身代词，因为夸人的和被抬高的其实是同一个。

abstract.en: One word covers a mother's lifted chin and a tyrant's closed ears, because both are the same self looking at itself.
abstract.cn: 一个词同时装着母亲抬起的下巴和暴君堵住的耳朵，因为两者都是「自我在看自己」。

abstract.en: Pride as dignity is pride turned inward and kept quiet; pride as conceit is the same force turned outward and made loud.
abstract.cn: 作为尊严的 pride 向内收着、不出声；作为自负的 pride 是同一股力向外放、喊得很响。

abstract.en: The lion sense survives as a fossil: a whole medieval habit of naming animal groups, kept alive by one entry.
abstract.cn: 狮群义像一块化石：中世纪给动物群体起名的一整套习惯，只靠这一条留了下来。

examples.en: She looked at her finished painting with quiet pride.
examples.cn: 她带着平静的自豪看着自己画完的画。

examples.en: It was pride, not principle, that stopped him from admitting the mistake.
examples.cn: 让他不肯认错的是自大，而不是原则。

examples.en: The old chef prides himself on never using a shortcut.
examples.cn: 这位老厨师最得意的是自己从不走捷径。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「扑赖德」——一股气从胸口扑上来，赖着不走，那就是 pride。

root: 古英语 prȳde（骄傲）由 prūd（骄傲的）加名词词尾构成，prūd 一般认为借自古法语 prud、prod，可上溯到晚期拉丁语 prode（有用的、有利的），出自拉丁语 prodesse（有益）。同源的形容词 proud 保留了另一支词形。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a self looking at itself with approval; the senses divide into the warm feeling, the cold excess, the line of self-respect, the lion group, and the verb of taking pride in something.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「自我满意地看着自己」；义项由此分出温暖的自豪、过头的自负、守住的尊严、狮群，以及表示「以……为荣」的动词用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a chest lifting and a chin rising for a moment.
core.cn: 核心意象：胸口往上一提，下巴微微一抬的那一瞬。

branches.en: a mother's back straightening at a ceremony
branches.cn: 典礼上母亲把背挺直的一瞬

branches.en: a man who will not say sorry
branches.cn: 一个死活不肯道歉的人

branches.en: a hand pushing away a coin offered in pity
branches.cn: 一只推开怜悯施舍的手

branches.en: tawny bodies resting in tall grass
branches.cn: 高草里卧着的一群黄褐色身影

branches.en: a chef boasting about his own knife work
branches.cn: 厨师夸自己的刀工

intro.en: The word is an Old English noun grown from a borrowed adjective, and the eight pieces below trace that adjective back through French to a Latin word of profit.
intro.cn: 这个词是古英语里从借来的形容词长成的名词，下面八条把它经由法语一路追回拉丁语中表示「有好处」的词。

latinIntro.en: A Late Latin adjective of profit stands behind the French form that English borrowed, so a Latin cognate does exist here, although the link is indirect.
latinIntro.cn: 英语借来的法语词形背后有晚期拉丁语中表示「有好处」的形容词，所以这个词确有拉丁同族，只是关系是间接的。
